l1_0.t: Happy birthday, Josh! Did you get a new laptop? I know you wanted one.
No, Mum said I have to wait until Christmas for that. But I got a camera from my parents.
Cool! And did your brother give you anything?
He said he'd buy me an MP3 player, but he forgot! He's going to get it next week.

l1_1.t: Dad, have you seen my mobile? I can't find it anywhere.
Did you look on the sofa? You were sitting there this morning.
Yes, and it isn't in my school bag either.
Oh, wait – I can see it. It's in the kitchen, next to the cooker. You were making breakfast with it in your hand!

l1_2.t: Mum, something's wrong in my bedroom.
Is it the lamp again? I bought a new light for it yesterday.
No, the lamp's fine. It's my clock. It stopped in the night, so I nearly missed the bus.
Oh dear. Well, use the alarm on the radio until we get a new one.

l1_3.t: Those are great headphones, Sophie. Were they expensive?
Well, they usually cost fifty pounds, but they were half price in the sale.
So you paid twenty-five?
That's right. My friend bought some for fifteen pounds, but they don't sound as good as mine.

l1_4.t: What's on TV tonight? Is there a good film?
There's one at nine, but it finishes too late for the children.
What about the football?
That was yesterday. Let's watch the programme about lions in Africa at seven. Everyone will like that.
Good idea.

l2.t: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to tell you about our new Technology Club. Last year the club met on Mondays, but lots of students had football practice then, so this year we're meeting on Wednesdays, from half past three until five o'clock. We won't be in the computer room, because it's too small. We'll meet in Room fourteen, next to the library. This term we're going to make something really exciting. We thought about building a small robot, but it's too difficult for beginners. So instead, you'll each make your own radio, and you can take it home at the end of term! You don't need to buy anything – the school will pay for everything. But please bring a notebook, because you'll need to write down the instructions. You don't need to bring a laptop. The club is run by a new teacher, Mr Kemp. That's K-E-M-P. He was an engineer before he became a teacher, so he knows a lot about electricity. If you want to join, please write your name on the list outside the staff room before Friday.

l3.t: Hi Anna. Why aren't you answering my texts?
Sorry, Mark. My phone's broken. I dropped it on the floor in the kitchen and now the screen doesn't work. It wasn't slow or anything – it was a good phone!
Oh no. Are your parents going to buy you a new one?
Mum says I have to pay for half of it myself. I've got some birthday money, and my grandma's going to pay the rest. That's really kind of her.
So what kind of phone do you want? One with a big screen for watching videos?
The screen doesn't matter much. I want one with a really good camera, because I take so many photos. The battery's important too, but I can always charge it at school.
Are you going to buy it online? It's usually cheaper.
I looked on the internet, but my mum doesn't like buying things that way. And the shops in the city centre are so expensive.
Why don't you ask my cousin Tim? He's selling his phone because he's got a new one. It's only a year old and the camera's amazing.
Really? That's a great idea! I'll ask him. I'll buy it from him if it's not too expensive.
Shall we go to the cinema this weekend?
Maybe next week. On Saturday I want to go to the phone shop in town to buy a case for my new phone. Do you want to come?
Sure. Then we can take some photos in the park on Sunday!

l4_0.t: Mum, can I stay up until ten tonight?
It's a school night, Ryan. Is there something on TV?
No, it's the game I'm playing online with Jack and Leo. We're on the last level and we want to finish it together tonight.
Hmm. OK, but only until half past nine.

l4_1.t: Hi Dad, it's Mai. I'm still at school because the science teacher asked us to help with the computers for tomorrow's exam. Can you collect me at five, not four? Don't worry about my laptop – I've got it with me. And my phone's fine, I charged it in the classroom. See you later!

l4_2.t: Your parents bought a new fridge, didn't they? What's it like?
It's really modern and quiet – our old one made a terrible noise at night. And Dad found it in the sale, so it was cheap.
Sounds perfect.
Not really. It's so huge that we can't open the kitchen door properly now!

l4_3.t: Before we start, listen please. From next Monday, you must leave your mobile phones in your lockers during lessons. You can use them at lunchtime, but not in the classroom. If I see a phone in a lesson, I'll keep it until the end of the day. Is that clear? Good. Now, open your books at page twenty.

l4_4.t: My grandma's seventy-five, and I thought she wouldn't know anything about computers. But when I visited her last weekend, she showed me her new laptop. She sends emails to her friends, she reads the news online and she even calls my cousins in Australia on video! I couldn't believe it. She knows more than my dad!

l5.t: Emma, what's your homework about tonight?
We have to find out which machine each person in our family uses the most. Can you help me, Dad? Let's start with Mum. Is it the laptop? She works on it a lot.
She uses her work laptop at the office, but at home she's always in the kitchen. She loves cooking, so I'd say the cooker.
OK. What about Grandpa? He watches a lot of TV.
Not really. He says there's nothing good on TV these days. He listens to the radio all day – the news, the football, everything.
That's true. And my brother? He's always on the computer.
Well, he doesn't have his own computer. But he watches cartoons on the television every afternoon after school. He'd watch it all night if I let him!
Ha! And Aunt Rosa? When she stayed with us, she was always cold, so she turned the heating up.
Yes, but what she really used every day was your mum's hairdryer! She spent ages doing her hair every morning.
That's right. Now me. I think it's my lamp, because I read in bed every night.
Really? I think it's the laptop – you use it for homework and for chatting with your friends.
OK, you're right. I'll write laptop.

l1_0.t: Hi Zoe. What did you get at the shops? Did you buy that new hairdryer?
No, it was too expensive. I'll wait for the sale.
Oh. So what's in the bag?
There was a lovely clock, but I've already got one in my room. So I bought a lamp for my desk. Now I can read in the evenings.

l1_1.t: Sam, the man from the heating company phoned. He can't come at ten o'clock tomorrow.
Oh no. Is he coming later? I'm home at half past eleven.
No, he's coming earlier, at half past eight. I'll be here, so you can go to school as usual.
Great. I'm so tired of being cold!

l1_2.t: Mum, are we getting a new cooker? Ours is really old.
It's old, but it still works well. The problem is the fridge. It makes a terrible noise and the milk isn't cold any more.
So we're buying a new one?
Yes, on Saturday. Dad wants a radio for the kitchen too, but that can wait until next month.

l1_3.t: Did you see the match last night, Ali? Did you watch it on your big TV?
No, my brother was watching a film on it, and he wouldn't change the channel.
What about your laptop?
I left it at my grandad's. So I watched it on my phone. The screen was so small, but at least I saw the goals!

l1_4.t: Does your grandad watch a lot of TV in the evenings, Jamie?
Only the news. Then he turns it off.
Does he watch films? He's got lots of DVDs, hasn't he?
He never watches them! What he really loves is sitting in his armchair and listening to his old jazz CDs.

l2.t: Hello, everyone, and welcome to the Museum of Home Technology. Here you can see how people lived before computers and mobile phones. Lots of visitors think the oldest thing in our museum is the radio in the first room, but it isn't. It's a telephone from eighteen ninety, and you'll find it near the main stairs. Now, if you're interested in cooking, the old kitchen machines, like the first electric cookers and fridges, are in Room eight. Room nine has televisions and video recorders from the nineteen sixties and seventies. My favourite place is the photography room. There, you can take a picture with a real camera from the nineteen fifties. You can't use your own phones in that room, I'm afraid. The museum closes at five o'clock, but the café closes earlier, at a quarter past four, so get your drinks before then. Finally, a message for your teachers. If your school would like to visit again, please contact Mrs Pryce. That's P-R-Y-C-E. She organises all our school visits. Right, let's start in the first room.

l3.t: Hi Sam. Are you bringing anything to the school sale on Saturday?
Maybe. What's the money for this year? Last year it paid for the class trip to London, didn't it?
That's right. This year they want to buy new laptops for the library. The heating in the gym is broken too, but the town is paying to repair that.
OK. So what are you selling?

Well, I wanted to sell my old MP3 player, but I still use it when I go running. And Grandad offered me his video recorder, but nobody has videos any more! So Dad's given me his DVD player. He watches everything online now.
I've got an old camera I never use. I thought I'd ask twelve pounds for it.
That's a lot. People only pay about five pounds for old cameras on the internet.
But mine has a really nice case. I'll ask for eight. That's fair.
Good idea.
Are you helping at the sale?
Yes. Mr Ford wanted me to take the money, but I'm terrible at maths! So I'm going to test all the electric things and make sure they work. The Year Seven students have already made the posters.
When should I bring my camera?
Mr Ford says Friday afternoon is best.
I've got football then. And Saturday morning is too late. I'll bring it on Thursday morning – Mum can drive me.

l4_0.t: Is that your new hairdryer, Grace? It looks nice and light.
It is light, and it gets really hot, so my hair dries quickly.
So you're happy with it?
Not really. When I turn it on, it's so noisy that it wakes up my little brother. Mum isn't very pleased!

l4_1.t: Hi Nadia, it's Josh. I'm really sorry, but I can't come to watch the film at your house tonight. My mum isn't well and I have to look after my little sister. Don't worry about the DVD I borrowed – I'll give it back to you at school tomorrow. Maybe we can watch something together at the weekend instead. Bye!

l4_2.t: Leo, are you cold? You're only wearing a T-shirt.
A bit. Can I turn the heating up?
No, electricity is so expensive this winter. The windows are all closed, so go and get your sweater from your room, please.
OK, Mum.

l4_3.t: Good morning, class. Last week we learned how batteries work, and next week we'll talk about how we can save electricity at home. But today I want to show you something different. When you switch on the lights or the TV, where does the electricity come from? How does it travel all the way to your house? Let's watch this short video and find out.

l4_4.t: My grandparents live on a farm, and they don't have a TV or a computer. There's just an old telephone in the kitchen. My friends think I must be bored there, but I'm not at all. I sleep really well, I go for long walks with Grandpa, and I help Grandma in the garden. And there are always lots of people around. I feel so calm when I'm there.

l5.t: Mum, is Dad taking his laptop on holiday? He always says he has to work.
Not this time! I told him no work on holiday, so the laptop's staying at home. He's taking his camera instead. He wants to take lots of pictures of the mountains.
Good. What about Grandma? Is she bringing her CD player? She loves her music.
She wanted to, but there isn't space in the car. She's only bringing her little travel clock. She never uses the alarm on her phone – she says it's too difficult.
And Lily? I bet she's taking her MP3 player.
It's broken, actually. But she's packed her hairdryer. She says there won't be one at the cottage.
Is cousin Ben coming with us in the car?
Yes, and it's a long journey for a six-year-old. So his mum's giving us her small DVD player. He can watch cartoons in the back of the car.
That's a good idea. Can I take something too?
Of course. What do you want to take?
There's no TV at the cottage, so I'm taking my radio. Then I can listen to the football results on Saturday.

l1_0.t: Are you wearing your new blue shirt to Emma's party tonight?
I wanted to, but there's a mark on it, so Mum's washing it.
What about your T-shirt with the football on it?
It's a bit old now. I'll wear my green sweater. It's going to be cold this evening anyway.

l1_1.t: I need a new bag for school. Can I look at that backpack, please?
Of course. It's a nice one, and it's got lots of pockets.
Hmm, it's quite expensive. How much is the sports bag?
Twenty pounds, but it isn't big enough for all your books. And the handbags are only for small things.
Then I'll take the backpack. I can use my birthday money.

l1_2.t: What's wrong, Leo? You look worried.
I've lost something at the swimming pool.
Not your watch again!
No, I'm wearing my watch, look. And my glasses are here in my bag. It's my gloves. I think I left them in the changing room.
Let's go back and ask.

l1_3.t: Dad, where's my denim jacket? I need it for school.
Did you leave it in the car yesterday?
No, I've checked. And it isn't on the chair in my bedroom.
Oh, I remember now. It was wet, so I put it behind the kitchen door to dry.

l1_4.t: Do you like my new trainers?
They're great! Were they expensive?
They were fifty-five pounds in the shop window, but I got ten pounds off because I'm a student.
So forty-five? That's not bad.
Yes. My brother paid thirty-five for his, but they aren't as nice as mine.

l2.t: Hello, everyone. Next week our school is having a clothes swap to make money for the children's hospital. It was going to be on Thursday, but there's a parents' evening that day, so now it's on Friday, after school. We can't use the hall because the drama club needs it, so please come to the library. It's bigger than you think! Here's how it works. Bring clothes that you don't wear any more – jackets, jeans, skirts, blouses, sweaters, T-shirts, even belts and bags. Please make sure they're clean. Then you can choose some different clothes to take home. You can try things on in the room next to the library. Tickets cost one pound for students. Teachers and parents pay two pounds. All the money goes to the hospital. Please don't bring shoes or trainers – we haven't got enough space for them this year. Hats, purses and watches are fine. If you have any questions, talk to Miss Doyle. That's D-O-Y-L-E. She's our new Art teacher, and she's organising everything.

l3.t: Hi Leo. Your mum says you're going on a school trip soon.
Yes, Aunt Kate! We're going skiing in February. Last year the class went to France, but this year we're going to Italy. I can't wait!
Lovely! Have you got all the clothes you need? It'll be very cold in the mountains.
Not yet. The teacher gave us a list. I need a warm coat, a hat, gloves, boots and special ski trousers. Grandma's already given me a hat and gloves for Christmas.
What about a coat?
My cousin Ben gave me his old ski coat. It fits me and it's nearly new, but it's bright orange and purple! I look terrible in it.
Ha! Well, nobody cares what you look like on a mountain.
I know, but everyone will take photos! Anyway, the school's going to lend us the ski trousers, so I only need to buy some boots. My old ones are too small.
Shall I take you shopping? There's a market on Sundays, but they don't sell good boots there.
Mum says the big shopping centre is really expensive. My friend got his boots at the sports shop in town. They've got a sale at the moment.
Then let's go there. Are you free on Saturday?
I've got football practice in the afternoon, but the morning's fine.
Great. I'll pick you up at ten. And maybe we can find you a different coat in the sale too!

l4_0.t: Mum, I don't want to wear this dress to the wedding.
But it looks lovely on you! And I made it longer for you last week.
I know it looks nice, and the colour's great. But it's so tight that I can't sit down or eat anything!
Oh dear. Let's go and find something else, then.

l4_1.t: Hi Sam, it's Jake. You know the costume party at school tomorrow? I'm going as a cowboy, but I haven't got any boots. Have you still got those brown ones from the school play? Could I have them for the evening? I'll give them back on Monday, I promise. See you at the party – and don't forget your costume! Bye.

l4_2.t: Have you seen the new uniform for next year?
Yes, the grey trousers and the dark blue jacket? Mum says it costs the same as the old one.
I think it looks boring.
Really? I much prefer it. The old skirt was horrible, and now girls can wear trousers too. I'll be much warmer in winter!

l4_3.t: Yesterday Dad took me to buy a suit for my sister's wedding. I thought it would be really boring, but the shop was quite interesting. The problem was Dad. He kept telling the shop assistant about me – how fast I'm growing, how small I was as a baby – in front of everyone! And two girls from my class were in the shop too. I wanted to hide behind the coats!

l4_4.t: This week we visited a new shop in Bridge Street called Second Chance. Everything there – coats, shoes, jeans, even school uniforms – was given by local families. And the best thing is, it's all free! If you need clothes, just go in and take what you need. Most of the clothes are for children, but there are some for adults too. The shop is open every day except Sunday.

l5.t: Hi Amy. How was the costume party on Saturday?

Brilliant, Jack! Everyone dressed up. My brother wanted to be an astronaut, but that costume was forty pounds in the shop, so Mum said no. In the end he was a pirate. He wore Dad's old boots and a big black hat.
Ha! What about Lucy? Was she a princess again?
No, she says she's too old for princess dresses now. She wore black tights, a black T-shirt and a black skirt, and she had two little ears on her head. She was a cat – a really cute one!
And Mr Hill? I heard he came too.
Yes! Everyone thought he'd come as a doctor again, like last year. But this time he wore a long red coat and a gold crown. He was a king!
What about Kim? She always has funny ideas.
She was a clown. She had yellow trousers, orange hair and enormous red shoes. She could hardly walk!
And your dad? Did he dress up?
He borrowed my uncle's uniform – a dark blue jacket, trousers and a hat. My uncle's a police officer, you know. Dad tried to look very serious, but he kept laughing!

l1_0.t: Dad, what should I wear to the school concert? I was going to wear my long dress.
It'll be really hot in the hall. What about your black skirt?
Hmm, I'd prefer to wear my jeans and my new pink top. The teacher says we don't need to dress smartly.
Fine. That sounds comfortable.

l1_1.t: Did you get a present for Mum's birthday, Tom?
Yes. I wanted to buy her an umbrella because she lost hers, but Dad's already bought her one.
So what did you get?
I looked at some scarves, but they were all too expensive. In the end I got her a purse. Her old one's broken.

l1_2.t: Which one is your cousin Daniel? Is he the boy in the cap?
No, that's his friend. Daniel wears glasses.
Oh, the one in the long coat?
No, he never wears a coat, even in winter! He's the one in the red T-shirt, next to the door.

l1_3.t: Do you want to go to the sale at Fashion Corner? I want some new jeans.
Is it still on? I thought it finished last Saturday.
No, the poster in the window says it goes on until Monday.
Great. Then let's go on Sunday – I'm busy tomorrow.

l1_4.t: Mum, where are my sports shorts? I need them tomorrow.
Isn't PE on Thursday? Tomorrow's Wednesday.
Oh, you're right. But we're going to the park for science, and the teacher says we need trainers, not school shoes.
OK. Take your raincoat too.
I don't need it. It's going to be sunny all day.

l2.t: Welcome to the City Museum. My name's Rachel, and I'm going to tell you about our new exhibition, Fashion Through Time. It isn't on the ground floor with the paintings – you'll find it on the third floor. Take the lift next to the café. The exhibition shows clothes from the last three hundred years. Most people think the oldest thing is the beautiful blue dress near the door, but that's from 1850. Our oldest thing is a pair of brown leather boots from 1720 – they're very small! In the next room there are skirts, tights and shoes from the 1960s. In the last room, you can try on some hats from the past and take photos. Please don't touch the coats and suits, because they're very old. Don't miss the modern room – there's a wonderful pink suit by the young designer Lily Grant. That's G-R-A-N-T. She's only twenty-four! After your visit, you can go to the museum shop. It sells T-shirts, bags and umbrellas with pictures from the exhibition. The museum closes at six o'clock, but the shop closes a little earlier, at half past five.

l3.t: Sam, are you going to be in the fashion show on Friday?
Yes, Mr Ford asked me. I'm a bit nervous. What about you, Emily?
I'm in it too. Everyone has to wear clothes made from old things. I wanted to make a dress from newspapers, but it was too difficult. So my grandma and I made a skirt from old plastic bags!
Cool! I'm wearing a suit made of old maps. My sister made it – she's really good at that kind of thing. Mum wanted to help, but she's too busy at work.
A suit made of maps? I want to see that! Is the show going to be in the school hall?
It was going to be there, but now it's going to be outside in the playground, because more people can come. If it rains, we'll use the sports hall.
And how much are the tickets?
Three pounds for adults and one pound for students. All the money's going to an animal hospital.
Who's choosing the winner? Mr Ford?
No, he's just organising it. Last year it was the head teacher, but this year a woman from a fashion magazine is coming!
Wow! Now I'm really nervous. What shoes are you going to wear?
My black school shoes – they look good with the suit. My trainers are too dirty.
Ha! I'll wear my boots with my skirt.

l4_0.t: When the eye doctor said I needed glasses, I was really worried. I thought everyone at school would laugh at me, so I chose some boring brown ones. But on my first day, my friends said they looked great, and now I can see the board clearly. I love them! Next time I might choose a more exciting colour, but these are fine for now.

l4_1.t: Hello. I bought this jacket here on Saturday, but I'd like to bring it back.
Is it too small? We've got bigger sizes.
No, the size is fine, and I love the colour. But look – there's a hole in the pocket. I only saw it when I got home.
Oh, I'm sorry. Would you like another one?

l4_2.t: Ryan, have you seen your bedroom? There are clothes all over the floor – jeans, socks, your school sweater. And your clean shirts are still on the bed. I've already washed your football shirt, so don't worry about that. But please put everything in your cupboard before dinner. I'm not doing it for you!

l4_3.t: Have you tried that new clothes website, Style Teen?
Yes, my sister showed me. There are lots of nice jackets and trainers for boys on it.
And the prices are good, aren't they?
Not really – most things cost more than in the shops. And it's so confusing! I spent twenty minutes trying to find my size and then I gave up.

l4_4.t: OK, everyone, just a few things about tomorrow's trip to the farm. We'll meet here in the classroom as usual. Now, it's going to be very muddy, so please don't come in your school uniform or your best trainers. Wear old clothes and boots, and bring a raincoat. And put a warm hat in your bag – it can get cold there in the afternoon.

l5.t: Oscar, the hotel phoned. They found lots of our things in the rooms! I can't believe this family.
Oh no! What did they find? Was it Dad's watch? He couldn't find it at the airport.
No, he found his watch in his coat pocket on the plane. But he left his belt on the bathroom door.
Typical! What about Grandma? She's always losing her glasses.
Her glasses are fine – she's wearing them now. It was her umbrella. She left it next to the bed.
And Ruby? I'm sure my sister forgot something.
Yes, her swimming costume. It was still wet, so she put it outside on the balcony and forgot about it.
Uncle Pete said he left his trainers under the bed.
No, he found those when he was packing. But the hotel has got his raincoat. It was in the cupboard by the door.
Well, that's everyone except me. I packed everything really carefully.
Really? Then whose shorts are these? The hotel says they're blue with yellow stars on them.
Oh! They're mine. I wore them on the beach on the last day.

l1_0.t: I like this T-shirt, but which colour should I get? Red or green?
You've already got lots of red clothes. What about this grey one?
Grey's a bit boring. I'll take the green one. It goes well with my jeans.
Good choice.

l1_1.t: I got my new bike today!
Great! Is it pink, like your old one?
No, I wanted something different. I nearly chose a white one, but white gets dirty so quickly. So I got a purple one, with black wheels.
Cool! Let's go for a ride.

l1_2.t: Dad, where are my paints? They aren't in my black bag.
Did you look in the brown box under your desk?
Yes, but there are only pencils in there.
Oh, sorry, I remember now. I put them on the shelf in the kitchen, next to the radio.

l1_3.t: What are you painting, Tom? Is it the sea? There's so much blue.
No, the blue is the sky. Look, this is the orange sun. It's going down behind the hills.
Oh, it's a sunset! I thought those dark green shapes were trees.
No, they're hills. Maybe I'll add some trees later.

l1_4.t: Look, that's my dog in this photo.
Which one? The brown one?
No, that's my neighbour's dog. Mine is the white one with black ears.
Oh, and who's the black one with white ears? They look the same!
That's his brother. He lives with my cousin.

l2.t: Hello, and thanks for coming. I'm here to tell you about the Hillside Colour Run. It's a fun run where people throw coloured powder at you while you run! It's on Sunday the twelfth of June. We wanted to have it in May, but the park was already busy then. Don't worry – you don't have to be a fast runner. The run is five kilometres. Last year it was ten, but lots of people told us that was too long. At every kilometre there's a different colour: first red, then yellow, then blue, then green. And at the finish, everyone gets covered in purple! So please wear white clothes – you'll look like a rainbow at the end. Tickets for adults are fifteen pounds. If you're under sixteen, it's eight pounds, and you get a free T-shirt too. All the money goes to the children's hospital. The run starts at Wickham Park. That's W-I-C-K-H-A-M. It's next to the railway station. Please arrive at nine o'clock. And one more thing: bring some sunglasses to keep the powder out of your eyes!

l3.t: Hi Oliver. How was the school trip to the art gallery?
Really good, Hannah! I thought it would be boring, but it wasn't at all.
What did you see?
There were lots of old paintings of kings and queens, but they were very dark – mostly brown and black. My favourite was a modern one. It was just a big yellow circle on a light blue background.
That sounds easy! I could paint that.
That's what everyone said! But the guide told us the artist painted it in 1960, and now it's worth millions.
Did you do anything else?
Yes, in the afternoon there was a class. We wanted to paint, but there wasn't enough time, so we made pictures with coloured paper instead. I made a green and orange fish.
Cool. Did you buy anything in the gift shop?
The postcards were really expensive, and I've already got lots of pens. So I bought a poster of the yellow circle for my bedroom wall. It was only three pounds.
Are you going to go back?
Yes! Next month there's a new exhibition all about the colour red – red clothes, red paintings, even red food! My mum wants to go, and you can come with us if you like.
I'd love to. But not on a Saturday – I've got swimming.
That's fine. We'll go on a Sunday.

l4_0.t: Mum, can we paint my bedroom a different colour?
But you chose that dark blue only last year! You said blue was your favourite colour.
It still is. My friends think the room's cool, too. But it's so dark – it feels tiny, like a cupboard. I'd like something lighter, like white or light grey.

l4_1.t: My aunt gave me a sweater for my birthday. It's bright pink with big yellow spots.
Wow! Did you know she was going to give you clothes?
Yes, she always does. She was so pleased with it, so I said thank you. But I'll never wear it – I only like black and grey clothes. I really wanted some new headphones.

l4_2.t: Tomorrow we're going to start painting the big picture for the school hall. We'll use lots of paint, especially red and black, and they're very difficult to wash out. So please bring an old shirt or T-shirt to wear over your uniform. Don't worry about paint or brushes – I've got everything we need. And we'll all clean the room together at the end.

l4_3.t: Did you enjoy the film last night?
Well, the story was a bit silly, and the music was much too loud.
Oh dear. So you didn't like it?
I did, actually, because it looked amazing. Every part had different colours – purple forests, orange seas, pink mountains. I've never seen anything like it.

l4_4.t: Hillcrest Garden is lovely all year, but May is the best time to visit. That's when thousands of flowers open – red, yellow, white, and even dark purple ones that look almost black. People come from all over the country to see them. You can have a picnic by the lake, but please don't pick the flowers. And the garden shop sells plants, but only in the autumn.

l5.t: Lily, do you know the team colours for sports day yet?
Yes, Mr Price told us this morning. You're in the Lions, aren't you? You wanted yellow, but the Lions are orange this year.
Orange? Oh well, it's quite like yellow. What about your team, the Eagles?
We all wanted black, but the teachers said it's too hot to wear black in the sun. So we've got purple.
Purple's nice. And the Dolphins? Blue, I suppose, like the sea?
That's what everyone thought! But no, they're green. Blue is for the Bears.
That's strange. Bears are brown!
I know, but the shop didn't have any brown T-shirts. Dark blue was the closest colour, Mr Price said.
And the Tigers? My sister's in that team. She said they asked for pink.
They did, but some of the boys weren't happy about it. So in the end they chose red. It looks really good with the white shorts.
So everyone wears white shorts?
Yes, and white socks. By the end of the day they'll be grey, I'm sure!

l1_0.t: Have you seen Dad's new car? It's outside.
Is it that red one?
No, that's Mrs Taylor's. Dad's is the grey one next to it.
Grey? He always said he wanted a white car.
He did, but the white one was more expensive.

l1_1.t: I'd like some flowers for my grandma, please. She loves yellow ones.
Sorry, we haven't got any yellow ones today. But these pink roses are lovely.
Hmm, her garden's already full of pink roses. What about those purple ones?
They're five pounds.
Perfect. I'll take them.

l1_2.t: Which one is your sister Hannah? The girl with light hair?
No, that's my cousin. Hannah's got dark hair, like me.
Is she the one in the blue dress?
No, that's her friend. Hannah's wearing green. It's her favourite colour.

l1_3.t: Dad, there was a beautiful bird in the garden this morning.
Was it a robin? They've got a red front.
No, it was small and blue, with a yellow front.
Ah, that's a blue tit. We often see blackbirds here, but blue tits don't come very often.

l1_4.t: Look at these pencil cases, Sam. This pink one's lovely.
My sister's got that one. I want something different.
What about black? It won't look dirty.
Black's so boring. I'll get the orange one. Then nobody will take it by mistake!

l2.t: Are you between eleven and fifteen? Do you love colours? Then come to our summer painting course! The course runs from Monday to Thursday every week in August. We used to have classes on Fridays too, but now that's the day we clean the studio! In the first week, we'll go down to the harbour and paint the boats. They're all different colours – red, blue, green and orange – so it's a great place to start. In the second week, we'll paint the flowers in the city park. The course costs forty-five pounds a week for students. Adults can join too, but they pay sixty pounds. We'll give you brushes, paper and some paints – we've got lots of red, black and brown. But please bring your own blue, yellow and white, because we always run out of those colours. And wear old clothes, of course! Your teacher will be Mrs Fenton. That's F-E-N-T-O-N. She's a well-known artist, and her paintings of the sea are in lots of galleries. We hope to see you there!

l3.t: Welcome back, Mia! How was Iceland?
Amazing, Grandpa! It was really cold, but I loved it.
Did you see the northern lights?

Yes! We tried on the first night, but it was too cloudy. On the second night we were too tired after a long walk, so we went to bed early. But on the third night the sky was clear, and suddenly there they were!
What colours were they? I've seen photos with pink and purple lights.
Sometimes they're pink, but ours were mostly green – bright green, moving across the dark sky like a river. There was a little bit of purple at the end.
Did you take any photos?
I tried, but my phone wasn't good enough – all my photos were just black! Luckily Dad had his big camera, so he got some great ones.
And what else did you do?
We swam in a hot pool outside, even when it was snowing. And we walked on some beaches where the sand is black, because of the volcanoes. It looked so strange!
Did you bring me anything?
Of course! I wanted to get you a sweater, but they were really expensive. So I got you this grey and white hat instead.
Lovely, thank you! Will you go back one day?
I hope so. Mum says next time we'll go in summer, when it's light nearly all night. But you can't see the northern lights then.

l4_0.t: Dad, can you help me with my geography project? It's a poster about flags of the world.
Sure. Do you need help finding information?
No, I've done that, and I've drawn all the flags. But I can't decide on the background. White looks boring, and black is too dark.
What about light blue, like the sky?

l4_1.t: Hi Ana, it's Kevin. I'm at the concert already – I got here early. It's really busy, so it won't be easy to find me. I'm near the front, next to the big speaker on the left, and I'm wearing my orange cap. So look for orange! Text me when you arrive.

l4_2.t: Have you been to the new café in the square?
Yes, last weekend. The cakes are really good, and they aren't expensive.
It's quite small, isn't it?
There's enough space. But the walls are bright red and the chairs are bright yellow – it hurts my eyes! I couldn't relax at all.

l4_3.t: Last week we watched a video about light and colour. Today you're going to do an experiment. Each group has three small bottles of water – red, yellow and blue. Mix them and see what new colours you can make. Can you make green? Orange? Purple? Write everything in your book. Next week we'll try to make our own rainbow with a glass of water and a torch.

l4_4.t: In my job, I talk to people about colour all the time. Lots of people want white walls in every room, but I try to help them choose something more exciting – a light green for a bedroom, maybe, or a warm orange for a kitchen. I'm not an artist, and I don't paint pictures. I just make people's homes look beautiful. I can usually finish one room in two days.

l5.t: Jack, have you seen the paintings for the art competition? They're all in the hall now.
Yes! Ruby's is amazing. At first I thought it was a big pink flower, but it's a flamingo standing in a lake.
Oh yes, Ruby loves birds. What did Daniel paint? He said he was going to do a horse.
He wanted to, but he said horses are too difficult to draw. So he did a big grey elephant instead. It's really good.
And Kai? He always paints the sea.
Not this time. He painted a green frog sitting on a leaf. It's very funny – it's got huge eyes.
What about Lucy? Did she paint her cat?
No. Her cat's black, and she says black paint looks too dark on paper. So she painted the yellow sun going down over the hills behind her house. The sky's orange and pink.
Lovely. And yours? You haven't told me!
Mine's a white boat on a dark blue sea. I wanted to put an orange fish in the water under the boat, but I didn't have enough time.
Well, I think you'll win!

l1_0.t: Did you get a new keyboard for your computer, Jess? Your old one hasn't got all its letters.
I wanted to, but the one I liked was too expensive. I'll ask for one for my birthday.
So did you buy anything?
Yes, a new mouse, because my old one stopped working. I looked at the cameras too, but only for fun.

l1_1.t: Peter, Grandma wants to see the photos from your school trip.
OK, I'll email them to her tonight.
She hasn't got a computer any more, remember? It broke.
Oh yes. Then I'll text them to her phone.
Her phone's too old for photos. Why don't you print them and send them by post? She loves getting an envelope with pictures in it.
Good idea. I'll do that.

l1_2.t: Shall we chat online tonight about our project? At five o'clock?
I've got a swimming lesson until six. What about eight?
I'm not allowed on the internet after half past seven. How about half past six?
OK, half past six. I'll be home by then.

l1_3.t: Dad, have you seen my laptop? I need to send my homework to my teacher.
Did you leave it at school?
No, I used it on the bus on the way home. And it isn't on my bed – I've looked.
Then it must be in the car. You had it on your knees when I drove you home from the bus stop.
Of course! Can I have the keys?

l1_4.t: I need a photo for the class website. What about the one from sports day?
Everyone's seen that one already. What about the school play?
It's too dark. You can't see anyone's faces.
Then use the picture from our trip to the forest. Everyone's smiling in it.
You're right. That's the one.

l2.t: Hello everyone, and thanks for coming. I'm from the city library, and I'd like to tell you about our new photography course for teenagers. Lots of people think the course is on Sundays, because that's when our book club meets, but it's actually on Saturday mornings. It starts at quarter past ten and finishes at twelve, and it lasts for six weeks. Last year the course cost twelve pounds, but this year the library is paying for some of it, so it's only eight pounds for all six weeks. You don't need an expensive digital camera. The camera on your mobile phone is fine. Your teacher will be Ms Delaney. That's D-E-L-A-N-E-Y. She takes photographs for newspapers and magazines, so she's got lots of great ideas. Every week you'll go out and take pictures around the city – in the park, at the market and by the river. At the end of the course, we'll choose the best photos from each student. We won't print them, because that's very expensive. Instead, we'll put them on the library's website, so your family and friends can see them online. If you'd like to join, please fill in a form at the front desk.

l3.t: Hi Sophie. Mrs Bell says you're organising the video call with the other school. Is it the school in Japan again?
No, we talked to them last year. Mrs Bell wanted a school in Canada this time, but they couldn't do it. So it's a school in Australia, near Sydney.
Cool! When is it? In the lunch break?

That's the problem. When it's lunchtime here, it's the middle of the night there. And after school, they're asleep too! So the call's at eight o'clock in the morning, before our lessons start. We have to come in early.
Eight o'clock! OK. And what are you going to do in the call? Ask them questions?
Tom's going to ask the questions – he's written about twenty! I'm going to show them photographs of our town on the big screen. They want to see what it looks like here.
Nice. I hope it works better than last time. Do you remember?
Oh yes! The internet was fine and we could see everyone on the screen, but the sound was terrible. Nobody could hear what the other students were saying. We just smiled and waved for half an hour!
That was funny. Is everything OK now?
Mr Lee says yes. But the school laptops are really slow. Daniel, could I borrow yours? It's much faster.
Of course. I'll bring it to school on Tuesday. Do you want me to take some photos of the call, too?
Thanks, but Mr Lee's already doing that. He's going to put them on the school website with an article about the call.
Great. I can't wait!

l4_0.t: Have you seen the website called Learn It? It's brilliant.
Is that the one where you can download songs?

No, that's a different one. There's a chat page where you can talk to students from other countries, but I haven't tried it yet. What I really love are the maths videos. They explain everything so clearly, and my homework's much easier now.

l4_1.t: Hi Ali, it's Kevin. I know we said we'd meet outside the cinema at four, but my mum needs me to help her at home this afternoon. Can we meet at six instead? The film starts again at quarter past six. I've got the cinema's address, so don't worry about that. Text me back, OK? Bye.

l4_2.t: Ryan, the phone bill came this morning. It's only ten pounds this month.
Is that bad?
No! Last month it was forty, because you were watching videos all the time when you weren't at home. You really listened to me. Well done – I'm very happy about this.
So can I have more time online at weekends?
Let's talk about that later.

l4_3.t: OK, everyone, before you start typing your stories, listen, please. Last week some of you lost your work because you didn't save it properly. Today, when you finish, click on the folder called 'Class 8B' and save your story there. Don't send it to me by email, and don't print it. I'll read everything on my computer tonight.

l4_4.t: So what did you think of the film? I loved the music.
Me too – the songs were amazing. But it went on for three hours!
Really? I didn't notice that. But I couldn't understand the story at all.
Oh, I thought the story was easy. Can I borrow the DVD again next week?

l5.t: Jack, can you help me write down everyone's job for the class website?
Sure, Ms Brown. Lucy first. She wanted to draw pictures for the home page, didn't she?
She did, but her drawings are a bit small for a screen. She's got a great camera, so she's going to take photographs at all our school events.
Good. What about Omar?
Omar's very organised and he checks his phone all the time. So he'll answer the emails that people send us.
That's perfect for him. And Hanh? She types really fast.
Yes, but she's also our best writer. She'll write the news stories – one every week.
OK. Ben said he wanted to choose the music for the website.
We aren't going to have music. It's annoying when you open a website and music starts! Ben's going to film a short video about our class instead. He's got a good camera on his mobile.
And Ella?
Ella loves games, so she's making a quiz about the school. Visitors can click on the answers and see their score.
Great. And what about me?
You can type all the information about our class trips.

l1_0.t: Who were you talking to on the phone for so long? Uncle Tuan?
No, I talked to him yesterday. It was Grandma. She wants to know what to buy for Linh's birthday.
Your cousin Linh?
Yes. I told her Linh wants a camera, so she's going to get her one.

l1_1.t: What are you going to do with your birthday money, Sam? Buy an MP3 player?
No, I can listen to music on my phone. I'd love a DVD player for my bedroom, but they cost too much.
So what are you going to get?
A new keyboard for the computer. My old one's terrible for games.

l1_2.t: Can you give me your email address? I'll send you the photos from the party.
Sure. It's kate dot lim at pix dot com.
So there's a dot between kate and lim?
Yes. Katelim without the dot was my old address. I don't use it now.
And is there a number after lim?
No, there aren't any numbers.

l1_3.t: How did you find out about the concert? Did you see the advert on TV?
No, I missed that. Joe sent me a text about it yesterday, but I already knew.
So how did you know?
I read about it on the band's website last week, and I bought the tickets at once.

l1_4.t: Mum, can we go to the phone shop today? It closes at seven, doesn't it?
It closes at seven on weekdays, but today's Saturday. On Saturdays it closes at six.
Oh no. It's already half past five!
Then get your coat quickly. We can still get there.

l2.t: Good morning, everyone. This term our class is starting an email project with a school in another country. Last year we wrote to students in Denmark, but this year our new partner school is in Norway, in a small town near the sea. Their English teacher is called Mr Brekke. That's B-R-E-K-K-E. He's very friendly, and he's visited our town before. There are twenty-eight students in his class. We have thirty-two in our class, so a few of you will share a partner. In your first email, please don't write about your family. You can do that later. This time, I want you to write about your hobbies, because that's an easy way to start a conversation. Write about eighty words, and remember to check your spelling. You can type your email at home or in the computer room at lunchtime. Please send it to me first, and I'll check it before I send it to Norway. The last day to send it to me is Friday. Some of you asked for Wednesday, but that's too soon. If you have any questions, come and talk to me after the lesson.

l3.t: Dad, the internet isn't working again. I can't open any websites. Is it our computer? It's quite old.
No, the computer's fine. I called the internet company this morning. They said there's a problem with the cables in our street, not in our house.
So when will it work again? Tonight?
Probably not until Thursday, I'm afraid. Someone's coming to repair the cables on Wednesday afternoon, and then it takes a day to work again.
But I have to send my English homework to my teacher by email tomorrow! I was going to download some new songs too, but that's not important.
Can't you send it from your phone?
I haven't got any data left this month. And the screen's too small to type a long story.
What about the library? It's open until eight.
It's always full after school, and you have to wait for a computer. Could I go to Grace's house? She lives next door, and her internet's from a different company.
Good idea. Call her first and ask her mum.
OK. But what about you? Don't you need the internet for work? Will you go to your office?
It's too far. I'll take my laptop to the café near the station. They've got free internet, so I'll work there all day tomorrow.
Lucky you! You'll drink coffee all day.

l4_0.t: So, do you like your new phone? It looks really big.
It's bigger than my old one, but it still fits in my pocket. And the battery lasts for two days, which is great.
Brilliant.
But I'm not happy with the photos. They're not very clear. My old phone took much better pictures!

l4_1.t: Hello, this is a message for Ava Jones. My name's Paul, and I'm calling from Teen Tech magazine. You sent us a photograph for our competition last month, and I'm happy to tell you that you're the winner! Congratulations! Your prize is a new digital camera. We've got your address from the form you filled in, so we'll post it to you next week.

l4_2.t: Do you use Teen Zone? I think it's great for school projects, and it's really easy to use.
I used to, but now there are adverts everywhere. Every time you click on something, another advert opens! So I stopped using it.
Really? They don't worry me.

l4_3.t: My cousin Hoa called me from Hanoi last night. We hadn't talked for months, so at first the conversation was a bit strange. But then she told me that her family is coming to stay with us in December! I couldn't sleep after that. I kept thinking about all the places I'm going to show her.

l4_4.t: Now, about tomorrow's trip to the museum. You can bring your mobile phones, but you don't need chargers, because we'll be back by three. You can use your phones on the bus, too. But before we leave, everyone must write their parents' phone number on this form, in case there's a problem.

l5.t: Kate, you're always on your phone! Who are you talking to?
Lots of people! My family lives all over the place. My grandma's in Scotland now.
Does she write you letters? My grandma always sends letters.
She used to, but now she loves video chats. She bought a laptop last year, and she calls me every Sunday so she can see my face.
And your brother? He's at university, isn't he?
Yes, and he never answers texts or calls! The only way to talk to him is in an online game we both play. We chat while we play.
Ha! What about your aunt in Canada?
She sometimes sends me postcards when she travels, but mostly we write long emails to each other. She tells me all her news.
And your dad? He's away for work a lot.
He sends voice messages to Mum, but I never listen to them, so he just sends me short texts – 'Good night', 'How was school?' – things like that.
And your best friend, Nadia?
We see each other every day at school, but we still talk on the phone for hours in the evening! My mum can't believe we have so much to say.

l1_0.t: Oh no, I've left something at home.
Your diary? Mr Green's checking them today.
No, my diary's in my bag. And I've got my library card, too.
So what is it?
The form for the museum trip. Mum signed it last night, but it's still on the kitchen table!

l1_1.t: Are you getting your football magazine again?
I usually do, but it's more expensive this month.
What about the games one?
My brother's already bought that, so I can read his. I'll get this one about animals. There's an article about sharks in it.

l1_2.t: Excuse me, I think there's a mistake on our bill. It says thirty pounds.
Let me see. Two pizzas – that's eighteen pounds – and two juices.
Yes, but it also says two ice creams. We didn't have any.
Oh, I'm sorry. So it's twenty-four pounds, not thirty. I'll bring you a new bill.

l1_3.t: Dad, I'm going to Anna's. I'll leave a note for Sam on the front door.
He always comes in through the garden. Put it on the fridge. He goes there first.
There are too many notes on the fridge already. He won't see it.
Then put it on his bed. He always throws his school bag there when he gets home.
Good idea.

l1_4.t: Have you chosen a topic for your history project?
I wanted to do castles, but Lucy's already doing that.
What about ships? You love the sea.
There aren't any good books about ships in the library. I'll do trains. My grandad's got a box of old train tickets, and I can put them in my project.

l2.t: Hello, everyone. My name's Helen Shaw, and I work for our local newspaper. I'm here to tell you about our Young Reporters competition. This year, we'd like you to write an article about an interesting person in your town. Last year the topic was buildings, and we got lots of articles about the castle, so we wanted something different! It could be a neighbour, a shop owner or even someone in your family. Your article must be no longer than two hundred and fifty words. Some students sent us five hundred words last year, and we couldn't read them all! You can type it or write it by hand, and send it to us by email or by post. Our newspaper is called The Kesworth News. That's K-E-S-W-O-R-T-H. You'll find our address on the back page. The winner will get a diploma and a new laptop. Last year's winner got a camera, but we think a laptop is more useful for a young reporter. We'll print the winning article in the newspaper on Saturday the twentieth of June. The newspaper usually comes out on Thursdays, but that week we're making a special weekend newspaper. Good luck, everyone!

l3.t: Hi Nina. You look happy!
I am! Do you remember I wanted to write to Ruby Hart, the writer of the Moon Island books?
Yes. Did you send her an email?

I wanted to, but there was no email address on her website. So I wrote her a real letter and sent it to the company that makes her books. I put a birthday card in the envelope too, because it was her birthday that month.
Nice. When did you send it?
In September, so I waited two months. I thought she'd never answer. Then yesterday a big envelope arrived.
What was in it? A signed book?
I hoped so! But no, it was a long letter, and at the bottom she drew a picture of the dragon from Moon Island. It's amazing. I'm going to put it on my bedroom wall.
Cool. What did she say?
I asked her how to become a writer. She said lots of people tell you to read a lot, and that's important, but the best thing is to write in a diary every day – even just a few lines.
Are you going to do that?
I've already started! And Mr Davis wants me to write an article about the letter for the school magazine. I'm doing that this weekend.
Maybe one day you'll write your own book!
Maybe – but not yet!

l4_0.t: Mum, can you help me with this form for the swimming club? I've already written my name and address.
So what's the problem? I've paid for it already.
It asks for the name and phone number of our doctor. I don't know them.
OK, I'll find them for you after dinner.

l4_1.t: Did you see the article in yesterday's newspaper about the old cinema? The photos were OK, but the best part was the interview with Mr Brooks. He lives next door to us! He told them about working at the cinema fifty years ago. I'm going to cut it out and keep it.

l4_2.t: Excuse me. I don't think this bill is mine. I only had a cheese sandwich and a coffee, but this says two burgers and a milkshake.
Oh, I'm so sorry. That's for the table by the window. Here's yours.
Thank you. And the sandwich was lovely.

l4_3.t: Remember, your projects about famous people are due on Friday. Every project must have at least three pictures and a list of the books and websites you used. If it doesn't have these, I can't give you a good mark. No, Tom, I'm sorry, I can't give you more time. Friday is the last day.

l4_4.t: Are you still buying Pop Teen every week?
No, I stopped last month. It's the same price as before, and there aren't more adverts than in other magazines. But all the articles are about the same three singers now. It's boring.
Oh, I didn't know that.

l5.t: Mum, the post's here! There's lots today.
Great. Is there anything for me? I'm waiting for my new driving licence.
Yes, this one's for you. It says 'Driving Licence' on the envelope.
Finally! Now I can drive again. What else?
This one's for Dad. It looks like a bill.
Oh dear. It's probably the phone bill. He won't be happy.
And here's a postcard for Grandma. It's got a picture of Rome on it.
That's from her friend Maria. She's on holiday in Italy. Is there a birthday card for Grandma, too? It's her birthday next week.
No, nothing else for Grandma. Here's Lucy's magazine – the one about horses. She gets it every month.
She'll be pleased. Anything from school? They said they'd send a letter about the trip.
No, nothing from school. And the newspaper isn't here yet.
It always comes later on Saturdays.
Oh, and look – this one's for me! It's my ticket for the concert in May!
Lucky you! Is that everything?
There's just an advertisement for a new pizza restaurant. Shall I put it in the bin?

l1_0.t: Have you got everything for the trip, Zara? Your passport?
Yes, it's in my bag with my ticket.
What about your diary? You always write in it on holiday.
Oh no, it's still on my desk! Thanks, Dad. I'll go and get it.

l1_1.t: How much was your train ticket to London, Noah?
It's usually twenty-four pounds, but I showed my student card, so it was half price.
So only twelve pounds? That's cheap!
Yes. My friend Jack forgot his card, so he paid twenty pounds for his.

l1_2.t: Shall we eat at the hotel tonight? I saw the menu – it looks good.
It's very expensive. What about the pizza place near the beach?
We had pizza last night. Let's try the fish restaurant by the harbour. The man at reception says it's the best in town.
OK, let's go there.

l1_3.t: I want to get something for Grandma from Edinburgh. Maybe a postcard?
You can send her a postcard, but get her a present too. What about a guidebook? She's coming here next year.
She's already got one. I'll get her this calendar with pictures of the castle. She can put it in her kitchen.

l1_4.t: Good morning. Can I see your passport, please?
Oh, I left it at the hotel. Is that a problem?
Not for hiring a car. What I really need to see is your driving licence.
Here it is. And do I pay by card now?
No, you can pay when you bring the car back.

l2.t: Hello, everyone. I've got some important information about our school trip to France in May. We'll leave school by coach very early on Tuesday the fourteenth. Many of you thought we were going on Monday, but that's a holiday, so it's Tuesday. Everyone must have a passport, of course. Please bring your passport to school next week, so I can make a copy of it. Don't bring your ticket – I've got all the tickets here in my office. Your parents need to fill in the yellow form and sign it. Please give the forms to Mrs Quinn, not to me. That's Q-U-I-N-N. She works in the school office. Every student also needs travel insurance. It costs fifteen pounds. Last year it was twenty, so it's a bit cheaper this time. You can pay at the office. While we're in France, you'll have to write in a diary every evening, in French, about what you did that day. It'll be part of your French project when we come back. Don't bring a laptop – an ordinary notebook is fine. OK, any questions?

l3.t: Hi Sara! How was Italy?
Amazing! But the start was a bit difficult.
Why? Was it the flight?
We didn't fly. The plane tickets were too expensive in August, and Dad didn't want to drive all that way. So we went by train. It took two days!
Wow. Was that the problem?
No, the train was fun. The problem was on the first night. Dad lost his wallet in the station in Paris. All his bank cards were in it.
Oh no! What about his passport and his ticket?
Luckily they were in Mum's bag. And we had travel insurance, so we got the money back later.
Where did you stay? In a hotel?
We looked at some hotels online, but my aunt lives in Florence, so we stayed in her flat. It was great.
Did you send any postcards? I didn't get one!
I wrote you one, honestly! I had your address and everything. But I forgot to post it. It's still in my bag – here you are!
Ha, thanks! So what did you enjoy most?
The food was great, and the museums were interesting, but the best thing was the boat trip to a small island. We swam all afternoon.

l4_0.t: Sorry, you can't go into Screen 2 with this ticket.
But I paid for it online this morning! And I'm fourteen.
Yes, but it's a ticket for Screen 3 – the film about the space ship. This is Screen 2. It's a different film.
Oh! I'm so sorry.

l4_1.t: Can you help me with this form? It asks for my date of birth, my address and the name of my school.
What's it for? The swimming club?
No, that's next month. It's for the library. When I've got a card, I can borrow ten books at a time.

l4_2.t: I start work very early, at six o'clock. First I collect the letters, cards and magazines at the office, and then I walk round the town with them. I read the newspaper on my break! Lots of people say hello to me. The worst thing is the dogs – some of them don't like me at all!

l4_3.t: Hi Jade, it's Sofia. I just got your card in the post. It's beautiful! And thank you so much for the book. I started reading it last night and I can't stop. You know me so well! I'll tell you all about my party at school tomorrow. Bye!

l4_4.t: Dad, have you seen today's newspaper? Look at page six!
Is that your football team?
Yes! There's a photo of us, and they wrote about my goal! I've never been in a newspaper before. I'm going to buy five copies – one for Grandma, one for Uncle Kai…
That's wonderful!

l5.t: Mum, have you got my passport? I can't find it.
Don't worry. I've got all the passports in my handbag. I don't want anyone to lose them.
OK. What about the train tickets? Are they in the blue bag?
No. I printed them this morning, but I forgot to take them off the printer. They're still there. Can you get them later?
Sure. And the insurance papers? Dad said they were in the kitchen drawer.
They were, but I've put them in the blue bag now, with the hotel information.
Good. I'm going to take my diary. It's on my desk. Shall I put it in my backpack?
Your backpack's already very full. Put it in the suitcase. There's space at the top.
OK, there – I've just put it in the suitcase. Oh, and Dad's looking for his driving licence. He needs it to hire a car in Spain. He thinks he left it in the car.
Tell him to look in his jacket. He always keeps it there, in the inside pocket.
Dad's just looked – you're right, it's in his jacket! I think we're nearly ready!

l1_0.t: What lessons have we got tomorrow morning, Leo? Is it History first?
No, History's on Tuesdays. Tomorrow's Wednesday, so it's Geography first.
And then Science after the break?
That's right. Oh no – I haven't finished my Geography homework yet! I'll do it tonight.

l1_1.t: Oh no, I've left it at home!
Your calculator? You can borrow mine for the Maths test.
No, I've got my calculator, and my pencil case. It's my dictionary. We need it for French after lunch.
Ask in the library. They've got lots of dictionaries on the shelves.
Good idea. Thanks!

l1_2.t: Shall we meet in the library on Friday to study for the exam?
It's closed on Friday afternoons. What about our classroom?
Mr Hill says students can't stay in the classrooms after four o'clock.
Then let's go to the school hall. The teachers put tables in there for pupils who want to do homework.
OK, see you there.

l1_3.t: Does the Science exam start at nine tomorrow?
We have to be in the hall at nine. But the teacher reads the instructions first, so we start writing at quarter past nine.
And it finishes at quarter to eleven?
Yes. It's an hour and a half long.

l1_4.t: Did you get your English test back, Sam?
Yes, this morning.
Did you get twenty out of twenty again?
Not this time. I made two small mistakes, so I got eighteen. My friend Paul got fifteen, and he's really happy with that.

l2.t: Hello, everyone. I've got some exciting news about the summer Science course at Brookfield University. It's for pupils in Year Eight and Year Nine, and it lasts for five days. Last year the course started on a Monday, but this year it begins on Tuesday, because Monday is a holiday. Every day you'll do experiments with university students, and you'll have lessons from real scientists. The course usually costs fifty pounds, but our school is paying part of it, so you only need to pay thirty-five pounds. That includes lunch every day. You don't need to bring any books – the university will give you all the information you need. But please bring a calculator, because there's a lot of Maths in the experiments. On the last day, we won't stay at the university. We'll all go by train to the Science Museum in London, and your families are welcome to come too. The course leader is Doctor Fenwick. That's F-E-N-W-I-C-K. She was a teacher at this school before she went to work at the university. If you'd like to go, please take a form from my desk today.

l3.t: Hi Nam. You look tired. Are you OK?
Not really. The exams start next week and I'm a bit worried.
Which one are you worried about? History? You always say there are too many dates to remember.
History's OK, actually. I've made lots of notes. And English is fine too. It's Science. I don't understand the part about electricity at all.
I can help you with that. Where do you usually study? In your bedroom?
I tried, but my little brothers are so noisy. The town library is quiet, but it's a long way from my house. So I go to the school library after lessons. It's open until six.
That's where I study too. Do you know what helps me remember things? I write the important information on small cards and stick them on my bedroom wall. Then I read them every morning.
Cards? Good idea. My teacher says we should make drawings, but I'm terrible at drawing.
What does your mum think? Is she angry about the exams?
No, she's really nice about it. She says I shouldn't study late at night, and that I need to sleep more. She's probably right.
Of course she is! And what about after the exams? Shall we go to the cinema to celebrate?
Everyone's going to the cinema. Why don't we go swimming at the new sports centre instead?
OK! And maybe a pizza afterwards?
Maybe – if I pass Science!

l4_0.t: Our new English teacher, Mr Ross, is great.
Is he funny? Our old teacher always told jokes.
Not really, he's quite serious. And he gives us more homework than our old teacher! But his projects are brilliant. This term we're making our own class magazine, and I'm writing an article for it.

l4_1.t: I didn't practise much for the Maths test because I thought it would be really difficult and I'd fail anyway. But when I opened the paper, I couldn't believe it – I knew how to do every question! I finished twenty minutes early. I haven't got my mark yet, but I'm not worried about it at all.

l4_2.t: Good morning, everyone. I know you wanted your test papers back today, but I haven't finished marking them yet – sorry. You'll get them on Friday. Now, one important thing. From next week, our History lessons will be on Thursday afternoons, not Monday mornings. Please write that down in your diaries now.

l4_3.t: Mum, can I do this Chinese course? It's for beginners, so it won't be too hard.
It looks good, and the price is fine. But look – the lessons are on Saturday mornings at eight o'clock. You never get up before ten at the weekend!
I would for this, I promise!

l4_4.t: Do you like the new school library?
It's great. There are new computers and lots of comfortable chairs.
I like it too, and it's open until six now, which is really useful. But most of the books are so old. I'd love to see some new stories on the bookshelves.

l5.t: So, Ella, how was your first week at the new school? Do you like your teachers?
They're all really nice, Dad. Mr Grant is my favourite.
Is he the young one who wears a tracksuit? Does he teach Sport?
No, that's Mr Ward. Mr Grant teaches us Geography. He's been to forty different countries, and he shows us his photos in every lesson.
And Mrs Okafor? Is she the one who plays the piano?
She plays the piano at home, but at school she teaches Science. We do experiments with her every week.
What about Miss Lopez? Is she from Spain? Does she teach French?
She's from Mexico, actually, and she doesn't teach languages. She teaches Mathematics. She's really clever – she can do difficult sums in her head!
So Mr Ward teaches Sport, then?
He wears a tracksuit because he was a football coach before. But he doesn't teach Sport now. He teaches History, and he tells us great stories about kings and queens.
And the last one, Mrs Hill?
She teaches Art. Our class is painting a big picture for the school hall. We have Music with Mr Brown, but I haven't met him yet.

l1_0.t: Have you decided what you're going to study at college next year, Daniel?
Well, my parents want me to do Science, because I always get good marks in it.
But you love music!
I do, but I'll play in a band in my free time. I'm going to study languages. I want to work in another country one day.

l1_1.t: Dad, have you seen my English dictionary? It isn't on the bookshelf.
Did you leave it on your desk?
No, I've looked there.
Then look in your school bag. You took it to your lesson yesterday.
Oh, here it is! Thanks, Dad.

l1_2.t: Mum, can you drive me to school tomorrow? My exam starts at nine.
Sorry, I need the car for work. Why don't you take the bus?
The buses are always late. I don't want to miss the start of the exam.
Then leave early and walk. It only takes twenty minutes.
OK, I'll do that.

l1_3.t: Dad, I need some things for the new term.
Didn't we buy you a new calculator last month?
Yes, and I've still got my ruler. But I need three notebooks – for Science, History and Geography.
OK, we'll get them at the shop tomorrow.

l1_4.t: Mum, the parents' meeting with my teachers is next week.
Is it on Monday? I'm working late on Monday.
No, it was on Monday last year. This year it's on Thursday, at six o'clock.
Thursday? That's my yoga class. Never mind, I'll go to yoga on Tuesday instead.

l2.t: Good afternoon, and welcome to Riverside Language School. I'd like to tell you about our summer English course for teenagers. Some of our courses last two weeks, but this one is three weeks long, and it starts on the first of August. Lessons are every morning from Monday to Friday. Breakfast is at eight o'clock, and the first lesson starts at half past nine. We finish at one, and then it's time for lunch. We put students in classes by level, so beginners and advanced students don't study together. There are never more than twelve students in a class, and most classes have only ten. In the afternoons, students can choose sports, art or music. And every Friday afternoon, all the students take part in a big quiz in the main hall. The winning team gets a prize! Before the course, every student does a short test online, so we know your level. If you have any questions, please email the course director, Ms Bryce. That's B-R-Y-C-E. She'll be happy to help.

l3.t: Hi Isla. Where were you on Saturday? We missed you at football.
I went to Northfield University with my sister Ruby. She's choosing a university for next year. Mum couldn't go with her, so I went instead.
Was it boring?

No, it was great! We went on a tour. The sports centre was big, but not as nice as ours in town. The science labs were very modern. But the best thing was the library. It's got six floors, and you can study there until midnight!
Midnight? I'd fall asleep! Did you talk to any students?
Yes, a few. I thought they'd say the hardest thing is studying all the time, but they said it's cooking for yourself! Lots of them live in student flats, and they have to learn to cook.
Ha! So does Ruby want to go there?
Yes, she wants to study History there. And I've decided what I want to study too.
Let me guess – Geography? You love maps.
I do, but I want to study languages. They have Japanese and Spanish courses, and students can spend a year in another country.
Sounds great. Maybe I'll go to the next open day with you. When is it?
In March. But you have to book a place online first.
I'll ask my dad about it tonight. I'm not sure he'll let me go, but I'll ask.

l4_0.t: How's your Geography project going? We've almost finished ours.
Not great. We chose volcanoes as our topic, and we've still got two weeks, so there's lots of time. But Jake hasn't done anything at all! Anna and I are doing all the work.
Tell your teacher!

l4_1.t: Mum, I've got my report! Look – Mr Shaw says I'm the best in the class at Science, as usual. And my English has got much better this year. I worked really hard for that, and I'm so pleased. Even my Maths mark is good! I can't wait to show Dad.

l4_2.t: OK, everyone, you have forty minutes for this test. Your names are already on the front, so don't worry about that. Now, the most important thing. Last time, lots of you lost marks because you didn't read the questions properly. So please, read every question twice before you answer. You can start now.

l4_3.t: Have you met the new girl, Yuki? She seems very quiet.
She's not shy at all when you talk to her. She sits next to me in Maths.
Is she in the basketball team?
No, she doesn't like sport much. But she speaks four languages – Japanese, English, French and Spanish!

l4_4.t: Hi Lucy, it's Dad. I'm calling because I've just remembered – your History essay is for tomorrow, and you said you hadn't started it! Please do it before you watch TV tonight. I'll be home at six as usual. And I can take you to the library on Saturday for your next project, if you like.

l5.t: So, Grace, what do your friends do after school? When I was young, we just played in the street!
Things are different now, Grandpa. Lily goes to French classes on Mondays. She wanted to learn the guitar, but her mum said languages are more useful.
Sensible woman. And Omar?
Omar's really clever. He goes to the chess club at the library. Last month he beat the teacher!
What about Hien? Does she do photography? She always has a camera with her.
She takes photos for fun, but her class is cooking. She learns to make food from different countries. Last week she made us a cake!
Lovely. And Joe? He's the boy who was in the school play, isn't he?
Yes, but he stopped doing drama. His Maths isn't very good, so his parents found him a teacher who gives him extra lessons on Wednesdays.
Poor Joe. And Sara?
Sara goes to the pool three times a week. Her coach says she might swim for the city team one day!
And what about you?
Me? I just do my homework, Grandpa!

l1_0.t: Are you still having guitar lessons, Ellie?
No, I stopped last year. My fingers always hurt!
So what do you play now? The drums? You always say you love them.
I'd love to, but our flat's too small and too quiet for drums. I play the piano now. My grandma gave us her old one.

l1_1.t: Did you see the singing competition on TV last night?
No, I wanted to, but my dad was watching the football on the big TV.
So you watched the football with him?
No, I went to my room and watched a film on my laptop instead – an old adventure one. It was great.

l1_2.t: Hello. How much are the tickets for the school play?
Adults pay five pounds, and students pay three pounds.
Great. I need one for me, and one for my mum.
So that's eight pounds altogether, please.
Here you are.

l1_3.t: Shall we meet at the station before the concert?
It'll be really busy there. Let's meet at the café opposite the concert hall.
That café closes at six. What about outside the ticket office?
Fine. See you there at quarter to seven.

l1_4.t: What are you going to draw for the art competition, Lucy? A horse again?
I've drawn so many horses! I thought about drawing our house.
That sounds nice.
But the competition is called 'People I Love', so I'm going to draw my grandma in her garden.

l2.t: Good morning! This is Radio Greenfield, and here's some news about this year's Greenfield Park Summer Festival. Last year the festival was only at the weekend, but this year it starts a day earlier, on Friday, and finishes on Sunday evening. Tickets are on sale now. Adults pay ten pounds a day, and children under sixteen pay just four pounds. Children under five go free. On Friday evening there's a film on a big screen in the park. On Saturday night, there's a concert by everyone's favourite pop group, The Kelby Brothers. That's K-E-L-B-Y. They've sold more than a million CDs! On Sunday afternoon there's a competition for young dancers. Last year it was for singers, but this time we want to see your best moves – hip hop, ballet, anything! You can't bring your own food or drinks into the park, but there are lots of places to eat. And don't forget to bring a blanket to sit on, because there aren't many chairs. See you there!

l3.t: Tom, have you seen the poster about the film competition? We could make something together!
Great idea. What kind of film? Maybe something about a normal school day?
Everyone will do that. What about a mystery? Something strange happens in the school library at night.
I love it! But who's going to be in it? My grandparents would be terrible actors.
Ha! We could ask people from our class. Kim and Sam are both in the Drama Club.
And my brother could play the librarian. He's nineteen, so he looks old enough.
Hmm, he's always busy. Let's just use our classmates.
OK. What about a camera? I could use my phone, but the picture isn't very good.
My dad's got a good camera, but he takes it to work. The school has some video cameras for students, though. Mr Lee says we can borrow one.
Perfect. Do you know what the prize is?
It's a day at a real film studio in London! Last year it was cinema tickets, so this is much better.
Amazing. When shall we start? We could start this afternoon.
I've got piano practice today. And we need to write the story first. Let's start filming on Saturday morning.
Fine. I'll write down some ideas tonight.

l4_0.t: Are you still watching that programme about space?
Yes, it's brilliant! Each programme is an hour long, but it feels like ten minutes. I never know what's going to happen next.
The actors aren't very good, though.
Who cares? I just love the story.

l4_1.t: I went to the new art museum on Saturday. It wasn't free – it cost twelve pounds, which is quite a lot. And I went with my cousin, who's a bit boring. But I had a great time, because you can touch everything! You can paint on the walls and play strange musical instruments. I'll definitely go back.

l4_2.t: Mum, can I go to the hip hop concert on Friday? The tickets are only fifteen pounds.
The price is fine, and I know you haven't got any exams this week. But it doesn't finish until midnight, and you're only thirteen. Sorry, Jack.
Oh, Mum!

l4_3.t: Have you seen this new magazine for teenagers? There are articles about pop music, and a competition every month. But the best thing is the drawing page. In every magazine, a real artist teaches you how to draw something. This month it's horses!
Can I borrow it when you've finished?

l4_4.t: This week's new film, Moon Dogs, is a cartoon, so you might think it's for little children. But it's quite long, and there are some scary parts, so I wouldn't take anyone under ten. Adults might find it a bit silly. But if you're between twelve and sixteen, you'll love it. It's funny and exciting, and the music is great.

l5.t: Ben, have you seen the list for the talent show? Lucas is going to sing!
Lucas? He's got a terrible voice! I thought he was going to play the guitar.
He broke his guitar last week, so he's going to sing instead. And Hoa's going to play the piano.
Really? I thought she was in the dance group.
She stopped going. But she's had piano lessons for years. She's really good.
What about Amy and Jess? Are they doing magic tricks again?
No, everyone's seen their tricks. This year they're doing a hip hop dance. They practise every lunchtime.
Is anyone doing a play?
No, not this year. The Drama Club is too busy with the school musical. But guess what? Mr Brown is in the show! He's going to tell jokes. He says he's the funniest teacher in the school.
Hmm, we'll see. I wanted to tell jokes myself, but now I'll do something else.
What will you do, then?
I'll play the drums. My neighbours will be happy when the show's finished – I practise every evening!

l1_0.t: Do you still want to be an actor, Emma?
Not any more. I'm not very good at remembering my words.
What about a photographer? You take great pictures.
Thanks, but that's just a hobby. I want to be a journalist and write for a newspaper.

l1_1.t: Can I watch the quiz show tonight, Dad? It's on at eight.
No, it isn't. The news is on at eight.
Oh. When's the quiz show, then?
At half past seven, after the cartoons. So you can watch it before dinner.

l1_2.t: Did you get Grandad's newspaper?
Sorry, Mum, they'd sold them all. I went to two different shops.
So what's in your bag?
A magazine about football. I wanted to get a new CD too, but they were too expensive.

l1_3.t: Which photo are you sending to the competition? The one of your cat?
I can't. The rules say no animals.
What about the one of the beach at sunset? It's beautiful.
Yes, that's my favourite too. The one of my family is nice, but it's a bit dark. So I'll send the beach.

l1_4.t: How did you hear about the new games shop?
