I saw an advertisement for it.
On TV? I saw one there last night.
No, I don't watch much TV. It was on the side of a bus! It was huge.
Really? Mum heard about the shop on the radio.

l2.t: OK, everyone, listen carefully. I've got some information about our visit to Bright TV Studios. We were going to go on Tuesday, but the studio changed the date, so now it's on Wednesday. The coach will leave from the school car park at quarter past eight, so please arrive by eight o'clock. The journey takes about an hour. When we get there, we'll go on a tour of the studios, and then we'll watch them filming a programme. It isn't the news or a quiz show – it's a cooking programme for children, and some of you might get the chance to taste the food! The trip costs six pounds. The school is paying for the coach, so that's just for your lunch. You'll also meet the presenter of the programme, Lucy Dawson. That's D-A-W-S-O-N. She'll answer your questions about working in television, so think about what you'd like to ask her. And please don't bring cameras – you can't take photos inside the studio.

l3.t: Grandad, can you help me with my school project?
Of course. What's it about?
It's about how people found out the news when you were young. Our teacher wants us to talk to someone old. Sorry!
Ha! That's OK, I am old. Well, when I was a boy, we didn't have a television. We listened to the radio every evening. My father always listened to the news at six o'clock, and we all had to be quiet.
Didn't you read newspapers?
My father bought one on Sundays, but newspapers were expensive for us. The radio was the most important thing in the house.
When did you get a TV?
In 1965, when I was twelve. It was black and white, and the screen was tiny. But all our neighbours came to our house to watch it!
That's funny. Did you always want to work in the news?
Not at first. I wanted to be a photographer. But I got a job at a newspaper, and I was a journalist for forty years. I wrote about sport.
Wow. Have you got any of your old articles?
Yes, there's a box of them in the garage.
Can I use some of them? I could stick them on a big poster for my class.
Good idea. I'll find them this evening.

l4_0.t: Did you read the article about our school in the local newspaper?
Yes. It says we've got the best football team in the city!
It's a nice article, isn't it?
Nice, but wrong! We lost every match last year. The journalist didn't check anything.

l4_1.t: Hi Josh, it's Kyle. About the cinema tomorrow – I know we said we'd meet at two, but my mum needs me to help her at home. Can we meet at four instead? The film's on again at half past four. Oh, and bring back that DVD you borrowed, if you remember. Bye!

l4_2.t: I've just finished a photography course at the art centre. I thought it would be easy – you just press a button, right? But there was so much to learn about light and colours, and my first photos were terrible! The course lasted six weeks, which was just right, and the teacher was really interesting. I'm glad I did it.

l4_3.t: Kim, that cartoon is so loud! I'm trying to work in the kitchen.
Sorry, Dad. Shall I turn it off? Or I can find something else.
No, you can watch it – it's Saturday. Just turn it down a bit, please.

l4_4.t: I saw the new space adventure film at the cinema last night. The actors were OK, but nothing special. And some of the pictures of space looked a bit cheap. But the music! It was played by a real orchestra, and it was amazing. I've listened to it about ten times since then.

l5.t: So, Josh, how's the media project going? What's everyone making?
It's great, Mum. Ana's group is making a newspaper about our school. She's writing an article about the new sports hall.
Really? I thought Ana wanted to do a photo exhibition.
She takes some photos for the newspaper too, but the exhibition idea was too difficult.
And Pete? He's very good at drawing.
Yes, so he's making a cartoon about a dog who goes to school. It's really funny.
What about Hung?
Hung wanted to make a film, but he couldn't find a camera. So he's making a radio programme, with music and news. He's recording it on his laptop.
Clever boy. And Becky? Is she writing a song? She's got such a nice voice.
She sings a bit in it, but it isn't a song. It's an advertisement for the school concert. She wants everyone to buy tickets!
And you, Josh? You haven't told me.
I'm making a magazine about video games. Ten pages! I've already written four, and Pete is drawing the pictures for me.

l1_0.t: Is that your brother in this photo, Amy? The boy with the glasses?
No, that's my cousin Leo. My brother's standing next to him.
Oh, the one in the cap?
No, that's Leo's friend. My brother's the one holding the guitar. He plays it all the time – even at breakfast!

l1_1.t: Dad, what are we getting Grandma for her birthday? Flowers again?
She's got lots of flowers in her garden. I thought about a scarf, but your aunt has already bought her one.
What about a photo of all the family in a nice frame?
That's perfect. She'll love that.

l1_2.t: Hi Josh. Where's your mum? I thought she was picking you up from school today.
She can't. She went to the supermarket this morning, and now she's next door at Mrs Hill's house.
Is Mrs Hill all right?
She isn't very well, so Mum's helping her.
That's kind. Well, you can come home with us.

l1_3.t: Have you got a big family, Nadia?
Quite big. My mum's sister has four children.
Four cousins! That's a lot.
And my dad's brother has two sons, so I've got six cousins altogether.
I've only got one!
That's nothing. My best friend has eight!

l1_4.t: Dad, what time are Uncle Mark and Aunt Lily coming? Two o'clock?
That was the plan, but their train's late. They phoned to say they'll be here at four.
Four? But we're having lunch at three!
I know. We'll have to wait for them. I'm hungry already!

l2.t: Hello everyone, and welcome to Riverside Youth Club. I want to tell you about our Family Sports Day. Every family in the town is welcome – parents, grandparents, brothers, sisters and even cousins! Last year it was on a Saturday, but this year it's on Sunday, the fourteenth of May, because the park is very busy on Saturdays. We'll start at ten o'clock in the morning and finish at about four. There are races for children, teenagers and adults, and grandparents can join the walking race! A ticket for one person costs five pounds, but if you come with your family, a family ticket is only twelve pounds. That's for up to six people. There's a café in the park, so you don't need to bring any food. But please bring a hat, because it can get very hot. You don't need special sports clothes – just comfortable shoes. If you want to join, please write to the organiser, Mrs Barlow. That's B-A-R-L-O-W. She'll send you more information. We hope to see you and your family there!

l3.t: Hi Tom! I heard your news. Congratulations – you're a big brother now!
Thanks, Lucy! She was born at about five o'clock on Sunday morning. Mum went to the hospital on Saturday night, but the baby didn't come until the next day.
Wow. And what's her name?
Well, I wanted to call her Lily, and Dad liked Grace, because that was his grandmother's name. But in the end Mum chose Rose. I think it's perfect for her.
That's a lovely name. So how do you feel about having a sister? Are you jealous? Everyone's going to look at her now, not you!
Ha! No, I'm not jealous at all. I'm really happy. But she cries a lot at night, so I'm quite tired. I fell asleep in Maths yesterday!
Oh no! Is anyone helping your parents?
Yes, my grandma's staying with us for two weeks. She doesn't take me to school – I still go by bike – but she makes dinner for us every evening. Dad's a terrible cook, so that's great!
Your grandma's soup is the best. Can I come and see the baby?
Of course. Come on Saturday.

Great. I wanted to buy her a toy, but my mum says babies get too many toys. And clothes are difficult because I don't know her size. So I'm going to give her a book of children's songs. My parents sang them to me when I was little.
She'll love it. Thanks, Lucy!

l4_0.t: My sister Hannah is nineteen and she's just finished her first year at university. It wasn't easy for her, because she lives a long way from home and she missed us a lot. But she's done really well – she got the best marks in her class! I've told all my friends about it. I want to be like her one day.

l4_1.t: Hi Sam, it's Ollie. It's my cousin Ben's birthday on Saturday, and my aunt's having a barbecue in her garden. She said I can bring a friend, so would you like to come? It starts at two. Don't worry about football – the match is in the morning, so we can do both. Call me back!

l4_2.t: Has someone moved into the house next to yours, Jess?
Yes, an old man called Mr Jones. My dad thought he'd be noisy because he's got two big dogs, but they're really quiet.
Does he talk to you?
Yes! At first I thought he wasn't very friendly, but yesterday he helped me carry my bike home when it had a flat tyre. He's lovely.

l4_3.t: Max, your Uncle Jack's arriving this evening and he's sleeping in your room, remember? So please put your clothes away and make the bed with clean sheets. You can sleep on the sofa. Dad's collecting Jack from the station, so you don't need to go. And don't worry about a present – we've already bought him one.
OK, Mum. I'll do it now.

l4_4.t: For next week's project, I'd like you to interview someone in your family who is over sixty – a grandparent, or maybe an old aunt or uncle. Ask them about their life when they were your age, and write down their answers. You don't need to bring any photos this time, and please don't draw anything. Just bring your notes to the lesson.

l5.t: Grandpa, look at this photo from cousin Mia's wedding. Can you see everyone?
Let me put my glasses on. Ah, there's your Uncle Peter. Is he eating cake again?
No, he'd already finished his cake! He's playing the guitar. He played all evening.
He's very good. And who's that next to him with the camera? Is that Aunt Sue?
Yes. She took photos all day because the photographer was late. She didn't stop to eat anything!
And where's your cousin Jake? Is he asleep in the corner? He usually sleeps at parties!
Not this time. Look, he's in the middle, dancing with the bride. He's a really good dancer.
Ha! And there's your grandma. She looks happy.
She is. She's holding Aunt Sue's baby, little Ellie. Grandma loves babies.
And what about your dad? Is he on the phone? He's always talking on his phone.
No, he put his phone away for the wedding. He's singing! Everyone asked him to sing a love song for Mia and her husband.
Your dad has a lovely voice. I wish I was there.

l1_0.t: Who was the boy you were with in the park, Ben? The one with the skateboard?
No, that's Harry from my class. My new friend is Dan. He's the one on the bike.
Oh. Does he play football with you?
Not really. He prefers cycling. He goes everywhere on his bike.

l1_1.t: How long have you known Kim? Did you meet at school?
No, she goes to a different school. We met three years ago on holiday in Spain. Our families were at the same hotel.
And now you play tennis together, don't you?
Yes, every Saturday at the tennis club.

l1_2.t: Mum, I'm having dinner at Tom's house tonight. Shall I take my new video game?
Not tonight – you'll be eating with his family, not playing games. It's polite to take something for his parents. What about some flowers for Mrs Shaw?
I thought about a book, but I don't know what she likes to read. OK, flowers.

l1_3.t: Is that your sister? She looks about fifteen.
Everyone says that! She's actually seventeen. She's learning to drive.
And your brother's twelve, isn't he?
Yes, he's the youngest in our family. He's always asking my sister to drive him to his friends' houses, but she can't yet!

l1_4.t: Are you having your birthday party on Saturday, Kevin?
My birthday's on Saturday, but my grandparents are visiting that day.
What about Sunday, then?
We're going to my aunt's on Sunday. So the party's on Friday, after school.
Great, I'll be there!

l2.t: Hi everyone. I'm here to tell you about the International Pen-friend Club. It's a great way to make friends in other countries and practise your English at the same time. The club is for teenagers, and you need to be at least eleven years old to join. Most of our members are between eleven and fifteen. At the moment we have members in thirty countries – last year it was only twenty, so we're growing fast! Joining costs eight pounds a year. It used to be ten, but we've made it cheaper this year. When you join, we'll send you the name and address of your new pen-friend. In your first letter, please don't write about school – everyone does that! Write about your family. Tell your pen-friend about your parents, brothers and sisters, grandparents and even your pets. If you'd like to join, speak to Mr Fenwick in the languages department. That's F-E-N-W-I-C-K. He'll give you a form. Remember, a pen-friend can become a friend for life. My mum still writes to her pen-friend in Japan after thirty years!

l3.t: Hi Sophie. Is it true your brother's getting married?
Yes! Daniel's getting married next month. I'm so excited.
Where's the wedding going to be? In the big church in town?
That was Mum's idea, but Daniel and Anna wanted to be outside. So it's going to be in my grandparents' garden. It's really big and there are lots of flowers.
Lovely. Is Anna the girl he went to school with?
No, everyone thinks that! They met at work – they're both nurses at the hospital.
Are you going to do anything special at the wedding? You're a good singer.
Anna's cousin is going to sing. I'm going to read a short poem about love. And Uncle Tom's taking all the photos.
Are you nervous?
Not about the poem – I've practised it lots, so I won't forget it. And I've already got my dress. It's blue and I love it. But I keep checking the weather on my phone. If it rains, we'll all get wet!
I'm sure it'll be sunny. How many people are coming?
Daniel wanted about fifty, and Anna wanted about eighty. In the end, they've invited a hundred guests! Grandma's worried there won't be enough chairs.
Ha! Well, I hope you have a great day.

l4_0.t: My grandad's seventy, but he still plays tennis twice a week. That's amazing! He always gives me some pocket money when I visit him, which is nice. But the best thing about him is his stories about when he was a teenager. They always make me laugh so much.

l4_1.t: Are you going to Chloe's party on Saturday?
I can't. My parents are going to my uncle's wedding, and someone has to stay at home with my baby brother.
Can't your grandma look after him?
She usually does, but she's on holiday. It's a shame – I bought a new dress for the party, too!

l4_2.t: Hello, Mrs Lee. We're going away for a week to visit my husband's parents. Could you keep this key for us, please? A man's coming on Wednesday to repair the washing machine, so could you let him in? Thanks so much. I'll bring you something nice from the seaside!

l4_3.t: What do you think of the new guy, Felix?
I like him. He said hello to everyone on his first day. He's really friendly.
Yes, I agree. He asked me to sit with him at lunch. He isn't great at football, though!
He says he prefers basketball. And his jokes aren't very funny.
Really? I think they're quite funny.

l4_4.t: Last year my grandparents sold their house and came to live with us. I was a bit worried at first, because I had to share a room with my sister. But actually it's great. Grandma helps me with my homework, and Grandpa and I play cards every evening. The house is never boring now!

l5.t: Mum, can we talk about my party on Saturday? Lots of people want to help.
That's nice. What about your cousin Zoe? She's good at cooking. Is she making sandwiches?
She wanted to, but Dad's already doing the food. So Zoe's going to put up the balloons. She's coming early in the morning.
OK. And your friend Ali? He's got a great camera.
Yes, but he says he wants to enjoy the party, not take pictures all the time. He's going to choose the music. He's got really good songs on his phone.
Perfect. And Grandpa's coming, of course.
I asked him to drive my friends home at the end, but he doesn't like driving at night. So he's going to organise some games. He knows lots of old party games!
Our neighbour, Mrs Grant, called this morning. She said she'd love to help.
Really? She makes amazing cakes.
Exactly. She's going to make a chocolate birthday cake for you.
Brilliant! And what about my sister? She always wants to do something.
Lucy wanted to choose the music, but Ali's doing that now. So she's going to take the photos with my camera.
Great. And who's going to clean up afterwards?
You are, Jamie!

l1_0.t: Did you have a burger at the café again today, Matt?
I wanted one, but they didn't have any. So I had pasta with tomato sauce.
Not the salad? You said you wanted to eat more vegetables.
I know. Maybe tomorrow!

l1_1.t: Jack, can you go to the shop for me? I'm making pancakes.
Sure. Do you need eggs?
No, I bought eggs yesterday, and there's plenty of butter in the fridge. But we haven't got any milk.
OK, I'll get a big bottle.

l1_2.t: Excuse me, how much is a cheese pizza, please?
A small one is seven pounds fifty, and a large one is nine pounds.
I'll have a small one, please. Does that come with a drink?
No, drinks are two pounds extra.
Oh. Just the pizza then, thanks. I've got some water in my bag.

l1_3.t: Shall we have our picnic in the park on Sunday?
It's always so busy there. What about the beach?
It's too far – it takes an hour by bus. Let's go to the river. There's a nice place under the trees.
Perfect. I'll bring the sandwiches.

l1_4.t: What are we having for dessert tonight, Mum? Chocolate cake?
I didn't have time to make a cake. I thought about a fruit salad, but Grandma doesn't like fruit much.
Everyone likes ice cream!
Good idea. There's some in the freezer. We'll have that.

l2.t: Hello, everyone. If you love food, listen carefully! This summer, the Green Street Community Centre is running a cooking course for teenagers. It's in the first week of August, and it lasts for five days, from Monday to Friday. Last year the course was only three days, but everyone wanted more time in the kitchen! Each day starts at half past nine and finishes at one o'clock, so you can go home for lunch – or eat what you've cooked! On the first day, you'll learn to make pizza. We'll make the bread ourselves, and you can choose what to put on top. Later in the week you'll cook soup, pasta and a chicken salad, and on the last day there's a cake competition. You don't need to bring any food – we'll buy everything. But please bring a plastic box, because you'll want to take some food home for your family. The kitchen has all the knives, plates and bowls you need. Your teacher is a real chef. His name is Paul Harding – that's H-A-R-D-I-N-G – and he works in the kitchen at the Riverside Hotel. The course costs forty pounds. To book a place, please call the centre before the end of June.

l3.t: Dad, it's Mum's birthday on Saturday. Can we cook a special dinner for her?
That's a lovely idea, Hannah. But on Saturday evening we're going to the theatre with Mum, remember?
Oh yes. What about Sunday lunch?
Your grandparents are taking her out for lunch on Sunday. Let's do it on Friday evening. She'll be tired after work, so she'll love it.
OK, Friday. What shall we cook? Roast chicken? It's her favourite.
It was her favourite, but she doesn't eat meat any more.
Pasta with vegetables, then?
Hmm, we have pasta every week. Let's do something different. What about grilled fish with rice? I can show you how to cook it.
Yes! And can Sam help?
Your brother can't cook at all! The last time he fried some eggs, he burned them. He can wash up after dinner – he's good at that.
Ha! OK. Do we need to buy anything?
Let me check. We've got rice, and there are plenty of lemons and potatoes. But there aren't any onions, so I'll get some tomorrow.
And a birthday cake?
Grandma phoned yesterday. She's making a chocolate cake and she'll bring it on Friday. So we don't need to make one.
Great. Mum's going to be so surprised!

l4_0.t: I went to the new café by the river yesterday. Everyone says you can see the whole river from the windows, but we sat at the back, so I didn't see much. The sandwiches were OK, nothing special. But the waiters were great – so friendly and funny. One of them even sang 'Happy Birthday' to my friend!

l4_1.t: Mum, is there anything to eat? I'm really hungry.
Didn't you eat your lunch at school? It was fish and chips today – you love that.
Yes, I ate it all. But I got up late this morning and didn't have time for breakfast, so I've been hungry all day.
There's some bread and cheese in the fridge.

l4_2.t: Lots of teenagers don't eat breakfast. They say they're not hungry, or they don't have time. But breakfast gives you energy for the morning and helps you to think at school. It doesn't need to be a big hot meal – a bowl of cereal, or some bread and fruit, is fine. Just try to eat something before you leave home every morning.

l4_3.t: Did you enjoy the school barbecue on Saturday?
Not really. The burgers were nice and they only cost a pound each. But there were so many people! I had to wait half an hour for my food, and I couldn't find anywhere to sit.
The band was good, though.
Yes, the music was great.

l4_4.t: Hi Ellie, it's Grace. About the picnic tomorrow – Mum's made lots of sandwiches and I'm bringing some fruit. We've got paper plates, too. But we haven't got anything to drink. Could you bring some lemonade or a bottle of orange juice? Thanks! See you at eleven.

l5.t: How was the food festival on Sunday, Josh?
Brilliant! There was food from all over the world.
What did your dad have? He loves steak.
He does, but the steak was really expensive. So he went to the Chinese stall and had noodles with vegetables. He said they were the best he's ever eaten.
And your mum?
She wasn't very hungry, so she just had a salad with cheese and tomatoes.
What about your sister? Did she get a burger? She always has burgers.
She wanted one, but the queue was too long. So she had a pizza instead. She ate the whole thing!
Ha! Did your grandpa come too?
Yes. He doesn't like trying new food, so he found a stall selling fish and chips. He was very happy.
And you?
I had a chicken curry from the Indian stall. It was really hot, so I needed lots of water! After that I wanted an ice cream, but they didn't have any left.
It sounds like a great day.

l1_0.t: Hello. What would you like to drink? We've got tea, coffee, milk…
Have you got any orange juice?
Sorry, there isn't any today. But we've got lemonade.
Lovely, I'll have a glass of lemonade, please. And my mum would like a cup of tea.

l1_1.t: Mum, where's the bread? It isn't on the table.
I put it in the fridge, so it stays fresh.
I've looked in the fridge. There's only butter and cheese.
Oh, sorry, I remember now. It's in the cupboard next to the cooker.

l1_2.t: Let's go to the café after school. What time does it close?
In winter it closes at five, but in summer it stays open until six.
It's June now, so that's OK.
Yes, and school finishes at half past three, so we'll have lots of time.

l1_3.t: Do you like carrots, Dan?
They're OK, but I don't love them. And everyone thinks I like potatoes, because I eat so many chips!
So what's your favourite?
Onions. I know it's strange, but I love them – fried, in soup, in salad, anything.

l1_4.t: What did you get at the market? Apples?
No, the apples looked a bit old. I wanted bananas, but there weren't any left.
So you didn't buy any fruit?
Yes, I did. I got some grapes. They're really sweet.
Great, I love grapes.

l2.t: Hello, Year 8! I'm here to tell you about this year's Food Fair. It's on Saturday the twenty-first of June – not the fourteenth, as we said in the school newsletter. Last year we had it in the school hall, but it was too hot and crowded, so this year it'll be outside in the school garden. If it rains, we'll move to the sports centre. Each class will have a stall and sell food from a different country. You can make pizza, pasta, curry, soup – anything you like! Students can come in free, but parents and other adults need a ticket. It costs three pounds, and children under five are free too. All the money will go to the children's hospital. There will also be a prize for the best stall. Last year the winners got cinema tickets, but this year the prize is a visit to a chocolate factory! I'm sure you'll all want to win that. If you have any questions, please talk to Miss Quinn. That's Q-U-I-N-N. She's the new cookery teacher, and you can find her in Room nine at lunchtime.

l3.t: Hi Ben! I saw you in the Corner Café on Sunday. Are you working there?
Hi Ruby. Yes, I started last month. I work every Sunday morning, from eight until twelve. I wanted to work on Saturdays too, but I've got football practice then.
Cool. How did you get the job?
My uncle owns the café. My neighbour worked there before, but she's gone to university, so my uncle asked me.
Do you cook? You make great pancakes!
Ha! No, the cook doesn't let anyone into the kitchen except to wash up. That's my job – I wash all the plates, cups and glasses. Sometimes I make drinks when it's busy, but not usually.
That sounds like hard work. Do you like it?

Yes. The money's OK, and I get a free breakfast, which is nice. But the best thing is the people. Lots of old people come in every week and they always talk to me. One man tells me about his travels around the world.
That's nice. What are you going to do with your money? Buy a new phone?
My phone's fine. I thought about getting a new bike, but my dad says I can have his old one. So I'm saving for a guitar. I want to start lessons in the summer.
Great idea!

l4_0.t: Last night I had dinner at Kenji's house. His mum made a Japanese fish soup. I usually hate fish, so I was a bit worried. But I tried it, and it was delicious! I had two bowls. I couldn't believe it. Now I want to try more Japanese food.

l4_1.t: Mum, can we get these chocolate biscuits?
You don't usually like chocolate biscuits, Maya.
I know, but they're Amy's favourite, and she's coming to stay tomorrow.
They're quite expensive, and they aren't on sale this week. But OK, put them in the basket. Amy's a lovely guest.

l4_2.t: Remember, it's going to be very hot tomorrow, so bring lots of water – at least two bottles. Don't bring sweets or chocolate. Bring healthy food like fruit, sandwiches and salad. And please don't buy burgers and chips at the café there. You need good food to walk all day. OK? See you at the bus stop in the morning.

l4_3.t: What did you think of the new Italian restaurant?
The pizza was amazing – the best I've ever had.
Me too. I loved it. But we waited a long time for the waiter, didn't we?
Did we? I didn't notice. And it was quite cheap, too.
Cheap? I thought it was really expensive!

l4_4.t: Today we're making something quick and easy. First, break three eggs into a bowl and add a little salt and pepper. Mix them well. Then cut an onion and a tomato into small pieces. Put a little oil in a frying pan and, when it's hot, add the eggs and the vegetables. Cook for three minutes, then put it on a plate. It's lovely with a green salad!

l5.t: So, Lucy, what's everyone bringing to the class picnic on Friday?
Well, I'm doing the sandwiches. I wanted to make chicken sandwiches, but some people don't eat meat, so I'm making cheese ones.
OK, I'll buy some cheese tomorrow. What about your friend Sam?
Sam's mum makes amazing pizza, so we asked him to bring some. But it's difficult to carry on the bus. So he's bringing drinks instead – two big bottles of lemonade.
Good. And your teacher? Is Mrs Hall bringing anything?
Yes. She's bringing all the plates and cups, because she doesn't want us to use glass.
Very sensible. And Hana?
Hana loves baking. She's making chocolate biscuits for everyone.
Lovely. What about Kevin?
Kevin said he'd bring water, but Mrs Hall said everyone should bring their own bottle of water. So he's bringing some apples from his grandparents' farm.
Good. His grandparents grow the best apples I've ever eaten. So, sandwiches, lemonade, plates and cups, biscuits and apples. Is anyone bringing a cake?
No, but there's a café in the park, so we can buy ice cream there if we're still hungry.
It sounds like a great picnic. Can I come too?
Sorry, Dad – no parents!

l1_0.t: Tom, you didn't eat any breakfast. Have you got a stomach ache?
No, Mum, my stomach's fine. It's my tooth. It really hurts when I drink something cold.
Oh dear. Have you got a headache too?
No, it's just the tooth.
Right. I'll phone the dentist and make an appointment for this afternoon.

l1_1.t: Hello, I'd like to make an appointment with Doctor Shaw for my daughter, please.
Doctor Shaw can see her at quarter past nine tomorrow morning.
Oh, that's too early. She's got an exam at school. Is there anything later?
There's half past ten or eleven o'clock.
Her exam finishes at half past ten, so eleven, please.
Fine. Eleven o'clock, then.

l1_2.t: Do you still play tennis on Saturdays, Kate?
Not any more. I hurt my arm last year, and the doctor said tennis wasn't good for it.
So do you go cycling with your brother?
I'd like to, but my bike's broken. I go swimming now, three times a week. It's great exercise, and my arm doesn't hurt at all.

l1_3.t: Good morning. Can I help you?
Yes, my son's got a cold. Have you got any cough medicine for children?
I'm sorry, we haven't got any today. We'll have some tomorrow.
Oh well. I'll take some soap, then. No, wait, we've got lots at home. Just this toothbrush, please. He needs a new one.

l1_4.t: Sam, what happened to your leg? Did you fall off your skateboard again?
No, I haven't used it for weeks.
Was it at football, then?
Everyone thinks that, but I wasn't even playing. I fell down the stairs at school because I was carrying too many books!

l2.t: Hello, everyone. As you know, next week is Health Week here at Greenfield School, and I'd like to tell you what's happening. There are lots of activities at lunchtime every day, but the biggest event is the Fun Run. We planned it for Wednesday, but the men are cutting the grass on the field that day, so the Fun Run will be on Friday afternoon instead. Last year the run was five kilometres, and lots of younger students found it too long. So this year it's only three kilometres – that's two times round the park. Please wear trainers, and bring a bottle of water with you. Don't bring sweets or cola, please! On Tuesday, our school nurse is giving a talk in the hall about how to sleep well and stay healthy. Her name is Mrs Finch – that's F-I-N-C-H. She's new this year, so come and say hello. And every morning there'll be a healthy breakfast in the dining room from eight o'clock, with fruit, eggs and fresh bread. It usually costs two pounds, but during Health Week it's only one pound fifty. See you there!

l3.t: Hi Jake. I saw you in the park really early this morning. Were you running?
Yes, with my dad. We go every day now.
Really? Are you training for the school football team?
No, I'm already in the team. It's for my dad. He went to the doctor last month because he felt tired all the time, and the doctor said he had to get fitter. So I said I'd help him.
That's kind of you. But why so early? Why not after school?
I have too much homework after school, and Dad doesn't get home from work until eight in the evening. So we go at half past six, before breakfast. It's hard to get up, but it feels great afterwards.
Do you go running on Sundays too?
No. We wanted to go swimming on Sundays, but the pool's closed for repairs. We thought about tennis too, but it's really expensive at the sports centre. So we take our bikes and ride along the river.
That sounds lovely. And is it working? Is your dad thinner now?
Not much yet! But he says he isn't tired after work any more, and he has much more energy. He used to have a bad back too, but it doesn't hurt now.
That's brilliant. My mum always says she wants to do more exercise.
She could come running with us!
She'd never get up at six! But I'd love to come on a bike ride. Can I join you next Sunday?
Of course! We leave at nine o'clock.

l4_0.t: How was the dentist, Chloe? Were you scared?
Not really. I've been lots of times. And it was really quick, so I didn't get bored.
So was everything OK?
Yes, but I couldn't believe what she said. I eat sweets every day, and she said my teeth are perfect! I really thought I'd have a problem.

l4_1.t: Hello, this is Mrs Lee, the nurse at Park School. Your son Daniel is fine, so please don't worry – there hasn't been an accident. But he's got a high temperature and he says he feels sick. I've given him some water, and he's lying down in my room. I think he should go home and rest. Could you come and get him as soon as possible? Thank you.

l4_2.t: Is your grandma still going to that exercise class?

Yes, twice a week at the sports centre. At first I thought it would be too hard for someone who's seventy-two. But she's really good at it! She sleeps better, and she walks to the shops now. I think it's the best thing she's ever done.
Is it expensive?
No, it's cheap for older people.

l4_3.t: I saw you at the hospital yesterday, Lan. Was it your arm again? You broke it in the summer.
No, my arm's fine now. The doctor checked it last month.
Your grandad works there, doesn't he?
He did, but he stopped last year. No, I went to see my aunt. She had a baby girl on Tuesday! She's so small and beautiful.

l4_4.t: OK, everyone. Today we're running round the field four times. It's hot, so you won't need your jackets, and there's water by the door if you need it. But listen – this is the most important thing. Last week lots of you ran really fast at the start, and then you had to stop because you were too tired. So start slowly today. You'll finish much more easily.

l5.t: Welcome home, Mai! How was the sports camp?
Great, Dad, but lots of people had to see the camp nurse!
Oh no! What about Lily? She was so excited about the swimming.
She swam every day, but on Wednesday her ear started to hurt. She thought she was getting a cold, but the nurse said it was earache from the water.
Poor Lily. And your swimming teacher, the young man?
Mr Grant? He carried all the boats to the lake by himself on the first day, and then his back hurt for the whole week. He had to teach sitting in a chair!
Ha! What about Tom? Did he break his leg again?
No, he was very careful this time. But he helped with the barbecue on Friday and cut his finger with a knife.
Oh dear. Was it bad?
No, the nurse cleaned it and put a plaster on it. The cook had a worse problem. She burnt her hand on the cooker.
Ouch. And you? You didn't get toothache again, did you?
No, my teeth were fine! But on the last night I ate too much cake at the party, and I had a stomach ache all night.
Well, no cake for you this week, then!

l1_0.t: Anna, why have you got that bandage? Did you hurt your hand at volleyball?
No, my hand's fine. I fell over at the ice rink on Sunday and landed on my arm.
Is it broken?
No, the doctor checked it. But it hurts a lot.
Can you still walk to school?
Yes, my legs are OK, luckily!

l1_1.t: Excuse me, is there a chemist's near here?
There used to be one next to the bank, but it closed last year. There's a new one opposite the school on Green Street.
Is that near the station?
No, the station's the other way. Go straight on, and the chemist's is on your left, opposite the school.

l1_2.t: I want to do an exercise class at the sports centre. Which one do you go to?
The cycling class. It's on Tuesday evenings.
I'd like that, but I work late on Tuesdays. What about yoga?
It's full this month. But there's a dance class on Thursdays. It's really good for your heart.
Thursday's perfect. I'll try that.

l1_3.t: What did the doctor say, Minh?
I've got flu. He said I have to stay at home for three days.
Oh dear. You wanted to go back to school on Thursday.
I know. That's only two days, but he said no. And I can't play football for five days.
Well, you need to rest.

l1_4.t: Have you packed everything for the school trip, Lily? What about your toothbrush?
Yes, Dad. It's in my bag, with the soap.
And your comb? Your hair gets terrible without it!
Oh no, I left it in the bathroom. Can you get it for me, please?

l2.t: Hi everyone. I'm here to tell you about a special course for teenagers called Help in an Accident. You'll learn what to do if someone falls and hurts their head, cuts their hand or burns themselves in the kitchen. The course is on a Saturday – not this Saturday, but next Saturday – and it's one day only. We usually start at nine o'clock, but this time we're starting at half past nine, so you don't have to get up too early! It finishes at three. We wanted to have the course in the sports hall, but there's a basketball match there that day, so we'll be in the school library. The course normally costs fifteen pounds, but the hospital is paying seven pounds for each student, so you only need to pay eight pounds. Please bring something to eat for lunch. Your teacher on the day is a nurse from the City Hospital. Her name is Mrs Hartley – that's H-A-R-T-L-E-Y. She's worked in hospitals for twenty years, so she knows a lot! If you'd like to come, please tell your class teacher before Wednesday.

l3.t: Daniel! Your leg! What happened? Did you hurt it on the school ski trip?

Yes, but not while I was skiing. I was really careful on the mountain. On the last evening, I was walking from the hotel to a restaurant, and I fell on the ice. I heard a noise and I knew my leg was broken.
Oh no! Did you have to stay in hospital?
Only for one night. The doctors wanted me to stay for two nights, but my leg was OK, so they let me go home with my mum the next day.
Was it terrible in the hospital?
Well, the food was actually OK, and I had my phone, so I wasn't bored. But my leg hurt so much that I couldn't sleep at all.
Poor you. How are you getting to school now? You can't take the bus with that leg.
No, there are too many steps. And Dad starts work really early, so he can't drive me. So the school is paying for a taxi every morning for six weeks.
Lucky you! I'd love to come to school in a taxi.
It's not that great! Everything is difficult when you can only use one leg. I can't even carry my school bag. My brother's bringing me the homework I missed, but I need help at school.
Well, I can help with that. I'll carry your bag for you between lessons.
Really? Thanks, Hoa. That's really kind.
And shall we go to the cinema on Saturday?
Not with this leg! Maybe next month.

l4_0.t: Hurry up, Ben, or you'll be late for football training.
I don't want to go today, Mum.
Why not? Is your knee still hurting?
No, it's fine now. And I like the new coach – he's great. But I've had exams all week and I went to bed late every night. I really need a rest.
OK, you can stay at home this time.

l4_1.t: Hi Jo, it's Pam. I'm sorry, but I can't go running with you tomorrow morning. I've got a dentist appointment at nine o'clock and I can't change it. Don't worry, nothing hurts – it's just a check. Can we go on Friday morning instead? Same time, at the park gate? Call me back and tell me if that's OK.

l4_2.t: From this month, we can only drink water or milk at lunchtime in our school. No cola or other sweet drinks. Some of my friends are angry about it and say it isn't fair, but I don't agree. Sugar is really bad for your teeth, and most of us drink too much of it. I feel much better since I started drinking water, so I think the school is right.

l4_3.t: Nice helmet, Max! Is it new?
Yes. My old one wasn't broken, and it wasn't too small either. And I haven't had an accident, don't worry!
So why did you change it?
Mum read something about bike accidents in a magazine. She said my old helmet wasn't safe any more because it was too old, so she bought me this one.

l4_4.t: Lots of people think they need to join an expensive gym to get fit. Other people think they have to play a team sport, like football or basketball. But that's not true. The easiest thing you can do for your health is to walk more. Walk to the shops – don't drive. Take the stairs, not the lift. If you walk for thirty minutes every day, your heart will thank you!

l5.t: So, Megan, your mum says the whole family is doing more exercise now.
Yes, Grandma! It started in January. Dad goes running every morning before work.
Running? I thought he played tennis.
He used to, but his tennis friend moved away. So now he runs round the park.
And your mum? She loves dancing.
She does, but the dance class is on Monday evenings and she works late then. So she goes swimming at the new sports centre on Saturdays.
Good for her. What about your brother? Is Sam still in the football team?
No, he left. He says football's boring now. He's started doing yoga with his friend. He says it's good for his back.
Sam doing yoga! I don't believe it. And Uncle Paul? He's always so busy.
He bought a new bike, and now he cycles to work every day. It's twenty kilometres!
Goodness! And you, Megan? Do you still walk to school every day?
Yes, but that's not really exercise, is it? I've joined the dance club at school. We practise three times a week, and it's great fun.
Well done, all of you!

l1_0.t: Are you still going to dance classes, Rosie?
No, I stopped in the summer. I've started a new hobby now.
Is it photography? I saw you with a camera yesterday.
That was my brother's camera. No, I've started painting. I go to a class at the museum on Saturday mornings.

l1_1.t: Do you want to go for a bike ride on Saturday, Josh?
I can't. My bike's broken, and Dad can't repair it until next week.
Oh. What about a picnic in the park, then?
It's going to rain all weekend. Let's do something inside.
OK, let's go to the new science museum. It's free on Saturdays.
Great idea!

l1_2.t: Are you going to the concert on Friday? How much was your ticket?
Normal tickets are twenty-four pounds.
Twenty-four! I only paid twelve pounds last year.
Everything's more expensive now. But I'm a member of the band's fan club, so I only paid twenty.
That's not bad. Are you going with Lucy?
Yes, her mum's going to drive us there.

l1_3.t: What's in all these boxes, Jamie? Are they your grandad's stamps?
Yes, he collected stamps for fifty years. But I don't – I think they're boring.
What do you collect, then? Coins?
I tried collecting coins, but it was too expensive. I collect football cards. I've got nearly five hundred now!

l1_4.t: Dad, have you seen my guitar? I've got a lesson in half an hour.
Isn't it under your bed? That's where you usually keep it.
No, I've looked there.
Did you leave it at school after the concert?
No, you drove me home after the concert, remember? I had it with me.
Oh dear, it's still in the car! I forgot to bring it in. Sorry!

l2.t: Hello, I'm Paul from the Westbridge Photography Club, and I'm here to tell you about our competition for young photographers. Anyone aged eleven to sixteen can enter. Last year the subject was people, and we got some wonderful photos of families and friends. This year the subject is animals. Your photos can show pets, farm animals or wild animals – it's up to you. You can send us three photos, but please don't send more than that! The last day to send your photos is the fourteenth of June. The winner will get a fantastic prize. Last year it was a computer, but this year it's a new camera from the camera shop on King Street. There are also prizes for second and third place – books about photography. The best photos will be in the town museum during the summer holidays. Our judge this year is a famous photographer, Mr Dawson. That's D-A-W-S-O-N. He has taken photos of animals for lots of magazines. To find out more, come to one of our club meetings on Thursday evenings.

l3.t: Hi Ben. Did I see you in the library at lunchtime? You never go there!
Ha! I've joined the quiz club. We meet there on Mondays and Wednesdays.
The quiz club? Why? Did Mr Hill ask you to join?
He asked everyone in our class, but that's not the reason. My cousin Leo is the captain, and he said they needed someone who knows a lot about sport. So I said yes.
Well, you do know everything about football! What do you do at the club?
We practise with old quiz questions. There are questions about history, science, music... History's OK, but music is the hardest for me. I only know the bands my sister listens to!
And is there a competition?
Yes, there's a big quiz for schools in March. It's at the city museum. The winners get books for their school library and a trip to London.
Wow. Do you think you'll win?
Probably not! Last year our team came fourth. But the other members are really clever, so we might.
Can people come and watch?
Yes, family and friends can come, and it's free. Why don't you come? You could bring your camera and take photos of our team for the school magazine.
Great idea! I need some photos for my next article anyway.

l4_0.t: Mum, for my birthday this year, I don't want a dance party at home like last year.
OK. What about the cinema?
It's too expensive for twelve people. I'd like to have a picnic in the park with all my friends. We can play games and take a ball.
That's a lovely idea, if it doesn't rain!

l4_1.t: My grandpa gave me his old MP3 player last month. It isn't small – it's quite big, actually – and it was expensive when he bought it. But it's got about two thousand songs on it from the sixties and seventies. I listen to it every day on the bus, and I've found lots of great bands that I didn't know before!

l4_2.t: How was the toy museum, Ella?
I thought it would be boring – it's just old toys, right? But actually it was brilliant. You can play with lots of the toys, and there's a room where you can make your own.
Was it crowded?
No, it wasn't busy at all. You should go!

l4_3.t: Hello, this is Mark from the music school. This message is for Tim's mum. Tim's guitar teacher, Anna, is playing in a concert on Thursday evening, so she can't teach him at six o'clock this week. Could Tim come at four o'clock instead, on the same day? The price is the same, of course. Please call me back. Thanks.

l4_4.t: I started drawing comics two years ago. At first they weren't very good, and I was worried that people would laugh at them. But I practised every day, and last month the school magazine printed one of my stories. Everyone in my class read it! My mum put a copy on the fridge, and I smile every time I see it.

l5.t: So, Nina, how's your new school? Have you made any friends?
Yes, lots! There's Alex. He sits next to me in maths. He's always drawing in his book, but his real hobby is the guitar. He practises every evening and he wants to start a band.
Great! Who else?
Hana. She used to go to dance classes, but she stopped last year. Now she's crazy about photography. She takes her camera everywhere.
And the boy you talked about yesterday? Ryan?
Ryan collects old coins. He's got coins from more than forty countries! His brother loves reading, but Ryan says books are boring.
Ha! And Sophie? Does she like taking photos too?
No, Sophie's a dancer. She goes to classes four times a week, and she's in a show at the theatre next month. Her family goes camping every summer, but she doesn't really like it.
And does anyone like art, like you?
Yes, Minh. He draws amazing pictures of animals. He wants to make films one day, but at the moment he just draws all the time.
They all sound really nice.

l1_0.t: What shall we cook at the barbecue tonight? Burgers?
We had burgers last time. What about some fish?
Your brother doesn't eat fish. Let's get sausages – everyone likes those.
OK. I'll buy some on the way home from the beach.
Good. And can you get some bread too? We haven't got any.

l1_1.t: Shall we meet at the bus stop and go to the beach together?
The bus is always late. I'll go on my bike. Let's meet at the beach café.
The café's closed on Mondays.
Oh, OK. Then let's meet in the car park next to the beach. I'll wait for you there at ten.

l1_2.t: When does the concert at the festival start? Seven o'clock?
The doors open at quarter past six, and the first band starts at quarter to seven.
And when's our favourite band on?
Not until quarter past seven. But I want to hear the first band too, so let's get there early.

l1_3.t: Did you find anything good at the market, Tom?
I wanted some old CDs for Dad's CD player, but they were too expensive.
What about the paintings? There are always some nice ones.
I saw a nice one, but it was too big to carry. So I bought these comic books. Five for two pounds!

l1_4.t: Hello. I need a tent for a school camping trip.
This big blue one is very popular.
It's too heavy for me to carry. What about the small green one?
That's only for one person. This orange one is for two people, and it's very light.
Perfect. My friend Ana can share it with me. I'll take it.

l2.t: Good morning! This is Radio Bay, and I've got some news for young people who get bored in the summer holidays. Sandy Bay Holiday Club is back! It's for children aged ten to fifteen. The club starts on Monday the twenty-second of July and it goes on for two weeks. Every day there's swimming in the sea and sailing, and this year there's something new: photography. You'll learn how to take great photos of the beach and the animals that live there. Last year we did painting, but not many people wanted to do it again. You don't need to bring a camera – we'll give you one. But please bring a hat, because it gets very hot on the beach. Lunch is a picnic on the beach, and that's in the price, so you don't need to bring any food or drinks. It costs fifteen pounds for one day, or twelve pounds a day if you come for the whole week. To book a place, phone Kelly Mabbott. That's M-A-B-B-O-T-T. Have a great summer!

l3.t: Ryan, have you heard? Mrs Collins is leaving at the end of term. She's going to live in Scotland.
I know. I'm really sad – she's the best teacher we've ever had. Shall we have a party for her on the last day?
Good idea! It can be a surprise. Her birthday's in December, so she won't guess.
Where can we have it? The school hall's nice and big.
There's a concert in the hall that day. What about the park? We could have a picnic.
It might rain. Let's just have it in our classroom. We can make it look nice.
OK. My sister's going to make a cake – she makes amazing ones. Can you play your guitar? Everyone loves it when you play.
Sure. I'll learn one of her favourite songs. And Max can take photos with his new camera.
Perfect. We should buy her a present too. Everyone can give a pound.
What about a book? She reads all the time.
She's got hundreds of books! She always talks about her garden. Let's get her a nice plant.
Good idea. A camera would be nice too, but it's too expensive.
When shall we get the classroom ready? On Friday morning, before school?
That's too early – the school doors don't open until eight. And Friday lunchtime is too late. Let's do it on Thursday after school.
OK. Thursday at half past three, then.

l4_0.t: Is that the book Mr Ali told us to read in the holidays?
Yes. I thought I wouldn't like it because it's got four hundred pages. But I couldn't stop reading! Every chapter ends with something surprising. I read it in three days.
Is the English hard?
No, it's quite easy, actually.

l4_1.t: Everyone asks me why I joined the street dance class. My sister goes to it, but she didn't ask me to come – she was really surprised when I arrived! And none of my friends dance. I just wanted to do some exercise in the holidays, because I sit at my computer too much and football has finished for the summer. And now I love it!

l4_2.t: Dad wanted to go to the mountains again this year.
Oh no, all that walking! Can't we go to the beach?
Your sister doesn't like the beach – she gets too hot. So we've decided on Barcelona. There are beaches near the city, but we'll mostly visit museums and parks.
Great! I've always wanted to go there.

l4_3.t: Hi Kim, it's Lucy. You know the party at Sam's house on Saturday? I want to take some photos there, but my camera's broken. Could I borrow yours? I'll be really careful with it, I promise. I can come and get it on Friday after school. See you at the party! Thanks!

l4_4.t: Our new youth club opened last month in the old library on Bridge Street. We've already got sixty members, but we want more! There's a music room with guitars and drums, a computer room, and an art room where you can paint and draw. It's open every evening from four until eight, and it's free. So come along and bring your friends – you can join on your first night!

l5.t: So, Oscar, how was your first week at the holiday club?
Brilliant, Mum! On Monday we were going to ride our bikes along the river, but it rained all day. So we went to the transport museum instead.
Oh, you love that place. What about Tuesday?
Tuesday was art day. We painted pictures of the sea. Mine's in my bag. I'll show you later.
Lovely. And Wednesday? Did you go dancing? The club's website said there was a dance class.
That's next week. On Wednesday the weather was good, so we did the bike ride that we missed on Monday. We cycled twenty kilometres!
Wow! You must be tired. And Thursday?
We were going to go swimming, but the pool was closed. So we had a big quiz in the hall instead. My team came second.
Well done! And today? Did you have the picnic?
No, that's next Friday. Today we learned how to put up tents in the field, and tonight we're camping there! I've only come home to get my sleeping bag.

l1_0.t: Mum, I'm late for school and I can't find my keys. Did you put them on the table in the hall?
No, I didn't touch them. Have you looked on the sofa? You were watching TV there last night.
I've looked everywhere in the living room. They're not there.
Wait – I can see them. They're in the bathroom, next to the towels. You left them there when you had a shower!
Thanks, Mum!

l1_1.t: So how's the new flat, Lisa? Do you like it?
It's lovely. The kitchen's really big, so Mum's happy – she loves cooking.
And is there a dining room?
Yes, it's nice, but we only eat there at weekends. My bedroom is the best room, though. It's got a huge window and lots of shelves. I spend all my time there!

l1_2.t: Did you find anything at the furniture shop, Sam?
Yes! I wanted some new curtains, but they were too expensive.
What about a lamp for your desk?
My dad's going to give me his old one. So I bought a clock for the wall. It looks like a football!
That sounds great.

l1_3.t: Hi Rosa, I'm in your street, but I can't find your house. Is it the one with the garage?
No, that's my neighbour's. Ours hasn't got a garage. Look for the blue gate.
Oh, I see it. Is it next to the shop?
Yes. The flat above the shop is my cousin's, and we're the house next to it. Come in – the door's open!

l1_4.t: Dad, can I go to Tom's house now?
Not yet. Have you made your bed?
Yes, I did it after breakfast. And I cleaned my bedroom floor yesterday.
OK, good. But there are still some dirty bowls in the kitchen. Wash those first, please, and then you can go.
Oh, all right.

l2.t: Hello, everyone. I want to tell you about our trip to Hilltop Farmhouse, a museum that shows how families lived two hundred years ago. We planned to go on Thursday, but the museum is closed that day, so we're going on Friday instead. Please don't come to the classroom that morning. We'll all meet in the school hall, because it's bigger. The bus arrives at half past eight, and we'll leave at quarter to nine. Don't be late – the bus won't wait! At the farmhouse, you'll see all the rooms. The bedrooms are very small and there's no bathroom – people washed in a big bowl! But the best room is the kitchen. There's no fridge or cooker, just a big fire. You won't cook soup, because that takes too long, but you'll make bread, and you can take it home with you. Our guide for the day is Mrs Oakley. That's O-A-K-L-E-Y. She lived on the farm when she was a child, so she knows lots of stories about the house. Bring a packed lunch and a warm coat, because the old house has no heating and it's very cold inside.

l3.t: Hi Jack. Is it true that you're moving house?
Yes, it is. But don't worry, we're staying in the same town.
Oh good! I thought your mum had a new job somewhere else.
No, she's still working at the hospital. And our flat has enough bedrooms. But we got a dog last year, and he really needs a garden. The new house has a big one.
Great. So are you moving this weekend?
We wanted to, but the van wasn't free. So it's next Saturday. Then I'll have two weeks to get my room ready before school starts.
Can I help?
That would be great. Dad and my uncle are going to carry the furniture, and Mum's cleaning the kitchen. Could you help me put my books into boxes? I've got hundreds!
Sure, I love books. Is your new bedroom bigger than your old one?

Actually, it's about the same. And the house is further from school, so I'll have to take the bus. But there's a big room downstairs, and we're going to use it for games and table tennis. That's the best thing about it.
Cool! Will you send me your new address?
I'll write it down for you now – have you got a pen? And Mum says we'll have a pizza party when we're in. You're invited!

l4_0.t: We go to my grandparents' house every summer. It's a long journey, but I don't mind. The house was built three hundred years ago – the doors are so low that my dad always hits his head! There are no computers there, but it's warm and comfortable, and Grandma makes the best cakes.
It sounds lovely.

l4_1.t: Hi Ollie, it's Mum. I know you're going to football practice at six. Before you go, can you close all the windows and turn off the heating? It was on all day yesterday. I'll be home at the usual time, and there's food in the fridge for dinner, so you don't need to go to the shop. Thanks, love!

l4_2.t: Did your parents get the new sofa?
Yes, it came yesterday. I didn't like the colour at first – it's bright orange! But it's so comfortable. I fell asleep on it last night while I was watching a film.
Was it expensive?
Not really. It was in the sale. I really love it now.

l4_3.t: Welcome, everyone. Before you go to your rooms, I need to tell you a few things about the bathrooms. Boys use the ones downstairs and girls use the ones upstairs. Please don't stay in the shower for more than five minutes, so there's hot water for everyone. And take your towels back to your room – don't leave them on the floor. Oh, and dinner's at seven, but I'll tell you more about that later.

l4_4.t: My favourite place is a small room under the stairs. Dad keeps boxes in there, but there's space for a chair and a lamp. It hasn't got a window, so I can't see outside. My friends think it's strange, but nobody comes in there, and my little brothers can't find me. It's the only place in our house where I can read without any noise.

l5.t: Mum, there's so much to do before Grandpa's party tomorrow. Who's doing what?
Well, your dad wanted to clean the bathroom, but I've already done that. So he's going to tidy the garden. There are leaves everywhere, and people will sit outside if it's sunny.
Good idea. And Grandma? She can't do anything difficult.
She wants to help, so she's going to make her famous cakes. She'll be in the kitchen all afternoon.
What about Sam? He never helps!
Well, he has to this time. The dog has made the living room carpet really dirty, so Sam's going to clean it.
Ha! And Aunt Jo? Is she coming early?

Yes, she'll be here at two. I thought she could wash the curtains in the dining room, but there isn't time for them to dry. So she'll bring some chairs from her house and put them out in the garden and the living room.
And me?
Could you wash all the towels for the guests?
Mum! Can I do something more fun? What about the coloured lights? I could hang them up in the hall and around the front door.
OK, you're good at that. I'll do the towels myself.
Thanks, Mum!

l1_0.t: Hi Jess! I heard you moved. Are you still in that flat above the café?
No, we left in March. Mum wanted to buy a flat by the river, but it was too expensive.
So where are you now?
We're renting a house on Green Lane. It's got a garden, so we can finally get a cat!

l1_1.t: Is your new bedroom ready, Daniel?
Nearly. My cousin gave me his old desk and chair, and Mum made some curtains for me.
So you've got everything?
Not quite. The light in the ceiling isn't very bright, so I need a lamp for my desk. I'm going to buy one on Saturday.

l1_2.t: Hello, it's Mrs Carter. Our heating isn't working and the house is really cold. Could you come at half past eleven?
Sorry, I'm busy then. I've got another job at ten o'clock, but I could come before that. How about quarter to nine?
That's fine. My son leaves for school at half past eight, but I'll be at home.
Great. See you then.

l1_3.t: Is this your bedroom, Kai? The one with the big window?
No, that's my parents' room. Mine's at the end of the hall.
Oh, the one with the football posters?
That's my brother's. I'm in the small room with the bunk beds. My cousins sleep there with me when they visit.

l1_4.t: Hi, Mrs Lee. I've brought my sleeping bag and my pillow for tonight.
Great, Amy. Did you bring a towel? We haven't got many clean ones.
Yes, it's in my bag.
Good. Have you got everything else?
Oh no! My toothbrush is still in the bathroom at home.

l2.t: Hello, this is a message for the Wilson family. Welcome to Rose Cottage! I hope your journey was OK. I'm sorry I can't meet you today. The key isn't under the mat by the front door, like last year. I've put it in a small box next to the gate. The number to open the box is the same as the house number – twenty-two. The cottage has three bedrooms – two upstairs, and one small one downstairs, next to the bathroom. There are clean towels on every bed. It gets cold at night, even in summer, so you might need the heating. The switch isn't in the kitchen – it's in the garage, on the wall behind the door. If you need food, there's a shop in the village. It usually closes at six, but today's Sunday, so it closes at half past five. If you have any problems, please call me. My name's Mrs Penrose – that's P-E-N-R-O-S-E – and my phone number is on the fridge. Enjoy your stay!

l3.t: Hi Hoa! How was London? Were you there for two weeks?
We planned to stay for ten days, but Mum had to go back to work early, so it was only one week.
That's a shame. Where did you stay?

At my aunt's apartment. It only has two bedrooms. My cousin wanted me to share her room, but her bed is tiny. And the sofa in the living room was too short for me. So I slept in a little room next to the kitchen. That's usually where my aunt does her work.
Was there a good view? I know lots of apartments in London are near the river.

You can see the river from the kitchen window, but only a little. The kitchen's really modern too. But the best thing was the garden on the roof. There are lots of plants and a table, and we had breakfast up there every morning.
Amazing. Were there any problems?
Well, the lift was very slow, but it worked. The neighbours have a big dog, but it was always quiet. The worst thing was the shower – the hot water never lasted longer than two minutes!
Oh no! Did you take lots of pictures?
Hundreds! Come to my house after school and I'll show you. Mum wants to go back next summer, but we'll see.

l4_0.t: Dad, can I paint my bedroom this weekend? I'm bored of pink. I'd like green.
What about the carpet? It's very old. Shall we get a new one too?
No, the carpet's fine, and I love my furniture. It's just the walls. Please?
OK. Let's go and buy the paint tomorrow.

l4_1.t: We've got new neighbours next door. I was worried at first, because they've got three small kids. But they're really quiet! And yesterday they brought us a cake to say hello. They've invited us to their house for lunch on Saturday. Their garden's tiny, so we'll eat in the kitchen. They're lovely people.

l4_2.t: Lots of people think they need to spend money to keep their homes warm in winter. You don't need new heating or expensive carpets. Here's my best tip: when it gets dark, close your curtains. They stop the warm air from leaving through the windows. It's easy, and it's free!

l4_3.t: Are you having your birthday party at home, Leo?
I wanted to. Our living room's big enough, and Mum and Dad said they'd help. But my grandma's staying with us this month, and she isn't very well, so the house needs to be quiet.
Oh, I see.
So we're going to the bowling place in town instead.

l4_4.t: Hi Zoe, it's Kate. You know we moved last week? Well, I gave you the wrong address! It isn't fifteen Hill Street – it's fifty Hill Street. Five, zero. Please write it down before you send me the birthday card. I'll see you at school tomorrow. Bye!

l5.t: So how's the new house, Ryan? Does everyone like it?
Yes, it's great. Mum thought she'd love the garden most, but she's always in the kitchen now. It's twice as big as our old one, and it's got a huge cooker.
And your dad?
He's got a garage for the first time, so he spends all weekend in there repairing his old bike.
What about your sister? I'm sure she's in her bedroom all the time.
Not really – Amy's bedroom is quite small. But the bathroom has a really big bath, and she stays in there for hours! None of us can get in.
Ha! And your grandpa lives with you, doesn't he?
Yes. We thought he'd like the dining room, because he loves big family dinners. But actually he's always outside in the garden, growing vegetables.
And you? Is your bedroom your favourite?
It's nice, but my favourite room is the living room. We've got a huge sofa and a big TV, so I watch football there with my friends.
What's the hall like? My mum says the houses on your street have really big halls.
It's big, but it's just a hall! There's nowhere to sit.

l1_0.t: You look tired, Sara. Did you go running this morning?
Yes. Usually I run two kilometres around the park, but today I did five.
Wow! Are you training for the big race?
Yes, the ten-kilometre race in May. I've got two months to get ready!

l1_1.t: Shall we have lunch in the garden? It's sunny.
It's sunny, but it's only twelve degrees. Yesterday it was twenty-one!
Really? The radio said it would be eighteen today.
Well, the radio was wrong. Let's eat inside and go out later.

l1_2.t: Mum, I'm making pancakes for everyone. Is there any milk?
There's half a litre in the fridge. Is that enough?
The recipe says one litre for four people, but there are eight of us today with Grandma and Grandpa and the cousins.
So you need two litres. I'll go to the shop.

l1_3.t: Hurry up, Tom! Your swimming lesson starts at quarter past four.
No, Mum, they changed it. It's at half past four now.
Oh, OK. But it takes fifteen minutes to get there, and it's already quarter to four.
That's fine. We've got lots of time.

l1_4.t: Let's see how tall you are now, Ben. Stand still against the door for a moment.
Last year I was one metre forty-five.
Well, now you're one metre fifty-two! You've grown seven centimetres.
Great! I want to be one metre sixty, like my brother.

l2.t: Good afternoon, everyone. Next Saturday our school is having a charity walk to raise money for the town hospital. Last year the walk was eight kilometres, but this year it's longer – twelve kilometres. Don't worry, there'll be lots of stops! We'll meet at quarter to nine outside the railway station, not at school. The weather report says it will be warm – about twenty-four degrees – so please bring at least two litres of water. Half a litre isn't enough! Wear comfortable shoes and a hat. We'll stop for lunch after about six kilometres. We thought about having lunch at the café in the village, but it's too small for a hundred students. So we'll eat at a farm near the river, where you can buy sandwiches and drinks. We'll finish at about four o'clock, and your parents can collect you from the park. If you have any questions, please ask Mr Fletcher. That's F-L-E-T-C-H-E-R. He's organising the walk this year. And don't forget to collect your form from the school office this week.

l3.t: Hi Leo. Are you still doing the cycling race next month?
Yes! I'm really excited about it.
Is it fifty kilometres, like last year? My brother did that one.
That's the adults' race. Some of them do eighty kilometres! It's shorter for under-fifteens. We only do thirty kilometres – that's about eighteen miles.
That's still a long way. Are you training a lot?
I'd like to train every day, but I've got too much homework. Before, I only went out twice a week. Now I go three times – on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday.
Is your bike OK? It looks quite heavy.
It's about twelve kilos, which is fine. And I'm quite good on hills. My real problem is the heat. When it's more than thirty degrees, I feel terrible after a few minutes.
Why don't you train before school, when it's cooler? You could go out at half past six.
That's a good idea. I already drink lots of water, but that doesn't help much.
So when does the race start?
The adults start at half past nine, and we start forty-five minutes later, at quarter past ten. But I need to be there at eight o'clock to get my number.
I'll come and watch you!

l4_0.t: Mum, this recipe is from an American website. It says two cups of flour and one stick of butter. How many grams is that? Our scales only show grams and kilos!
Hmm, I'm not sure. Let me look on my phone.
Thanks. I've got all the eggs, and the oven's already at a hundred and eighty degrees.

l4_1.t: We drove eight hundred kilometres to the mountains. It took two days, which was really boring. The temperature was nearly thirty-five degrees every day – too hot for me. But on the last day we climbed to the top of a mountain, two thousand metres high. The view was amazing. I'll never forget it!

l4_2.t: It's been a lovely warm week, with temperatures of around twenty-two degrees. But get your coats ready! On Saturday and Sunday it'll only be ten or eleven degrees, and there'll be strong winds. The warm weather won't come back until next Wednesday.

l4_3.t: Look at this app. It counts how many steps I take and how many kilometres I walk every day. Yesterday I walked seven kilometres!
Cool. Does it tell you how many hours you sleep, too?
It can, but I don't use that. I just love seeing how far I've gone each day.

l4_4.t: Hi Jess, it's Mai. About the cinema tonight – the film still starts at seven, but let's not meet outside the cinema, because it's going to rain. Let's meet in the café opposite instead, at quarter to seven. I'll get there a few minutes early and buy the tickets. See you!

l5.t: How was Sports Day, Josh? Did your friends win anything?
Yes, lots! Ali won the three-kilometre run. He finished in eleven minutes – nearly a minute before everyone else.
Wonderful. Wasn't he in the eight hundred metres too?
He wanted to be, but you can only do two events, so he chose the relay race. His team came second.
And Hannah? She's very good at the long jump, isn't she?
She usually is, but this time she came third in that. She won the high jump, though – she jumped one metre forty!
Clever girl. And what about Kevin?
Kevin won the hundred metres. It took him only thirteen seconds. Everyone was cheering.
And your sister? Lucy's a good runner.
She hurt her leg last week, so she couldn't run. But she won the fifty-metre swimming race in the pool.
And you, Josh?
I wasn't fast enough for any of the races. But I won the ball throwing! I threw it thirty-five metres.
Well done, Josh! I'm very proud of you. Let's have some cake to celebrate.

l1_0.t: Dad, we need to buy flour for the birthday cake.
How much? There's about a hundred and fifty grams in the cupboard.
The recipe says two hundred and fifty grams for one cake. But I want to make two – one for home and one for school.
So you need five hundred grams. Let's buy a one-kilo bag.

l1_1.t: How long does the train to Brighton take, Mum? Is it an hour and a half, like last time?
No, we took the slow train last time. This one's much faster.
So about an hour?
Even less – forty-five minutes. We'll be there by ten.

l1_2.t: Is your new school near your house, Max?
Not really. My old school was only half a mile away, so I could walk.
And now?
It's two miles, so I cycle. My cousin's school is five miles away – he has to take the bus.

l1_3.t: What did you get at the market, Ana? Strawberries?
I wanted half a kilo, but they were all sold. And the apples didn't look very good.
So what's in the bag?
Bananas – two kilos! We can make banana bread this weekend.

l1_4.t: Is your swimming competition next Saturday, Jack? The fifteenth?
It was going to be, but they moved it. Now it's this Saturday, the eighth.
But today's Tuesday! That's only four days. Are you ready?
Nearly. I've got training today and on Thursday.

l2.t: Hi everyone. If you love food, why not join our cookery course for teenagers at the Riverside Centre? It starts next month, and it lasts for six weeks. Last year we had a four-week course, but everyone asked for more lessons! Classes are every Thursday, from half past four until six o'clock – that's an hour and a half each week. We can't have classes on Tuesdays, because another group uses the kitchen then. In the first lesson, you'll learn how to make pizza – the bread and everything! Then in week two you'll make soup, and later you'll try some cakes. Don't worry about measuring – we'll teach you how to weigh things in grams and kilos, and how to measure milk and water in litres. Please bring a plastic box so you can take your food home – you'll want to share it with your family! You don't need to bring any food; we buy all of it. Your teacher is Ms Bryant. That's B-R-Y-A-N-T. She works as a cook in a big hotel, so she really knows what she's doing. Call the centre or visit our website to book a place.

l3.t: Hi Nam! How was Scotland?
Brilliant, thanks! We drove all around the country for two weeks.
How far did you drive?
Dad said we'd do about five hundred miles, but we got lost twice! In the end it was about eight hundred miles.
Wow! That's more than a thousand kilometres.
Nearly thirteen hundred kilometres, Dad says.
Was it hot?
I thought it would be about twenty degrees, because it was July. But some days it was only twelve! It rained one day, but the rest of the time it was sunny.
Did you swim in any lakes?

Mum did, but the water was too cold for me! We visited a castle too, which was OK. But the best day was when we climbed Ben Nevis. It's thirteen hundred and forty-five metres high – the highest mountain in Britain!
Amazing! How long did it take?
The sign said three hours to the top, but it took us four and a half, because my little sister was slow. Then going down took another three hours, so we walked for seven and a half hours altogether.
You must have been tired! Did you take any photos?
I made a video at the top. Come to my house tomorrow and I'll show you!

l4_0.t: My cake was terrible! I put in two hundred grams of sugar, like the recipe said, and the oven was at a hundred and eighty degrees – exactly right. But then I went to watch TV and forgot about it. It was in the oven for an hour, not forty minutes. It was black!
Oh no!

l4_1.t: My new watch is great. It tells me the time and the date, of course, and even the temperature outside. But the best thing is when I go running – it shows my speed, so I know how many minutes it takes me to run a kilometre. It wasn't cheap. I saved my pocket money for a whole year!

l4_2.t: Right, everyone, listen please. Tomorrow's maths exam is an hour and a quarter long, and it's in this classroom as usual. You can't leave in the first thirty minutes. Bring a ruler, because some questions ask you to measure lines in centimetres. And all phones must be in your bags, switched off. Any questions?

l4_3.t: Well done, Lily! Twenty-five kilometres – that's the furthest you've ever cycled.
Thanks, Dad. It was fun, but my legs really hurt and I can't stop yawning. I just want to lie on the sofa.
Shall we go out for pizza to celebrate?
Maybe tomorrow. I need to go to bed!

l4_4.t: Today we're talking to Joe Banks, who has just walked from the north of Scotland to the south of England. That's more than a thousand kilometres! He wasn't fast – it took him nine weeks, walking about twenty kilometres a day. And Joe isn't a young sportsman. He's a seventy-year-old grandfather, and he did it to raise money for his local hospital.

l5.t: How's your science project going, Hana?
Good! We all had to measure something every day for a week. Kim wanted to measure the length of the playground, but that was too easy, so she weighed her cat every day.
Her cat? Did it get heavier?
No! It was four kilos every day.
Ha! What about Oliver?
He wanted to measure how far he walks in a day, but his phone broke. So he measured the big tree in his garden. It's eleven metres tall!
Wow. And Priya?
She put a big bottle in her garden and measured the rain. There was nearly two litres in one week!
That's a lot. What about Tom? He loves sport.
Yes – he ran a hundred metres every day and checked the time. On Monday it took him seventeen seconds, but by Friday it was only fifteen!
And you? Did you measure how many hours you sleep? You're always tired!
Dad! No. I checked the temperature in our classroom every morning and every afternoon. It was always about four degrees warmer after lunch.
Interesting! That's why everyone wants to sleep in the afternoon.

l1_0.t: Are you OK, Tina? You look sad.
I'm not sad, Dad. I'm just really tired. I went to bed very late because I was finishing my history project.
Are you still angry with your brother? He was very noisy last night.
No, that's fine. He said sorry this morning.

l1_1.t: How was the school trip to the zoo, Leo?
Brilliant! I thought the lions would be my favourite, but they slept all day. That was a bit boring.
What about the monkeys? They're always funny.
They were OK, but the best thing was the penguins. They were so cool – they swam really fast under the water.

l1_2.t: Did you get nice presents for your birthday, Ana?
Yes! My aunt gave me a book. It's interesting, but it's very long.
And your grandparents?
A watch. It's pretty, but I've already got one. My favourite was this soft toy from my little brother. He bought it with his own pocket money. Wasn't that sweet?

l1_3.t: You look happy, Kate! Did you go horse riding again on Saturday?
No, I've done that lots of times. I went surfing in the sea for the first time!
Wow! Was it difficult?
Really hard, but I stood up on the board twice! Next time I want to try climbing.

l1_4.t: Who's your new English teacher, Nga?
Mrs Brown. She's quite old, with short grey hair.
Is she the tall one with long red hair?
No, that's Miss Lane, the music teacher. Mrs Brown's quite small, and she's really kind.
And the young man with glasses?
That's Mr Park, the new art teacher.

l2.t: Hello, everyone. Next week is our school's first Kindness Week, and I'm really excited about it. We wanted to start on Monday, but there's a school trip that day, so we'll begin on Tuesday and finish on Saturday morning. The idea is simple: try to do one kind thing every day. It can be something small, like helping a friend with difficult homework, or saying something nice to someone who looks unhappy. When someone is kind to you, write a short thank-you message and put it in the message box. We were going to put the box in the canteen, but it's too noisy and busy there, so you'll find it next to the library door. Every class is also going to collect something for the children's hospital in town. They've got lots of toys already, but they need books, so please bring any old books you don't want.
