At the end of the week, the kindest class will win a special prize – a free trip to the cinema! Last year's prize was a pizza party, but we wanted something different this time. If you have any questions, please speak to Mr Dawson. That's D-A-W-S-O-N. Thank you!

l3.t: Hi Sophie! How was the camping trip?
Hi Nam. It was great, actually! I didn't think it would be. Before we left I was really worried, because I've never slept away from my family before.
Really? I thought you were excited about it.
Everyone else was excited. I just felt nervous.
So what was it like? Was the weather OK?
It was lovely and sunny all weekend. The tents were fine too – warm and dry. But the food was terrible! On the first night the pasta was cold, and on the second night they burned the sausages.
Poor you! Were you hungry?
A bit. Luckily my mum put some biscuits in my bag.
What did you do in the day?
On Saturday we walked up a hill. It was very high and I was tired at the top, but the view was beautiful. And on Sunday we swam in the lake. The water was so cold!
Which was your favourite?
Neither, really. The best thing was in the evening, when we all sat round the fire and sang songs. Mr Grant played the guitar, and it was so funny when he forgot the words.
Who was in your tent? Your friend Kim?
I wanted to be with Kim, but the teachers chose the groups. Kim was with Emma, and I was with a girl called Daisy. I didn't know her before, but she's really kind and now she's my friend.
That's lucky. Would you go again?
Definitely. Next summer the school is going on a trip to the mountains for a week. I was going to visit my cousins in August, but I'm going on the trip instead.
Cool!

l4_0.t: Did you see that new monster film at the weekend?
Yes! Everyone said it was really scary, but I wasn't afraid at all. It was nearly three hours, but it wasn't boring. Actually, I laughed all the way through – the monster was so silly!
Maybe I'll watch it, then.

l4_1.t: When the old man moved in next door, I was worried because Dad said he was a bit strange. But he's lovely! He always says hello, and he's teaching me to grow vegetables. He lives alone, but he isn't lonely – his family visit every weekend. And he's very quiet, much quieter than our old neighbours!

l4_2.t: Dad says you got your maths results today, Tom.
Yes. I got eighty-five per cent.
That's excellent! You worked so hard, and I'm really proud of you. You were worried, but you were wrong! I'm going to cook your favourite dinner tonight.
Thanks, Mum. Can I help?
No, you go and relax.

l4_3.t: How was Spain?
We had a great time, except for one thing. When we arrived at the airport, my bag wasn't there!
Oh no! Did you get it back?
Never. I had to buy new clothes. But the hotel was lovely and quiet, and it was sunny every day.

l4_4.t: Last year I nearly stopped my piano lessons. Practising every day was so boring, and the music was really difficult. But my teacher said, 'Just wait – it'll get easier.' She was right. Now I can play some of my favourite songs, and I'm really glad I didn't stop. I don't think I'll ever be famous, but I love it.

l5.t: So how was sports day, Ana? How did Kevin do in the running race?
He came second. We all thought he'd be sad, but he wasn't. He was really angry! He said another boy pushed him at the start.
Oh dear. And your teacher, Mrs Patel? She organised everything, didn't she?
Yes, she was busy all day. Everyone thought she'd be worried about the weather, but it was sunny, so that was fine. At the end she just sat down and said she was so tired she couldn't move.
Poor Mrs Patel. What about Lily? She's the fast one, isn't she?
She didn't run this year because she hurt her foot last week. She had to sit and watch all day. She said she was really bored.
And Josh? Did he eat all the cakes again?
Ha! He wasn't hungry for once. He won the long jump! He didn't think he could win, so he was really surprised. His face was so funny when they said his name.
And you? You must be sad that your team lost.
Not really. We lost, but I had so much fun with my friends. I was happy all day!
That's the most important thing.

l1_0.t: Did you enjoy your holiday in Italy, Marco?
It was great. The beaches were beautiful, but it was too hot to stay there for long.
Did you go to the theme park?
Yes, but we waited in terrible queues all day. The best part was the boat trip. We saw dolphins!

l1_1.t: Are you ready for your exam tomorrow, Bella? You look afraid.
Afraid? No, I'm fine – I've studied a lot. I'm just bored because I've read the same book all day.
Aren't you excited about the holidays after the exams?
Not yet! I need a break first. Shall we go for a walk?

l1_2.t: Is your sister coming to the party, Ben? I've never met her.
Yes, she'll be there. She's tall, with long fair hair.
Does she wear glasses like you?
No, she doesn't. She had short curly hair last year, but it's long now.

l1_3.t: Do you want to come to the zoo with us, Sam? They've got a new snake house.
Sure. I'm not afraid of snakes – I think they're cool.
Really? What about spiders? There are some big ones there.
They're fine too. Actually, it's dogs I don't like. A big dog bit me when I was small.

l1_4.t: I'm bored. What shall we do this afternoon? Shall we go swimming?
The pool's closed on Mondays.
Bowling, then?
It's too expensive. Let's play the new video game at my house. My brother says it's brilliant.
OK, great.

l2.t: Hello and welcome to Young Voices. This month we're starting a new writing competition called My Amazing Day. We want you to write about a special day in your life – maybe a day when you were very happy, very lucky, or even very afraid! The competition is for students aged eleven to fifteen. Last year it was only for students over twelve, but this year younger students can enter too. Your story must not be more than three hundred words. Please don't write more, because the judges won't read long stories! Now, the prizes. Last year the winner got a camera, but this year the first prize is a tablet, and there are books for the next five stories. The three best writers will come to our studio and read their stories on the radio. That will be on Thursday next month – not Tuesday, which is the day of our normal programme. Please send your stories to Mrs Penrose. That's P-E-N-R-O-S-E. Good luck, everyone!

l3.t: Hi Max. Why are you smiling so much?
You won't believe it, Lucy. Yesterday I met Jamie Blue!
The famous singer? No way! Where? At his concert?
No, I couldn't get tickets for that – they were too expensive. I was in a cafe near the railway station with my mum, and he walked in and sat at the next table!
Lucky you! What did you do?
At first I was too nervous to say anything. My hands were shaking. Mum said, 'Go on, talk to him!' But I couldn't.
So what happened?
He spoke to me first! He saw my T-shirt with his name on it and laughed. He said, 'Nice T-shirt!'
That's so funny! What was he like?
Really friendly. Much shorter than on TV, though. And he was quiet – not loud like in his videos.
Did you get a photo with him?
He was happy to do one, and there was nobody else in the cafe, but my phone battery was dead! And Mum's phone was at home. So he wrote his name in my school notebook instead.
That's still great. Are you going to take it to school and show everyone?
I'll show them a photo of it, but the notebook is staying in a safe place at home. I'm not going to use it for homework any more!
Ha! Good idea.

l4_0.t: I thought the science museum would be boring – my brother said it was. But it was really interesting! There were lots of things you could touch and try. We were there for five hours, but it felt like one. I want to go back with my family soon.

l4_1.t: What do you think of Nadia, the new girl?
Some people say she's unfriendly because she doesn't talk much. But I think she's just quiet.
She's good at maths, isn't she?
She's brilliant! She answered every difficult question in class today. I'm sure she'll be top of the class.

l4_2.t: Hi Leo, it's Danny. I'm really sorry about yesterday. I forgot about our tennis game, and you waited for me in the rain for an hour. I feel terrible. It was a bad thing to do, and I won't do it again. Please call me back – I hope you're not still angry.

l4_3.t: I'm so tired, Dad. We practised for three hours today!
Oh dear. Do you still want to be in the orchestra?
Of course! The music is so beautiful, and everyone's really friendly. I'm not even worried about the concert any more.
That's great.

l4_4.t: My grandad is seventy-eight, but he still goes on holiday to a new country every year. He's been to more than forty countries! People think he was rich or famous, but he was a bus driver. He just saved his money carefully. He only speaks English, but he says a smile works everywhere.

l5.t: Hoa, our English homework is about being afraid. Can I ask you about your family?
Sure. Let's start with my dad. He's big and strong, but he's afraid of flying! When we go on holiday, we always go by train.
Really? I thought he didn't like dogs.
No, he loves dogs – we've got two. My mum loves them too. What she really hates is insects. Even a small one in the kitchen makes her scream!
Ha! And your brother Minh?
He says he isn't afraid of anything. But he never swims in the sea now. Last summer he went too far out and couldn't swim back easily. Now he's afraid of deep water.
Poor Minh. What about your grandma?
Grandma's amazing. She climbs mountains, so she isn't afraid of high places at all. But she hates storms. When there's thunder, she hides under a blanket!
And you, Hoa?
Me? I was afraid of the dark when I was little, but not now. Now it's snakes. I saw one in our garden once – it was terrible!
Thanks, Hoa. That's really useful.

l1_0.t: Are you coming straight home after school, Josh?
No, Mum. I need to go to the library to borrow a book for my project. The bookshop doesn't have it.
I thought you had swimming today.
Not today – the pool's closed. It's on Thursday this week.

l1_1.t: Have you found your bag, Ruby?
Yes! I thought I left it in the cinema, but it wasn't there.
Did you go to the cafe after the film?
No, we went straight to the railway station. I left it on a seat there, and a man took it to the ticket office.

l1_2.t: Does your mum still work at the hospital, Anna?
No, she left last year. She works in an office in the city centre now.
Does she like it?
It's OK, but she misses the hospital. She'd like to work at the school near our house one day.

l1_3.t: Excuse me, I'm looking for the Grand Hotel. Is it near here?
Yes, it's not far. Go straight on and turn left at the post office.
Turn left at the post office. OK.
Then you'll see the museum. The hotel is opposite it, on the other side of the road.
Thanks very much.

l1_4.t: What shall we do on Saturday? We could visit the castle.
We went there last month. What about the football match at the stadium?
All the tickets have gone. But your sister wants to see the new play at the theatre.
OK, let's do that. I'll book the tickets online.

l2.t: OK, everyone, listen carefully, please. Next week we're going on our trip to the Bramley Chocolate Factory. We planned to go on Tuesday, but the factory is closed that day, so we're going on Thursday instead. Please meet at the main entrance of the school, not in the car park like last time, because there are builders working there. The bus leaves at quarter past eight, so please arrive by eight o'clock. The journey takes about an hour. At the factory, you'll see how they make chocolate, and you can try some, too! You don't need to bring lunch – the factory cafe will give us sandwiches. But you might want to bring some money for the shop. They sell boxes of chocolates at very good prices. Our guide will be Mrs Fenwick. That's F-E-N-W-I-C-K. She's worked at the factory for thirty years, so she can answer all your questions. We'll be back at school at about half past three. Any questions?

l3.t: Hi Leah. How was your weekend in London?

Brilliant, thanks, Tom. Dad wanted to stay in a big hotel, but they were all too expensive. So we stayed in a small guest-house near the railway station. It wasn't very modern, but the owner was really friendly.
What did you visit first?
Well, Mum wanted to see the cathedral, but there was a long queue outside the entrance, so we went to the Science Museum instead. It was amazing – we spent four hours there!
Did you go to the theatre? I know you love musicals.
We wanted to, but the tickets cost too much. We went to the cinema in the evening instead.
What did you think of London?
It's very exciting, and some things are cheaper than I thought. But it's so busy! There were people everywhere, and the underground trains were really full. I prefer our town – it's quieter.
Did you go shopping?

I went to a big department store on Oxford Street. I wanted some trainers, but they didn't have my size. So I bought a book about London in a little bookshop. I didn't need a map – the guest-house gave us a free one.
Cool. Would you go back?
Yes! Next time I want to see a football match at Wembley Stadium. My dad says we can go for my birthday in May.

l4_0.t: My new school is much bigger than my old one. The classrooms are modern, with a computer on every desk, which is nice. There's a swimming pool too, but we only use it in the summer. The best thing for me is the library. It's huge, with thousands of books and comfortable sofas. I spend every lunchtime there.

l4_1.t: Mum, can I go to the newsagent's?
What for? If it's sweets, the answer's no.
No! It's Grandma's birthday tomorrow and I haven't got a card for her.
Oh, good idea. And can you get me a newspaper while you're there?
OK.

l4_2.t: The big red building on River Street was a shoe factory for over a hundred years. When it closed, nobody used it for a long time. Some people wanted to make it into flats, but the town decided to turn it into a museum about the history of the town. It opened last year, and there's a nice little cafe next door too.

l4_3.t: How was the school disco last night, Amy?
Well, the music was great, and the hall wasn't too crowded. But it started at seven and finished at half past eight!
Only an hour and a half?
Yes. We were just starting to have fun when they turned the lights on.

l4_4.t: Good evening, shoppers. The supermarket will close in fifteen minutes, at ten o'clock. Please take your shopping to the checkouts now. Today's special prices on fruit have now finished, but there will be more great prices tomorrow. We'll open again at seven tomorrow morning. Thank you for shopping with us.

l5.t: Kevin, tell me about everyone's jobs. I can never remember! Your mum still works at the bank, doesn't she?
Not any more, Grandma. She left the bank last year. She works at the hospital now. She's a nurse again, like when she was younger.
Oh, that's good. And your dad? Is he still a police officer?
No, he left the police station two years ago because he hurt his back. Now he works at the post office in town. He likes it because he meets lots of people.
And Aunt Julia? She loves books.
Yes, she wanted to open a bookshop, but it was too expensive. So she works in a big hotel near the sea. She's the manager there now!
Goodness! And your cousin Sam? He's so sporty.
He teaches swimming at the new sports centre. He loves it, and the children love him.
And your sister Emma? Is she still at university?
She finished university last summer. Now she works at a bank in London. Mum says she's the clever one in the family!
Well, I'm very proud of all of you.

l1_0.t: Sam, I'll be at the bank until three. Shall we meet outside it?
It's going to rain, Mum. Can we meet inside somewhere? What about the bookshop?
It's closed this week. They're painting it. Let's meet in the cafe next to it.
OK, see you there at three.

l1_1.t: Which floor is your new flat on, Nina?
The ninth. Our old flat was on the second floor, so it's very different.
Wow. Do you take the lift?
Usually. But my friend Lucy lives on the fifth floor of the same building, so sometimes I walk down to her flat.

l1_2.t: Have you seen that big new building in the town centre? Is it a hotel?
That's what everyone thought. But my dad says it's going to be a cinema, with eight screens.
Great! I hoped it would be a swimming pool, but a cinema's good too.
It opens in June.

l1_3.t: Did you go to the castle with your grandparents yesterday, Tim?
We wanted to, but it was closed. So we went to the museum instead.
Was it good?
Yes, really interesting. Then Grandma wanted to see the old church, but we were too tired, so we went home.

l1_4.t: Are you going swimming at the sports centre on Saturday, Jess?
Not this week – I've got a cold. But I'm going to play badminton there with my dad.
I thought you wanted to try the climbing wall.
I do, but you have to be fourteen. Next year!

l2.t: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Bradley Castle. My name's Paul and I'm your guide today. This castle is very old. People started building it in eleven fifty, and it took about forty years to finish. Lots of visitors think it's much newer, because the outside is so clean! We'll begin our tour in the great hall, and then we'll visit the kitchens. After that, you can climb the tower. There are ninety-five steps – I know because I count them every day! Please be careful, because they're quite small. From the top you can see the cathedral and the university buildings in the city. You're welcome to take photos everywhere except the library. The old books there don't like the light from cameras. If you want to buy a present, the gift shop isn't near the entrance where you came in. It's next to the exit, at the end of the tour. And if you're hungry, the castle cafe is open until half past four today. It usually closes at five, but there's a special event this evening. OK, follow me, please!

l3.t: Hi Oliver. How was your week of work experience?
Really good, thanks, Grace. I was at a big company in the city centre. Their offices are in a really tall building – it's got thirty floors!
Wow. Were you at the top?
No, the company is on the twenty-second floor. I went up in the lift every morning. On the first day it was so fast I felt a bit sick!
Ha! So what did you do? Did you just make coffee?
My brother said I'd only make tea and coffee all week, but I didn't make any! I helped to make a website for a new hotel. It was really interesting.
That's cool. Were the people nice?
Very friendly. My manager, Lisa, was great. She explained everything clearly. The only problem was lunch. There's a cafe on the ground floor, and it's never too busy, but it was really expensive.
So what did you do?
After the first day, I took sandwiches from home and ate them in the park next to the cathedral. It was lovely and quiet there.
Would you like to work in an office one day?
I'm not sure. I loved the work, but I didn't like sitting down all day. I like moving around.
So what are you going to do?
Well, I'd like to study computers at university or college. Then maybe I can work from home!

l4_0.t: The old cinema in our town is closing next month. Lots of people say it's sad, but I don't really agree. It was always cold inside, and the seats were terrible. A new cinema is opening in the shopping centre, with bigger screens and better seats. I'm actually quite happy about it.

l4_1.t: Dad, did you know our new library was a hospital before?
Really? I thought it was an old school.
No, the school was on the other side of the road. My teacher told us the building was a hospital for a hundred years.
How interesting! I didn't know that.

l4_2.t: Hello, this is Mrs Gold. I've got a room at your hotel for the twelfth and thirteenth of July. I'm afraid I can't come then. Could I come a week later instead – the nineteenth and twentieth? I'd like the same double room with breakfast, please. Please call me back on 07700 900 456. Thank you.

l4_3.t: Have you been to the new sports centre yet?
Yes, on Saturday. It's much better than the old one – the gym is brilliant.
Isn't the swimming pool quite small?
No, it's the same size as before. And it's only five minutes from my house, so I'm going to go every week.

l4_4.t: OK, everyone, you can now look around the museum on your own. Please don't go into the shop – we'll visit it together at the end. At two o'clock, meet me at the main entrance, next to the big dinosaur. Don't go to the exit, because it's on the other side of the building and our bus is waiting at the front.

l5.t: How was your day in the city, Max? I'm sorry I had to work.
It was great, Mum. We all went to different places. Dad went to the university. He wanted to see the building where he studied.
Oh, I thought he wanted to go to the cathedral.
He did, but there was a wedding, so he couldn't go in. So he went to the university and met an old friend there.
And Grandpa? He loves old cars.
Yes! He went to the car factory just outside the city. They have tours on Saturdays. He said it was brilliant.
What about Uncle Peter?
He went to the theatre in the afternoon to see a play. He wanted me to go with him, but I said no. Plays are boring!
And Ruby? Did she go shopping?
She wanted to go to the big department store, but everything there is too expensive. So she went to her friend's college to see an art show. Her friend's paintings were in it.
That's nice. And Josh? Did he go with you?
Yes. We went to the museum together – there's a new dinosaur room. Josh wanted to go to the teen disco in the evening too, but we were too tired!

l1_0.t: Did you have a good holiday, Ben? Did you go to the island again?
No, we went there last year. Dad wanted to go to the mountains this time, but Mum said it would be too cold.
So where did you go?
We stayed in a little wooden house next to a lake. We went swimming every day. It was great!

l1_1.t: How shall we get to Grandma's village on Saturday? Shall we go by bike?
It's twenty kilometres – that's too far! The bus goes there, but only twice a day.
What about the train? They've opened a new railway station in the village.
Really? Great, let's take the train then. It's much quicker.

l1_2.t: Dad, guess what I saw in the forest this morning!
A squirrel? There are lots of them in the trees there.
No, it was bigger than that, and it was sitting on a branch. It was an owl! It looked at me with its big yellow eyes.
Wow, you were lucky. I've only ever seen deer in that forest.

l1_3.t: Let's have our picnic on the beach.
It's too windy there today. We'll get sand in our sandwiches!
OK. What about the top of the hill? There's a great view from there.
It's a long walk and I'm hungry now. Let's sit under that big tree by the river.
Fine. At least it's not too sunny there.

l1_4.t: Excuse me, when's the next boat to the island?
The nine o'clock boat has just left, I'm afraid. The next one usually goes at quarter past ten, but it's late today because of the weather.
Oh. So when does it leave?
At half past eleven. You can wait in the café over there.

l2.t: OK, everyone, listen carefully, please. Next Thursday we're going on our countryside day at Brook Farm. The farm is about an hour from here, so the bus will leave school at quarter to nine. Please don't be late! When we arrive, our first activity is a walk. We won't climb the hill behind the farm, because it's too steep and the path isn't safe. Instead, we'll walk through the wood down to the river, and you can look for birds and insects there. After that, we'll go back to the farm. There are lots of cows and sheep, but they live in the big fields, so we won't get close to them. You're going to help feed the goats. They're very friendly, but they eat everything, so be careful with your bags! The farm is very muddy at this time of year, so everyone must wear boots. Trainers are no good. You don't need to bring lunch, because the farm café is giving us soup and bread. The farmer will show us around. His name's Mr Dunmore. That's D-U-N-M-O-R-E. He has lived on the farm all his life, so please ask him lots of questions!

l3.t: Hi Daniel! How was your cycling trip with your dad?
Brilliant, thanks, Maya. We rode all the way along the river from our town to the sea. We planned to do it in two days, but it took three.
Why? Did you get lost?
No, the path next to the river is easy to follow. And our bikes were fine too. But on the first day it rained all afternoon, so we stopped early.
Oh no! Where did you sleep?
The first night we stayed in a small hotel in a village. It was lovely and warm. Then on the second night we put up our tent at a campsite by a lake.
Didn't Dad's friend live near there? You told me you might stay with him.
Yes, but he was on holiday, so we didn't see him.
So what was the best part? Swimming in the sea at the end?

The water was too cold for swimming, actually! And the ride through the forest was nice, but there were lots of insects. The best thing was the old railway bridge over the river. You can see the whole valley from the top. It was amazing.
It sounds great. I'd love to do that trip.
You should! I want to try something harder next summer. Dad and I are going to cycle in the mountains in Wales.
Wow. Rather you than me!

l4_0.t: Are you ready, Zoe? The weather's perfect for walking up the mountain today.
I know, Dad, and I usually love walking. But I fell over on the path by the river yesterday, and my foot still hurts a lot.
Oh dear. Then let's just walk along the lake today. It's flat there.
OK, thanks.

l4_1.t: Hi Felix, it's Kevin. You know we're going camping at the lake this weekend with my uncle? Well, I've got everything – the tent, the sleeping bags and the food – but I can't find my torch anywhere. Could I use yours? I can come and get it from your house tonight. We're still meeting at the bus station at ten tomorrow. Call me back!

l4_2.t: So, did you enjoy staying with your grandma in her village?
Yes! Before I went, I thought it would be really boring. But it's beautiful – there are old stone houses, a little river and fields of flowers everywhere.
Isn't it a long way from the city, though?
Only an hour by bus. And there's a great café there too!

l4_3.t: On Friday our class is going to Sandy Bay. I know some of you want to swim, but it's not a holiday – we're going to study the small animals and fish that live in the rock pools on the beach. Another class is going to clean the beach the week after, and you can help them if you want. Remember to bring a notebook and a pencil.

l4_4.t: Last Saturday I spent the day on my cousin's farm. I thought farmers just drove tractors around the fields all day! But we started at six o'clock, and we fed the animals, cleaned the barn and repaired a fence. The horses were big, but they were really gentle. By the evening I was so tired – I can't believe my cousin does that every day!

l5.t: So, Leo, did you hear about everyone's holidays today at school?
Yes! Ryan had the most exciting one. His parents took him to Brazil, and they spent a week in the rainforest. He saw monkeys and huge butterflies.
Lucky Ryan! What about Chloe? Did she go to the beach again?
She wanted to, but her parents chose somewhere different this year. They took a boat to a small island in Scotland. There were no cars at all!
Sounds peaceful. And Minh? He always goes camping, doesn't he?
Not this time. He went with his dad to climb a mountain in Wales. It took them six hours to get to the top!
Wow. What about Sara?
Sara stayed at her aunt's farm. She looked after the chickens and rode a horse every day.
She loves animals, doesn't she? And Jake? I thought his family had a holiday house by a lake.
They sold it last year. This summer they hired a boat and travelled along a canal for a week. He said it was really slow, but fun.
Everyone had such different holidays!

l1_0.t: These holiday photos are great, Anna. Is this one of the sea your favourite?
It's OK, but the colours aren't very good. I prefer this one of the forest in the snow. It's my best photo, I think.
And what about the field of flowers?
That's pretty, but my dad took that one, and I still like the forest more.

l1_1.t: Have you got everything for the walk, Sam? Have you got the map?
Yes, it's in my bag. And the tent's in the car.
But where's your jacket? It's going to be cold at the top of the hill.
Oh no! It's still hanging behind the door at home.

l1_2.t: Excuse me, how far is it to Ashby village?
Along the road, it's about eight kilometres. But if you take the path across the fields, it's only three.
What about the path by the river?
That one's five kilometres, and it's very wet at the moment.
Then we'll go across the fields. Thanks!

l1_3.t: Shall we take a boat out on the lake on Saturday afternoon?
Dad says it's going to be too windy for boats this weekend.
Oh. What about horse riding? The farm near the village has horses.
It's closed on Saturdays. Let's go fishing in the river with Grandad. He's got lots of rods.
OK, good idea!

l1_4.t: Is the campsite in the forest again, like last year?
No, this one's by the sea. You can walk straight from the tents onto the beach.
Oh. I wanted to go to that one at the bottom of the mountain.
Maybe next year. You'll love this one, I promise.

l2.t: Good morning and welcome to the Valley Steam Railway! This railway is more than a hundred years old, and today you're going to travel on one of our old steam trains. The train goes up the valley next to the river and an old canal, and stops at a little village at the end of the line. The journey takes forty-five minutes. Some people think it takes an hour, but it's much quicker than that! The best views are on the left side of the train. From there you can see the river, the forest and, on a clear day, the mountains. On the right side there's just a hill, so it isn't very interesting. When you arrive, you'll be in the village of Cardale. That's C-A-R-D-A-L-E. There's a lovely café there, next to the old church, and you can go for a walk by the lake. Please don't miss the last train back. It leaves at quarter past five. There's another train at half past three if you're tired. If you haven't bought your tickets yet, they're twelve pounds for adults and six pounds for children. Children under three travel free. Enjoy your day!

l3.t: Grandad, for my homework I have to ask someone about their childhood. Where did you grow up?
In a small village by the sea, Olivia. My parents had a farm on the hill above the beach.
Did you go to school by bus?
There wasn't a bus! And I didn't have a bike until I was fifteen. I walked across the fields every day – it took forty minutes.
Wow. What did you do after school? Did you play football?
Sometimes at the weekend. But after school I had to help my father with the cows and sheep. My friends went fishing, but I never had time.
Is the village still the same?
It's about the same size, but it's very different. Now it's full of visitors in the summer. They come for the beach and the walks along the cliffs. There are lots of cafés and gift shops.
Do you miss living there?
Sometimes. I see my old friends on the phone, and I can visit the sea any time. But I miss the quiet. At night you could only hear the sea and the wind. In the city there's always noise.
I'd love to see it.
Then let's go together next summer. I'll show you the farm and the path I walked to school.
Great!

l4_0.t: How was your walk in the hills on Sunday, Jack?
The views were lovely, and twelve kilometres was just right for me – not too hard. But the path was so busy! There were hundreds of people. It was like walking through the city centre on a Saturday.
Oh, that's a shame. Go on a weekday next time!

l4_1.t: Lily, I'm afraid we can't go to the campsite by the lake next week.
Why not? Is it going to rain?
No, the weather looks fine, and the car's ready. But I called them this morning and they're completely full. So I've booked a little cottage in a village by the river instead.
That sounds nice too!

l4_2.t: Yesterday our class had a forest school day in the wood behind our school. We learned how to make a small fire safely, but it was really smoky. Some people climbed trees, but I'm afraid of heights, so I didn't. My favourite thing was building a little house out of branches and leaves with my friends. We all sat inside it and ate our lunch!

l4_3.t: Good afternoon. This train is going to Seaton. The next station is Hilltop. Passengers for Bridgetown, please get off at Hilltop and change to the small train on platform two, because there is work on the railway line today. Passengers for Seaton, please stay on this train. The café is now open at the front of the train. Thank you.

l4_4.t: My uncle works as a ranger in the mountains. He looks after the paths and helps walkers who get lost. People think it must be lonely, but he meets lots of visitors every day. Sometimes he has to go out in snow or storms, but he's always very careful. I'd love to have a job like that when I'm older – working outside every day sounds perfect.

l5.t: Mum, my teacher wants us to write about our day out last Sunday. Can you help me remember what everyone liked best?
Of course, Jess. Let's start with your dad. He liked the lake, didn't he?
He said it was pretty, but he didn't stop talking about the river. He saw people fishing there and now he wants to buy a fishing rod!
That's true! And Grandma loved the castle.
She said it was too cold inside. Her favourite place was the village – she loved the old houses and the tea shop.
Yes, she had three cakes there! What about Sam?
Sam's favourite was the old steam train. He talked about the railway all the way home.
Of course. And Aunt Lily? She's always going on about the beach.
We didn't go to the beach this time. She liked the forest best, because she saw a woodpecker and lots of other birds.
And you, Jess?
I loved walking up the hill. From the top you could see the whole valley and the sea far away. It was the best part of the day.

l1_0.t: Shall we meet at the station before the film?
It's always so crowded there on Saturdays. What about the park?
It's too far from the cinema. Let's meet in the square, next to the fountain.
OK. See you there at two o'clock.

l1_1.t: You're early today, Mia! Did you come on the underground?
No, the underground's closed this week.
So did you get the bus?
I usually do, but it was full this morning. So my mum drove me here on her way to work.

l1_2.t: Have you been to the new café yet? Is it the one near the bridge?
No, that's the old one. The new one's on the corner of Mill Street and Queen Street.
Opposite the market?
No, the market's further down the road. It's next to the bookshop.

l1_3.t: So what do you want to do in the city tomorrow, Leo?
I really want to go to the zoo. But it doesn't open until eleven.
Then let's go to the market first. It's best early in the morning.
OK. And after the zoo we can have a picnic in the park.

l1_4.t: How much did you pay at the car park in town?
Six pounds! It's two pounds an hour, and I was there for three hours.
That's expensive.
I know. My sister only paid four pounds yesterday, but she stayed for two hours.

l2.t: Right, everyone, here's the information about next Friday's trip to the city. Please don't come to the classroom in the morning. We'll meet in the school playground at eight o'clock, and then we'll walk together to the station. Our train leaves at twenty past nine, and it takes about an hour. Don't be late, because we can't wait for anyone! In the morning we're going to visit the City Museum. It's in the main square, so it's only a short walk from the station. At lunchtime we won't go to a café, because they're too expensive. Bring a packed lunch, and we'll eat it in Tolland Park. That's T-O-L-L-A-N-D. There's a big playground there too, if you want to play after lunch. In the afternoon we were going to visit the market, but it's closed on Fridays, so we're going to the zoo instead. Tickets for students usually cost twelve pounds, but we have a special school price, so please bring eight pounds. You can bring a little extra money for the zoo shop if you want. We'll be back at school at about half past five.

l3.t: Ben, Grandma's plane lands at half past three tomorrow. Dad can't drive us to the airport.
Why not? Does he have to work?
No, he's free tomorrow. But there's something wrong with the car, so it's at the garage until Friday.
Oh. So shall we get a taxi?
That's too expensive. There's a bus, but it goes on the motorway and there's always a lot of traffic. Let's take the underground. It goes straight to the airport.
Good idea. Where are we meeting Grandma? At the information desk?
It's always busy there. She said she'll wait for us next to the café, just after you come out of arrivals.
OK. What are we going to do with her after that? She hasn't been to our city for five years.
I know! Lots of things have changed. I want to show her the new bridge over the river first. It looks amazing at night with all the lights.
And we can take her to the market on Saturday. And maybe the zoo – she loves animals.
Great. So, the journey on the underground takes about forty minutes. I think we should leave at one o'clock.
That's much too early! We'll have to wait for ages. Let's leave at half past one.
Hmm, the station is quite a long walk from here. Let's say two o'clock, then. That gives us enough time.
OK, two o'clock.

l4_0.t: Did you go to the new playground in the park, Tom?
Yes, it's only five minutes from here, and it's really big. But it's all swings and little slides. It's great for kids like my sister, but there's nothing for people my age.
Well, they're building a skate park next year.

l4_1.t: Hi Grace, it's Ana. I'm on the bus, but there's been an accident at the big roundabout, and the traffic isn't moving at all. I'm still coming, and I'll meet you outside the cinema like we said. But I think I'll be about twenty minutes late. Sorry! Can you buy the tickets? I'll give you the money.

l4_2.t: Do you like living in the city now, Nora?

Yes, much more than I expected. The shops are great, but I don't have much money! The best thing is the transport. There's a bus stop outside my flat and the underground is just round the corner, so I can go anywhere on my own.
Lucky you!

l4_3.t: And now the traffic news. The motorway to the airport is closed this morning after a lorry broke down near the petrol station at junction four. If you're going to the airport, please don't use the motorway. Take the old road through the town centre instead – it's slower, but it's moving. The bridge over the river is open again after yesterday's problems.

l4_4.t: Excuse me, is the bus station near here?
Yes, it's not far. Go straight on to the crossroads, then turn right. Cross the road at the crossing next to the bank, and the bus station is on your left, opposite the market.
Thanks very much.
You're welcome.

l5.t: Dad, for my project I have to write about five people and where they work in our town. Can you help me?
Sure. What about your cousin Sam? He works at the car park in town, doesn't he?
He did last year, but now he works at the petrol station on the corner of Station Road. He says it's more interesting.
OK. And our neighbour, Mr Lee? He's a train driver, isn't he?
No, Dad! That was his brother. Mr Lee works at the airport. He checks people's bags.
Ah, yes. What about Nina from your swimming club?
Her parents have a fruit stall in the market, and she helps them every Saturday morning.
Good. And Oliver? Isn't he a gardener in the park?
He was, but now he looks after the animals at the zoo. He loves it, especially the penguins.
And who's the last one?
Aunt Joy. She works in the ticket office at the bus station. She knows the times of every bus in town!
That's five. Well done!

l1_0.t: Ali, where's your school bag?
Oh no! I had it when I was waiting at the bus stop.
Did you leave it in the shop when you bought your drink?
No, I remember carrying it out of the shop. I put it on the seat next to me on the bus... and I forgot it there!
Let's phone the bus station.

l1_1.t: Excuse me, how do I get to the zoo, please?
Go straight over the roundabout – don't turn left there, that's the road to the motorway. Then you come to the crossroads.
Do I turn right there?
No, that goes to the station. Go straight on and cross the bridge. The zoo is just on the other side of the river.

l1_2.t: Dad, I'm going to the market. Do we need any strawberries?
No, Grandma brought some yesterday. Can you get some cheese? There's only a little bit left.
Sure. And what about flowers for Mum's birthday?
I've already bought them. They're hidden in the garage!

l1_3.t: Excuse me, has the ten past four train to Bristol left yet?
No, it's running late today, I'm afraid. It'll leave at about twenty to five.
Oh dear. Is the ten past five train late too?
No, that one's on time. But the twenty to five will get you there first.
OK, I'll wait for that one, then.

l1_4.t: Does your aunt still live in the city centre?
No, she moved last month. She wanted a house near the park, but they were all too expensive.
So where is she now?
She's got a flat on the corner of a street near the airport. She works there, so it's perfect for her.

l2.t: Good morning! Here's some news about Car-Free Sunday. On Sunday the fourteenth of June, there will be no cars in the city centre from ten in the morning until six in the evening. Last year it was on the seventh, but this year it's a week later. So how can you get around? Well, you can borrow a bike for free! The bikes will be in Kingsley Square. That's K-I-N-G-S-L-E-Y. There'll be lots of things to do. Children can play games in the streets, and there's a big market in the main square. My favourite part is the live music. Bands will play on the bridge over the river all afternoon, so you can listen while you look at the boats. If you're coming into the city by car, you can't drive into the centre. Please don't leave your car at the station, because the car park there will be full. Use the big car park behind the hospital instead, and then take a free bus into town. And if you prefer the underground, tickets will only cost one pound all day. Usually they're three pounds, so that's a great price!

l3.t: Hi Tom. I heard you're moving. Is it because of your dad's new job?
No, Dad still works in the same office. It's because our flat's too small now that my baby sister's here. We need another bedroom.
So where's the new flat?
It's on the tenth floor of a building near the river. From my bedroom window I can see the bridge and the boats. It's amazing, especially at night.
Is your bedroom bigger?
Actually, it's a bit smaller than my old one. But I don't mind. The kitchen's huge – Mum loves it.
What's the area like?
There's a big market just across the street. You can buy everything there. There was a playground too, but they closed it last year. And the underground station is quite far – about fifteen minutes.
How will you get to school? Will you take the bus?
I thought I'd have to. But it's only a ten-minute walk, along the river and across the square. My bike's too old, so I'll walk.
Can I come and see it?
Of course! We're moving on Saturday, so everything will be in boxes. Come on Sunday afternoon.
Great. See you then!

l4_0.t: Our class trip to the city was great. In the morning we went on a boat on the river, but it was raining, so we couldn't see much. Then we went to the market, but I didn't have much money. The best part was the tower in the main square. We went up to the top in a lift, and you could see every street and park in the city. Brilliant!

l4_1.t: Hello, I took one of your taxis from the airport to the city centre this morning. The journey was fine and the price was OK. But when I got to my hotel, I realised my phone wasn't in my pocket. I think it's on the back seat of the taxi. It's a black phone in a red case. Can you check, please?

l4_2.t: Have you seen the new roundabout at the end of Station Road? I think it's really ugly.
It isn't beautiful, I know. But before, there were traffic lights there and the cars waited for ages. Now the traffic moves much faster. My bus gets to school ten minutes earlier.
Maybe. But I'm scared to cycle round it.

l4_3.t: OK, everyone, I've got your tickets, so you can go in now. You can walk around in your groups and have lunch whenever you're hungry. But please be back here at the main entrance at two o'clock, because the bus is leaving at quarter past. Don't be late! And if you want to go to the zoo shop, do it before two.

l4_4.t: Every morning I take the underground to school. It takes forty minutes, which sounds like a long time, but I don't mind at all. I always get a seat, so I listen to music or read a book. My mum drives to work and she gets angry in the traffic, but I'm always calm when I arrive at school. It's my favourite part of the day!

l5.t: Josh, have you finished your photo for the 'My City' competition?
Yes! What did you choose, Hannah? The playground in the park? You were taking pictures there last week.
Those weren't very good. In the end I took one of the bridge at night, with all the lights in the river.
Nice. Mine's of the market. I took it early in the morning when the people were putting out the fruit and vegetables.
I love that! What about Mia? I think she wanted to photograph the bus station.
She went there, but it was too busy. So she went down into the underground and took a photo of a train coming into the station. It's really good.
And our teacher, Mr Brown, is entering too, isn't he?
Yes. He took a photo of the old square with the clock tower. It's in black and white.
My brother's entering too. He wanted to take a photo of the big roundabout with the flowers, but Mum said it was too dangerous.
So what did he do?
He went to the airport with Dad and took a photo of the planes taking off. He's sure he'll win!

l1_0.t: Dad, are we going to the library first? I need to give back my books.
We can't. The library doesn't open until ten on Saturdays.
Oh. What about the post office? You wanted to send Grandma's parcel.
That can wait until later. Let's go to the bank first – I need to get some money.
OK.

l1_1.t: Don't forget your dentist appointment this afternoon, Tom.
It's at three o'clock, isn't it?
It was, but they phoned this morning and changed it to half past four.
Half past four? But I've got football at the sports centre until four.
That's fine. The dentist is only five minutes from the sports centre.

l1_2.t: How was your school trip to London, Ali?
Great! We wanted to see a show at the theatre, but there wasn't one in the afternoon.
Oh no. So what did you do?
We went to the Natural History Museum instead. The dinosaurs were amazing! Some students wanted to go to the cinema after that, but our teacher said there wasn't time.

l1_3.t: Shall we meet at the café by the station on Sunday?
It's closed on Sundays. What about outside the Grand Hotel on King Street?
Hmm, I'm not sure where that is. Let's meet at the tourist information centre – it's in the main square.
OK, everyone knows where that is. See you there at ten.

l1_4.t: Mum, why are we taking the bus today? Where's the car?
It's at the garage. The mechanic is repairing it.
Is it the window again? It wouldn't close last week.
No, Dad fixed that. This time one of the lights at the front is broken.
What about the tyres?
They're fine. The mechanic checked them.

l2.t: Hello, and welcome to Radio Greenfield. I've got some good news for sports fans today. The new Greenfield Sports Centre is finally ready! We thought it would open this Friday, but the builders needed a little more time, so the big opening day is now Saturday. There'll be free activities all day, so come along. Now, prices. For adults, a swim costs five pounds, but if you're under sixteen, it's only three pounds. That's a great price for such a beautiful pool. And there's lots more to do as well as swimming. There are four tennis courts outside, but the most exciting thing is new for our town – a climbing wall! It's twelve metres high, and there are lessons for beginners every afternoon. After your sport, you can relax in the café on the first floor. It opens at nine in the morning and closes at eight in the evening, so there's lots of time for a drink and a snack. The manager of the sports centre is Mrs Dobson. That's D-O-B-S-O-N. If you have any questions, you can email her through the sports centre website. See you there!

l3.t: Hi Lily! How was your holiday in Italy?
Brilliant, thanks, Sam. We stayed in a hotel for a week.
Was it by the sea? You said you wanted a hotel near the beach.
We did, but all the hotels by the beach were full. So we stayed in the centre of the town. That was OK, because the beach was only ten minutes away by bus.
Was the hotel nice?
Our rooms were quite small, and the food in the restaurant was nothing special. But there was a swimming pool on the roof! That was the best thing. I swam there every morning before breakfast.
Lucky you! Did everything go well? Last year your car broke down, didn't it?

Yes, but not this time! On the first day I thought I'd lost my passport, but it was in Mum's bag. The real problem was my brother. He broke a tooth on a hard sweet, so we had to find a dentist. We spent the whole morning there.
Poor him! How did you know what to do in the town? Did you have a guidebook?

We forgot it at home! And the woman at the hotel reception was always too busy to help. So we went to the tourist information centre. A man there gave us free maps and told us about a great boat trip.
Cool. Hey, do you want to go to the cinema next Saturday? There's a new film on.
I'd love to, but my aunt's bought tickets for all of us to see a musical at the theatre. What about going to the museum on Sunday?
Sorry, I'm visiting my grandma on Sunday. Maybe another time.

l4_0.t: Hello, is that Riverside Sports Centre?
Yes, how can I help?
I was at the swimming pool yesterday afternoon, and I think I left my blue jacket in the changing room.
Let me look. Yes, someone gave us a blue jacket. Is your name inside it?
Yes, it's Tom Kerr. Can I come and get it after school?
Of course. We're open until nine.

l4_1.t: Have you been to the new café on Bridge Street?
Not yet. Is it good?

Yes! It isn't cheap – a hot chocolate costs four pounds. And they play music all the time, which I don't really like. But the people who work there are so friendly. The waiter remembered my name the second time I went!

l4_2.t: Good morning. Last week I booked a holiday in Spain here for my family.
Yes, I remember. Four people, flying on the twelfth of August.
That's right. The date's fine, and there are still four of us. But we've looked at the hotel on the internet, and it's a long way from the beach. Could you find us a different one?
Of course. Let me have a look.

l4_3.t: Our class went to the theatre in the city last night to see a play by Shakespeare. I thought it would be boring, because the language is so old and difficult. But the actors were fantastic and really funny, and I understood almost everything! I didn't want it to finish. I'm going to ask my parents to take me again.

l4_4.t: Good morning, everyone. I'm Mrs Patel from the town library. I'm here today because our opening times are changing. From next Monday, we'll open at eight o'clock, not half past nine, so you can come in before school. And on Saturdays we'll stay open until five. Oh, and the results of our story competition will be on our website next month. Thank you.

l5.t: Oliver, it's going to be a busy Saturday tomorrow. Everyone's going somewhere different.
Is Dad taking me to football?
No, sorry. Dad has to take the car to the garage first thing in the morning. The brakes are making a strange noise.
Oh. What about Grandma? Can she take me?
Grandma's busy too. She wanted to go to the bank, but she can do that on Monday. Tomorrow she's going to the hairdresser's. She's having her hair cut for Aunt Sue's wedding.
And Kate? Is she going to the library again? She's always there.
Not this time. She has to see the dentist at ten. Her tooth is still hurting.
Poor Kate. Is Uncle Jim coming to visit us?
No, he's going into town. He wanted to send some letters at the post office, but I said I'd do that for him. He's going to the travel agent to book his holiday to Canada.
So how do I get to my football match at the sports centre?
You can ride your bike. It's only ten minutes away.
OK. I'll leave at nine, then.

l1_0.t: Dad, where's Mum? Is she still at the bank?
No, she finished there an hour ago.
So is she at the library? She wanted to get a new book.
She was going to go there, but it's closed today. She's at the post office now, sending a parcel to Aunt Mai.

l1_1.t: Excuse me, how much is it to get into the science museum?
It's eight pounds for adults.
I'm fourteen. Is it cheaper for children?
Yes, under-sixteens pay six pounds. It's only four pounds on Wednesdays, but today's Saturday, I'm afraid.
That's OK. One ticket, please.

l1_2.t: Hello, Ben. What's the problem today? Is it your cold again?
No, doctor, that's much better now. I hurt my foot playing football yesterday.
I see. Does your head hurt too?
A little, but that's only because I didn't sleep well.
OK, let me look at your foot.

l1_3.t: Let's go swimming after school today. The pool closes at eight, doesn't it?
Only in summer. In winter it closes at seven.
OK, so we've got lots of time.
Not today. Today it closes at six, because there's a swimming competition in the evening. We'll have to go straight after school.

l1_4.t: I'm hungry. Shall we go to that Italian restaurant?
It's a bit expensive. What about the café in the park?
It's closed in the winter. Let's just go back to my house – my dad's making soup.
Even better!

l2.t: Good evening, everyone, and welcome to the Park View Hotel. I hope you had a good journey. I'm the hotel manager, and I'm going to tell you a few important things. First, breakfast. It's in the restaurant on the ground floor. For most guests it starts at seven o'clock, but for school groups it's at half past seven, so please don't come down earlier. We also have a lovely swimming pool. It isn't in the basement like in a lot of hotels – it's on the second floor, next to the gym. You can use it from four until eight every evening. Your teachers tell me you're going to visit the city museum on Tuesday and the castle on Wednesday. The tourist bus stops right outside the hotel, so it's very easy. If you have any problems with your room, please talk to our receptionist, Mr Ruiz. That's R-U-I-Z. He speaks Spanish and English. And finally, please be careful with your room keys. If you lose one, you'll have to pay fifteen pounds for a new one. Have a great stay!

l3.t: Hi Chloe. I heard you've got a job at the café in the high street. Is that right?
Yes! I started two weeks ago. I wanted to work on Saturday mornings, but another girl already does that. So I work on Sunday afternoons, from twelve until five.
Cool. Do you cook?
No, I'm not allowed to cook yet. I thought I'd be in the kitchen washing plates all day, but they have a machine for that. I take people's orders and bring the food to their tables.
Do you like it?
I love it. The money isn't much – five pounds an hour. I get a free lunch, which is nice. But the best thing is the other waiters. They're really funny and we laugh all afternoon.
What are you going to do with the money? Buy clothes?
My friends spend their money on clothes and concert tickets, but I'm saving it. My cousin and I want to go to Paris in the summer, and I have to pay for my train ticket.
That sounds great. Maybe I could ask for a job at the café too!
They don't need anyone at the moment. But the cinema next door is looking for someone to sell tickets at the weekend.
Really? I'll go there this afternoon and ask.
Good luck! And come and have a hot chocolate at the café one Sunday.
Not this Sunday – I've got a football match. But soon!

l4_0.t: Hello. My name's Helen Ward. I've got a room at your hotel for Friday and Saturday night.
Yes, Mrs Ward, I can see your booking here.
The problem is, I can't come on Friday now because of my work. Could I have the room for Saturday and Sunday night instead?
Let me check. Yes, that's fine.

l4_1.t: I went to the dentist this morning. I was really scared before I went, because last time it hurt a lot. We had to wait twenty minutes, but I didn't mind – I read a comic. The dentist was really kind, and she said my teeth were perfect, so she didn't need to do anything! I was so happy when I came out.

l4_2.t: So what did you think of the film?
Well, the actors were good, I suppose, and it wasn't too long.
But?
I didn't understand what was happening half the time. There were too many people in the story, and they kept going to different places!

l4_3.t: Good morning. Would you like a map of the town?
No, thanks, I've already got one. I'm looking for the Grand Hotel. I know it's in Hill Street, but I don't know the number.
It's number forty-two. Would you like to take the bus?
No, I'll walk. Thanks.

l4_4.t: The new swimming pool in our town is lovely. It's big, the water's warm, and tickets are only two pounds. I thought it would be a long way from my house, but it's only ten minutes on my bike. The only problem is that everyone in town wants to go there! There are so many people in the water that I can hardly swim.

l5.t: Hi Hannah. How's your project about jobs in our town going?

Great! Each of us visited a different place and talked to someone who works there. Ryan wanted to go to the garage, because he loves cars, but they were too busy. So he went to the hotel by the river and talked to the receptionist.
And Mia? She loves acting.
That's right, so she went to the theatre. She even met one of the actors!
What about Duc? Did he go to the post office? His mum works there.
He thought about it, but in the end he chose the bank. He wants to work with money one day.
And Sophie?
Sophie wanted to visit the café in the park, but it was closed for the week. So she went to the Chinese restaurant in Market Street instead. The cook showed her the kitchen.
Lucky her! And where did you go?
I went to the museum. I talked to a woman who looks after the old paintings. It was really interesting.
It sounds like a great project.

l1_0.t: Did you find anything at the shops, Joe?
I wanted a new T-shirt, but they were all too expensive. So I just got this cap. It was only eight pounds.
Nice! And did you get the socks for Dad's birthday?
Oh no, I forgot! I'll go back tomorrow.

l1_1.t: That's a nice book. Was it expensive?
The price on the back says twelve pounds, but there was a sale at the bookshop.
So how much did you pay?
Nine pounds. My friend bought the same book online for six, but she had to wait a week for it.

l1_2.t: That's thirty-two pounds fifty, please. Would you like to pay by card?
I usually do, but my credit card isn't working today. Can I pay by cheque?
Sorry, we don't take cheques any more.
Then I'll pay in cash. Here's forty pounds.
Thank you. And here's your change.

l1_3.t: Excuse me, is there a shoe shop near here?
There was one next to the bank, but it closed last month. There's one in the department store now, on the second floor.
Is that the big store opposite the supermarket?
No, that's a café. The department store is at the end of this street.

l1_4.t: Mum, can we go to the computer shop on Sunday? I want to buy a new game.
OK, but it doesn't open at nine like on weekdays. I think it opens at ten.
I checked on their website. It opens at eleven on Sundays and closes at four.
Fine. We'll go before lunch, then. Lunch is at twelve.

l2.t: Good morning, shoppers, and welcome to Kingsley's Department Store. Our big summer sale has started! It's on until Sunday – not next Wednesday, as it said in some of our advertisements – so don't wait too long. On the second floor you'll find everything you need for the new school year. School bags were thirty pounds, but now they're only fifteen pounds. School shoes are cheaper too, and if you buy any pair of shoes today, you'll get a free pair of socks. Sorry, but the free umbrellas finished yesterday. When you're tired of shopping, why not visit our café? It's on the fourth floor, and it has great views of the city. Try our chocolate cake – it's only two pounds fifty. And please remember that the store is closing earlier than usual tonight, at half past seven, not at nine o'clock. Thank you for shopping at Kingsley's!

l3.t: Amy, it's Mum's birthday next week. We need to buy her a present. I've got fifteen pounds. How much have you got?
Ten pounds. So that's twenty-five altogether.
Grandma said she'd give us five more, but she forgot.
Never mind. What about a scarf? I saw a lovely one in the department store.
I saw it too. It was forty pounds! That's much more than we've got.
Oh. Well, what about a book? She loves cooking.
She got two cookbooks for Christmas. What about a plant for her office? There's a flower shop next to the bank, and their prices are good.
Perfect! She always says her office is boring. Dad wanted to buy her a necklace, so a plant is a good idea from us.
Let's go after school today.
I can't, I've got swimming. And the flower shop is closed on Sundays. What about Saturday morning?
OK, Saturday morning. Shall we make her a birthday card too?
Yes. And I'll make a cake.
You always burn cakes! I'll make the cake this year. You can make the card.
Fine!

l4_0.t: Hi. I bought this jumper here last week, but I'd like to bring it back.
Is there a problem? Is it too small?
No, it fits fine, and I love the colour. But look – there's a hole in the arm.
Oh dear, I'm sorry. Would you like your money back, or a new one?

l4_1.t: The new supermarket near my house is great. It isn't cheap – some things cost more than at the market. And it closes at ten, like the other supermarkets. But you can buy food from everywhere – Japanese noodles, Mexican sauces, French cheese. My mum loves cooking, so she's really happy.

l4_2.t: Excuse me. This dress is lovely, but there isn't a price on it.
It's thirty-five pounds. Would you like to try it on? The changing rooms are over there.
Not now, thanks. I just wanted to know how much it costs. I'll come back with my daughter on Saturday.

l4_3.t: Do you buy things online?
Not much. Things are often cheaper online, and they arrive quickly, too.
So why don't you?
I like going into town with my friends on Saturdays. We look in all the shops and have lunch together. Shopping online on your own isn't fun.

l4_4.t: Attention please, shoppers. The store will close in fifteen minutes, at eight o'clock. Please take your shopping to the checkout now. Customers who are in the car park, please remember the gates close at quarter past eight. We'll be open again tomorrow morning at seven. Thank you for shopping with us.

l5.t: Hi Sara. Did you have a good time in town on Saturday?
Yes, the whole family went to the new shopping centre. Everyone bought something!
What did your mum get?
She wanted some sunglasses for our holiday, but they were all too expensive. So she bought some brown boots in the sale instead. They were half price!
Nice. And your dad?
His old watch stopped working, so he got a new one in the department store. He paid in cash because he forgot his credit card.
What about your brother? Did he buy a dictionary for school? Your mum said he needed one.
He was supposed to! But he spent all his money on a computer game. Mum wasn't very happy.
Ha! Did your grandma come too?
Yes. I thought she'd buy a necklace – she looked at them for ages. But in the end she bought a plant for her kitchen.
And you?
I tried on about ten pairs of jeans! Finally I found some I liked. They cost twenty-five pounds.

l1_0.t: Right, Lisa, we're in the department store now. What do you need for school?
A new pencil case. My old one's broken.
What about a school bag? Yours looks very old.
It's fine, Dad, really. And I've got lots of pens at home, so I don't need any.

l1_1.t: Excuse me, how much is this T-shirt?
It's twenty euros. But if you buy two, they're fifteen euros each.
I only want one. Have you got anything cheaper?
This one's only ten euros, but we haven't got it in your size.
OK, I'll take the first one, then.

l1_2.t: We need bread for the picnic. Shall we get it at the supermarket?
Their bread isn't very good. The baker's in Hill Street is better.
It's closed on Mondays. What about the market? There's a man there who sells great bread.
Good idea. It's on our way to the park.

l1_3.t: Your brother put an advertisement in the shop window, didn't he? Did he sell his bike?
No, nobody wanted it. But someone bought his old games console for fifty pounds.
Great! What about all his old books?
He's giving those to the library.

l1_4.t: Excuse me, where can I find football boots? I thought the sports things were on the ground floor.
They were, but we moved them last week. They're on the third floor now.
Thanks. Can I take the stairs?
Yes, or the lift. The first floor is only women's clothes, so don't stop there!

l2.t: Hello, everybody. I'm Kate Moreno – that's M-O-R-E-N-O – and I'm the owner of a new kind of shop in town called Borrow Box. At Borrow Box, you don't buy things, you rent them. Why spend lots of money on a tent or a bike if you only need it for one weekend? We're in Market Street, next to the bookshop. We wanted to open in the shopping centre, but the rent there was too expensive! Our most popular thing is the tent. It costs eight pounds a night, and we have sleeping bags too, for four pounds a night. We also rent bikes, skis and even things for parties, like lights and music speakers. We're open six days a week. We're closed on Wednesdays, because that's when we clean and repair everything. If you're under eighteen, you must come with a parent, because we need an adult to sign a form. Oh, and when you rent something, you get a free bag to carry it in. Come and visit us soon!

l3.t: Welcome home, Daisy! Did the hundred dollars I gave you last the whole week?
Yes, Dad. Grandma gave me fifty dollars too, so I had a hundred and fifty.
Lucky you! Did Aunt Jo take you to that famous department store?
We went in, but it was so busy that we left after ten minutes. Then we found a street market in Brooklyn. I bought nearly everything there. The hotel shop was much too expensive.
Did you get your brother a T-shirt? He asked for one.
They didn't have his size, so I got him a baseball cap instead. He wanted a football as well, but it was too big for my bag.
Was everything expensive?

About the same as here, really. And the shop assistants were friendly, like at home. But one thing was strange. The price on the label isn't the price you pay! They add a bit more when you pay. So I never had the right money ready.
Oh yes, I remember that. Have you got any dollars left? You could change them into pounds at the bank.
I've only got twelve dollars. The bank won't give me much for that. Aunt Jo says I can visit her again next summer, so I'll keep them for then.
Good idea. Just don't let your brother find them!

l4_0.t: Hi. I bought these trainers here on Saturday, but they're too small.
Would you like your money back?
No, thanks, I really like them. Have you got the same ones in a size forty-two?
Let me check. Yes, here you are.

l4_1.t: Everyone was excited when the new shopping centre opened. It's easy to get there on the bus, and there are some cheap shops too. But I think it's quite boring. It's the same clothes shops you can find in every town. I prefer the little shops in the old part of town – they sell things you can't find anywhere else.

l4_2.t: Max, what's all this in the trolley? Chocolate, crisps, three bags of sweets!
They're on special offer, Mum. They're really cheap!
I don't care. We only came for milk and bread. Put them back, please, and let's go and pay.

l4_3.t: I start work at eight. First I check that everything is ready before we open the doors at nine. During the day I talk to customers and help them find the right book. I often tell them about stories I've enjoyed. At lunchtime I sometimes help in the café upstairs, but that's not my real job. And I don't decide the prices – the manager does that.

l4_4.t: Hi Zoe, it's Amy. About shopping tomorrow – I can still come, but not at ten o'clock. I have to help my mum in the morning. Can we meet at two instead, outside the department store? Oh, and I've still got the money you lent me last week. I'll give it back tomorrow. See you!

l5.t: Hi Ryan. What's in all those bags? Did you spend all your money at the market?
Not all of it! Look, Mum, I got this camera. It's quite old, but it works.
How much was it?
The man wanted fifteen pounds, but I asked for a lower price and he said twelve.
Well done. And the football?
That was only two pounds. It needs some air, but it's fine.
And what's this? A comic?
Yes, it was fifty pence. The woman had lots of comics, but I only wanted this one because it's about football.
Is this lamp for your bedroom?
Yes! The label said ten pounds, but the woman said I could have it for five, because the switch is a bit broken.
Hmm. Dad can repair it. And this jacket?
That was eight pounds. It's like new! The man next to her was selling one for three pounds, but it had a hole in it.
So how much money have you got left?
Just one pound! But I think I bought some really good things for the price.

l1_0.t: Dad, can you drive me to the sports centre on Saturday morning?
For your swimming lesson?
No, the pool's closed this weekend. I'm playing volleyball with Anna's team. They need one more player.
Oh. I thought you were playing tennis with Grace this weekend.
That's on Sunday afternoon.

l1_1.t: Hello. How much are tickets for Saturday's hockey match?
Adult tickets are fifteen pounds.
I'm thirteen. Is it cheaper for me?
Yes. For under-sixteens it's eight pounds if you buy it now. If you buy it on the day of the match, it's twelve.
OK, I'll buy one now, then.

l1_2.t: Have you got everything for your tennis lesson, Sam?
I think so. My racket's in my bag, and I'm wearing my trainers.
What about a drink? It's very hot today.
Oh no! I left my water bottle on the kitchen table.
Don't worry. You can buy one at the club.

l1_3.t: Hi, is Lucas at home? We're going cycling this afternoon.
No, sorry. He went to the beach early this morning to go surfing.
Is he still there? Or is he at the pool? He sometimes has swimming practice on Saturdays.
Swimming's tomorrow. He phoned an hour ago – he's at the stadium with his dad now, watching the football. He'll be back at six.

l1_4.t: Are you going skiing with your family again this winter, Minh?
Yes, we're going to the mountains in February. But I'm a bit bored of skiing. I've done it for years.
So will you go ice skating instead?
No, I'm not very good at that. I want to have snowboarding lessons. My cousin says it's easier than it looks.
Cool! Send me a video.

l2.t: Hello, everyone. I'm going to tell you about this year's Summer Sports Camp at Hillside Sports Centre. The camp is for young people aged ten to fifteen. It starts on Monday the twenty-first of July – not on the Saturday, as it said on our website. Sorry about that! Please arrive at a quarter to nine every morning. Activities start at nine o'clock, and we finish at four. There are lots of sports to choose from: tennis, basketball, swimming in the indoor pool, and this year we're adding baseball for the first time. A week at the camp costs ninety-five pounds. That includes lunch every day, but you'll need to bring your own drinks. If you're a member of the sports centre, it's only eighty pounds. On the last day, Friday, there'll be a big race around the park, and the winner will get a prize, so practise your running! Parents are welcome to come and watch. Please bring your swimming costume and a towel every day. If you have any questions, please contact the camp leader, Mrs Dalby. That's D-A-L-B-Y. Her email address is on the website.

l3.t: Hi Oscar. Is it true you're entering the bike race next month?

Yes! It goes along the river from the town centre. My PE teacher told me about it. At first I wanted to do the ten-kilometre race, but my dad said I was ready for the twenty-kilometre one. There's a thirty-kilometre race too, but that's only for adults.
Wow. How are you getting ready for it? Do you go to the gym?
I wanted to, but there isn't enough time. I cycle to school every day now, and on Sundays I ride with my uncle in the hills. That's the hardest part. I'm always really tired afterwards!
Have you got a good bike? Your old one's quite small, isn't it?
Yes, it's much too small now. So I'm borrowing my cousin's racing bike. It's really light and fast. Mum says if I do well, she'll buy me my own bike next year.
Is there a prize for the winner?
Yes, a hundred pounds and a medal. But I don't think I'll win. Some of the riders are in cycling clubs and they're really fast. I just want to finish in under an hour. That's my plan.
Can I come and watch?
Of course! It starts at the bridge at ten o'clock, but there are always lots of people there. My family's going to wait at the finish line in the park. You could come with them.
Great. I'll make a sign with your name on it!

l4_0.t: We lost the match yesterday, sixty to forty-two.
Oh no. Were you upset?
Not really. The other team are much older than us, so we didn't expect to win. And I scored twelve points – my best ever! The coach said I played really well. I'm so happy with that.

l4_1.t: Hi Kai, it's Rob. About our tennis game tomorrow – it's still at the park at four o'clock, that's fine. But my racket's broken – I hit the wall with it yesterday! Have you got an old one I could use? Text me back. Thanks!

l4_2.t: Did you look at the swimming club, Leo? It isn't expensive.
Yes, I did. And the coach seemed really nice.
So what's the problem?
Practice is at six o'clock in the morning, three days a week! I'd be too tired for school.

l4_3.t: Sports day was great this year. I came third in the hundred metres, and I was quite happy with that. The weather was perfect too – sunny, but not too hot. But for me, the best part was the teachers' race at the end. Our maths teacher fell over, and everyone laughed – including him!

l4_4.t: How was your first golf lesson, Zara?
Fun, but I was terrible! It looks so easy when you watch it on TV. I hit the ground more times than the ball!
Will you go again?
Yes. The lessons are free for students, so why not?

l5.t: So, Hannah, all your friends go to the new sports centre, don't they?
Yes, Grandpa, but we all do different things. Ruby used to play table-tennis, but she stopped because her back hurt. Now she plays volleyball with a team on Mondays.
And what about Tariq? Is he still mad about football?
He still watches it on TV, but the sports centre doesn't have a football team. So he plays hockey instead. He says it's faster.
Duc is the boy who lives near the lake, isn't he? I've seen him out on the water in a little boat.
Yes, his dad takes him sailing in the summer. But at the sports centre he goes swimming every day before school. He wants to swim in competitions.
Good for him. And Megan?
Megan's really tall, so everyone thought she'd play basketball. But she says she's terrible at catching the ball! She loves the skateboard park outside the centre. She's there every afternoon.
Skateboarding? Isn't that dangerous?
She always wears a helmet. And then there's Felix. His dad wanted him to play golf, like him, but Felix found it really boring. He joined the basketball club last month, and now he's in the team.
And what about you, Hannah?
Me? I'm still trying everything!

l1_0.t: When does your swimming race start, Kate?
The competition starts at ten, but the girls' races are later.
So is yours at eleven?
No, that's my friend's race. Mine is at half past ten. But I have to be at the pool before that to get ready.

l1_1.t: Is your dad watching the tennis on TV again?
No, that finished yesterday. It's golf today. He watches it for hours!
My dad's the same with baseball. He even stays up at night to watch games from America.
Ha! Shall we go outside, then?

l1_2.t: Are you ready for the boat trip, Lan? Don't forget your swimming costume.
We aren't going swimming, Dad. The water's too cold. We're going fishing.
Oh! Have you got a fishing rod?
There are rods on the boat for everyone. But it's windy on the sea, so I'll take my warm jacket.

l1_3.t: You're late, Ali! Did you cycle here?
I wanted to, but my brother took my bike this morning.
So did you come by bus?
I waited at the bus stop for twenty minutes, but it didn't come. So in the end I walked. That's why I'm late. Sorry, coach.

l1_4.t: Well done for winning the race, Ella! Did you get a medal?
Everyone who finished got a medal. But the winner got something better.
A cup?
No, the cup was for the best team. I got a pair of new running trainers!

l2.t: Hi, everyone. Thanks for coming to hear about the Blue Water Sailing Club. We're a club for young people aged eleven to sixteen, and we sail on Green Lake, just outside town. Last year we met on Sundays, but the lake is very busy then, so now the club meets on Saturdays, from ten until one. You don't need to know anything about sailing before you start. But you must be able to swim two hundred metres. Fifty metres isn't enough – sometimes you fall in, and the lake is quite deep! It costs thirty pounds a month to be a member. That pays for the boats and your lessons. We give everyone a life jacket, so you don't need to buy one. But please bring a towel, because you'll probably get wet. And wear old trainers, not your best ones! Your teacher will be Kevin Nolan. That's N-O-L-A-N. He's sailed all over the world and he's won lots of races. If you'd like to join, please fill in a form at the sports centre.

l3.t: Hi Leo! How was your skiing holiday in Austria?
Amazing, thanks, Nina. We stayed in a small hotel in the mountains. Last year we went to France and rented a flat with some friends, but Mum didn't want to cook this time!
Was it your first time on skis?
Yes. The first day was really hard. Standing up on the snow wasn't too bad, and carrying the skis was OK. The problem was the boots. They were so heavy, and I could hardly walk in them!
Did your dad teach you? He's a good skier, isn't he?

He wanted to teach me, but he's not very patient! So I joined a ski school. My teacher was a young woman called Anna. She was great, and she spoke really good English. My sister had lessons with her too.
Did you try snowboarding as well?

My sister did, but I didn't have time. Skiing down the mountain on the last day was fun. But the best thing was on the last afternoon, when we went ice skating on a frozen lake. There were mountains all around, and it was snowing a little. It was beautiful.
Sounds lovely. Will you go back to Austria next year?
I hope so! But first I want to practise. There's an indoor ski centre about an hour from here. Dad says we can go there next month. Some of my friends from school want to come too.
Can I come?
Of course!

l4_0.t: How was the match? You won, didn't you?
Yes, four–one. But the coach kept me on the bench for the whole game. I didn't play at all! And I practised so hard this week.
Oh dear. Well, I'm sure you'll play next time.

l4_1.t: OK, everyone, listen please. The weather forecast says it's going to rain all day tomorrow, so we won't have our PE lesson on the field. Instead, we'll play table-tennis and volleyball in the sports hall. So please bring your indoor trainers, not your football boots. Thank you.

l4_2.t: So we're cycling to the beach on Saturday? It's thirty kilometres!
I know. Why don't we leave at seven instead of nine? Then we can have a rest on the beach before lunch.
Seven? That's so early!
But it'll be cooler then, and we won't get so tired.
