l4_3.t: The new sports centre opened last week. It's got a big pool, a climbing wall and four tennis courts, and everything's really modern. The only thing is, you can't walk or cycle there. It's outside town, next to the motorway, so you need a car or the bus. I go with my mum on Saturdays, but I'd love to go more often.

l4_4.t: Did you enjoy the match yesterday, Sami?

Yes! The game wasn't very exciting – it finished nil–nil. And my favourite footballer didn't play because he was ill. But the fans were amazing. Fifty thousand people singing together – it was so loud! I loved it.
And the food?
Too expensive!

l5.t: Hi Rosa! How was your holiday by the sea?
Brilliant, thanks. We all did different things. My dad hired a little boat and went sailing every morning. He wanted to go fishing too, but he never had time.
What about your mum? Did she go in the boat with him?
No, she feels sick on boats! She played tennis once, but mostly she went for long walks along the cliffs. She walked about ten kilometres every day.
Wow. And your brother? Did he play volleyball on the beach? He's in the school team, isn't he?
He watched other people play, but he spent all his time with his surfboard. He's really good at surfing now.
And your grandpa came too, didn't he?
Yes. He sat by the river with his fishing rod for hours every day. He caught a really big fish on the last day!
So what did you do? Lots of swimming?
No, the sea was too cold for swimming! There was a riding school near our hotel, so I went riding every afternoon. My horse was called Star.
That sounds great.

l1_0.t: Did you see any animals on your walk in the forest, Tom?
We hoped to see some rabbits, but there weren't any.
That's a shame. What about birds?
We heard lots of them, but they were too high up in the trees to see. But when we stopped for lunch by the river, a fox came really close to us! I took a photo.

l1_1.t: Shall we climb the mountain tomorrow?
Let me check the weather. Today it's raining, but tomorrow it'll be sunny all day.
Will there be any snow at the top?
Not now, it's summer! There was snow up there in May, but it's all gone.

l1_2.t: Where shall we have our picnic? By the lake?
There are too many people there on Sundays. What about the top of the hill? The view's amazing.
It's a long walk with all this food!
OK, then. What about the field next to the farm? There's a big tree there, so we can sit in the shade.
Perfect.

l1_3.t: What are you growing in your part of the school garden, Ryan?
I wanted to grow tomatoes, but Mr Clark said our garden is too cold for them.
So what are you growing?
Sunflowers! They can grow really tall – maybe two metres. Next year I'm going to try strawberries.

l1_4.t: How did you get to the island? By boat?
That's how most people go. But in the morning the sea goes out a long way, and you can walk across the sand.
Really?
Yes! We walked there in the morning. But we had to come back by boat in the afternoon, because the water came back.

l2.t: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Greenwood Forest Centre. Here's the plan for today. First, you can leave your bags in the classroom. Our walk through the forest starts at a quarter past ten, so you've got fifteen minutes to get ready. The walk is six kilometres. Some groups do the long walk to the top of the hill – that's ten kilometres – but it's too far for today. On the way, we'll look at the different trees and plants, and if you're quiet, you might see some deer. At about half past twelve we'll stop for lunch next to the river. Please don't go into the water – it's deeper than it looks! In the afternoon, you're going to help us plant trees. Every year about a thousand trees in this forest are lost because of strong winds, so we need your help. We'll give you gloves, but please wear old shoes or boots. My name's Kate Morrow, and I'll be your guide today. That's M-O-R-R-O-W. If you have any questions, just ask me. OK, let's go!

l3.t: Hi Ben! You look really brown. Where have you been?
I spent three weeks on my uncle's farm in the countryside.
Is that in the north, near the mountains?
No, it's in the west, near the sea. My uncle used to live in the south, but he moved there five years ago.
So what did you do there all day?
Lots! Every morning I got up at six and helped to give food to the sheep. In the afternoons I sometimes worked in the fields, but only when it wasn't too hot. And once or twice we went to the beach.
Was the work hard?

Not really. But the thing that surprised me was how quiet it was. At home in the city there's always noise from cars. On the farm, at night, I could only hear the wind in the trees. And the sky was full of stars.
Was there anything you didn't like?
The weather was perfect and my aunt's food was great. But the insects were terrible, especially near the river in the evenings. I've still got bites everywhere!
Will you go back?
Definitely. My uncle wants me to come in the spring, when the baby sheep are born. But I can't, because I've got exams. So I'll go next summer again, and maybe I'll take my sister.

l4_0.t: Dad, can you help me with my science project?
Sure. What's it about? Space again? You did the moon last term.
No, this time it's about the river at the end of our street. We have to find out what plants and animals live in the water. Can we go there on Saturday?
Good idea.

l4_1.t: Yesterday I climbed Snow Hill with my brother. It took four hours to get to the top, and my legs really hurt. When we got there, there was so much cloud that we couldn't see anything! But I didn't mind. It's the highest hill in our area, and I did it. I'm really pleased with myself.

l4_2.t: Right, everyone, we're in the forest now. You can take as many photos of the flowers as you like, but please don't pick them. Leave them for other people to enjoy. In this part of the forest, you don't have to stay on the paths – you're free to explore. But stay where you can see a teacher, please.

l4_3.t: It's so cold today. The news says it might snow tonight.
I hope it does! I don't want to make a snowman or anything – I'm too old for that.
Ha! So you want school to close?
No, I like school! I want to take photos of the hills when they're white. It's for a photo competition.

l4_4.t: Tonight at eight, don't miss Wild World. This week, the team travels to a small island in the far north, where it's winter for nine months of the year. They'll show you how the birds there find food on the ice and snow. And next week, the team visits a hot desert in Africa.

l5.t: Right, Nam, you're helping me with the list. Let's check who's doing what for the nature project. Lily wanted to do flowers, didn't she?
She did, Miss, but Sara chose flowers first. So Lily's doing mountains. She climbed one with her family in the summer, so she's got lots of photos.
So Sara's doing flowers. Good. What about Omar? Islands, wasn't it?
He was going to, but he couldn't find enough information. He's doing rivers now. He lives next to a big one, so he can go and look at it.
Great. And Duc?
Duc's really interested in space. He wanted to do the moon, but you said there wasn't enough to write about. So he's doing stars.
Oh yes, I remember. And you, Nam? Are you doing the sea?
I was going to do forests, but Lily's sister did forests last year, and I want something different. So I'm doing ice – you know, in the far north and the south of the world.
Excellent. That's an interesting topic. Get started, then!

l1_0.t: Shall we start with the space room? I really want to see the rocket.
Look, it's very busy in there now. Let's go to the Planet Earth room first. There's a big model of the world with all the mountains and seas.
OK. And the dinosaur room?
It's closed today. We can see the rocket after lunch.

l1_1.t: Hi Mum, it's me. We're on the island!
Great! What's the weather like? It was raining when you left.
Yesterday it rained all day here too, but today it's really hot and sunny. We're going to the beach.
Is it windy? It's very windy here.
No, not at all.

l1_2.t: That's a nice hat, Max. Is it new?
Yes, my grandma made it for me from wool. She wanted to make a scarf, but she didn't have enough wool.
And are those gloves new too?
No, I've had those for ages.

l1_3.t: Let's watch the stars tonight. Shall we sit in the garden?
There are too many lights from the houses. What about the beach?
It's too cold and windy by the sea at night. Let's drive up the hill behind the village. It's really dark up there.
Good idea.

l1_4.t: Two tickets for the ten o'clock boat to the island, please.
Sorry, that one's full. The next one leaves at half past ten.
Is there one at eleven?
No. After half past ten, there isn't another boat until the afternoon.
OK, half past ten, then.

l2.t: Good morning, and welcome to Sea Bird Tours. Today we're taking you to a very special place – Fenna Island. That's F-E-N-N-A. It's a small island about five kilometres west of here, and nobody lives there – only thousands of birds! Our boat leaves at a quarter past nine, so please be here ten minutes before that. Don't be late – we can't wait for anyone, because the sea gets rough later in the day. The trip takes three hours in total. Some people think it's a whole day, but we're back by lunchtime. We'll sail all round the island first, and then we'll stop for lunch. There isn't a café on the island, so we'll have a picnic on the beach. We give you sandwiches and water. Remember it's windy on the sea, even in summer, so bring a warm jumper. Tickets cost twenty pounds for adults and twelve pounds for children under sixteen. And if you're lucky, you might see some seals swimming near the boat. Any questions?

l3.t: Hi Sara. How was the space centre?
Brilliant, thanks, Tom! I went with my cousin Ella. My parents were busy, and my class is going next month, but I couldn't wait that long!
So what was the best part?
We saw a real rock from the moon, which was cool, and we watched a film about the stars. But the best thing was trying on a real space suit. It was so heavy, but I loved it!
Did you learn anything interesting?
Yes! Astronauts on the space station go round the world very fast, so they see the sun come up sixteen times every day. Can you believe it? And they drink water from special bags.
Wow. Did you buy anything?
The shop was really expensive. I wanted a model rocket, but it was forty pounds! So I just got a poster of the moon for my bedroom wall. Ella bought a pen with stars on it.
Sounds great. I'd love to go.
You should! It's only an hour away by train. Actually, there's a special star night there next month. You can look at the planets through a really big telescope. Shall we go together?
Yes, please! I'll ask my mum tonight.

l4_0.t: Dad, can I watch the programme about the Pacific Ocean tonight?
Really? I thought you didn't like nature programmes.
I don't usually. But our geography teacher says we have to watch it and write about it for tomorrow.
OK, then. It starts at seven.

l4_1.t: Most of my friends love summer, but my favourite season is winter. It's not because of the cold – I hate being cold! And I'm terrible at skiing. But in winter my whole family comes to my grandparents' house in the countryside. We sit around the fire, tell stories and play games. It's the best.

l4_2.t: Welcome to Blue Lake, everyone. Before we start, some important things. The water here is very deep and very cold, even in summer, so nobody goes into the water without a life jacket. Stay together on the path, and don't climb on the rocks – they're wet. Later, I'll tell you about the plants and fish that live here.

l4_3.t: How was your walk in the hills yesterday? Did it rain?
No, the weather was lovely. But the map said it was eight kilometres, and it was more like fifteen! We didn't get home until nine o'clock.
Did you get lost?
No, we followed the path. The map was just wrong!

l4_4.t: Hi Jo, it's Amy. About tomorrow's picnic by the river – I've got all the food, so don't worry about that. We're still meeting at twelve at the bridge. But it's going to be colder than they said on the news – only ten degrees – so please bring a warm coat. See you!

l5.t: So, Mai, where are all your friends going this summer?
Well, Ella went to the mountains in Switzerland last year, but this year she's going to an island in Greece. She's so lucky!
And Josh?
Josh's parents wanted to go to a big city, but his little sister wanted to see animals. So they're staying on a farm in the countryside. He has to get up at six every morning to help!
Ha! What about Hana?
Hana's going camping in a forest with her outdoor club. They're going to sleep in tents and cook on a fire.
That sounds fun. And Ben?
Ben loves fishing, so his grandfather is taking him to a lake in the north of Scotland. They're going to stay in a little wooden house next to the water.
And Sofia?
She's going to the mountains with her parents. They're going to walk every day, about twenty kilometres! I'd be too tired.
Well, you're going on a river boat trip with us!
I know, Dad. I can't wait!

l1_0.t: Dad, what time is my swimming lesson tomorrow? Four o'clock, like last week?
No, the pool has changed the times. It starts at half past four now.
So we can leave home at four?
Yes. And it finishes at five, so I'll pick you up then.

l1_1.t: Is your birthday party on Friday, Tom? That's your real birthday, isn't it?
Yes, but everyone has school the next day, so it's not then.
Saturday, then?
My cousins can't come on Saturday, so we're having it on Sunday afternoon.

l1_2.t: Did you buy a new watch at the shopping centre? Yours is broken.
I looked, but they were all too expensive. I got an alarm clock instead. I'm always late for school!
Good idea. Did you get a diary for next year too?
No, I'll ask for one for Christmas.

l1_3.t: When's the school trip to the castle? Is it in June?
That's what Mr Lee said at first, but we have exams then. So it's in April now.
Oh. I thought it was after the summer holidays.
No, that's the trip to the museum, in October.

l1_4.t: How much homework do you do every day, Kai? Two hours?
No way! That's what my sister does. She's in her last year at school.
So less than that?
Usually about an hour. Thirty minutes is enough for maths, but then I need the same again for English.

l2.t: Hello, everyone. I'm going to tell you about this year's Summer Holiday Activity Club. School finishes on Friday the eighteenth of July, and the club starts the next Monday – that's the twenty-first. It runs for two weeks, every weekday. Please don't come too early. The doors open at a quarter to nine every morning, and activities start at nine o'clock. We finish at three, not half past three like last year. Every day there are sports in the morning and art or music in the afternoon. There's also a special trip. Last year we went to the zoo on a Tuesday, but this year we're going to the beach, on the Thursday of the second week. The coach leaves at eight o'clock that day, so you'll need to come early. You'll need to bring lunch and a water bottle, and because it's summer, please bring a hat every day. We'll spend a lot of time outside. You don't need to bring sports clothes – just wear them. The club leader this year is Mrs Dawson. That's D-A-W-S-O-N. If you have any questions, you can email her before the end of June.

l3.t: Hi Lucy. How's your new school? You look tired!
I am! I have to get up at six o'clock now. My old school was near my house, but this one is forty minutes away by bus.
Six! That's early. What time do lessons start?
At ten to eight. Lots of students arrive at half past seven to play football before school, but I'm never there that early.
And when do you finish?
Usually at four. But on Wednesdays we finish at half past two, because the teachers have a meeting. That's my favourite day of the week.
Do you get lots of homework?
Quite a lot. But I do it in the library at lunchtime, so I don't have to do it in the evening. Then I can watch TV or practise the guitar after dinner.
Good idea. What's your favourite lesson?

I thought it was going to be Art, because I loved it at my old school. But actually, it's History. The teacher tells us amazing stories about people from hundreds of years ago. Last week we learned about the fifteenth century.
Cool. Hey, are you free this weekend? We could go to the cinema on Saturday.
I'm visiting my aunt on Saturday. And on Sunday morning I'm going to sleep! But I'm free in the afternoon. Let's meet at three.
Perfect. See you on Sunday.

l4_0.t: Leo, it's nearly seven o'clock! Where were you?
Sorry, Mum. The football team had a meeting after lessons. The coach wanted to talk about next Saturday's match.
Why didn't you phone me?
My phone battery was dead. But I caught the first bus after the meeting, I promise!

l4_1.t: Hi Jess, it's Ana. About tomorrow – I know we said we'd meet at the library at ten, but I've got a dentist's appointment at half past nine and I don't think I'll finish in time. Can we meet at eleven instead? Then we can still work on our project before lunch. Text me back. Bye!

l4_2.t: Nice watch, Mai. Is it new?
Yes, it was a birthday present from my uncle. It's a lovely colour, and it's not heavy at all.
Can you go swimming with it?
Yes. But the problem is the numbers. They're so small that I can never see what time it is! I always have to ask someone.

l4_3.t: Listen, everyone, I've got some news. The October holidays will start a week later than we said. That's because the swimming competition is now on the twentieth of October, and many of you are in the team. So your last day of school before the holidays is Friday the twenty-fourth, not the seventeenth. Please tell your parents tonight.

l4_4.t: Every Sunday I help my uncle at his bakery. I have to get up at five o'clock in the morning, when it's still dark. My friends think I'm crazy, and at first I really hated it. But now I love it. The streets are so quiet, and the bread smells amazing. And I finish at noon, so I have the whole afternoon free.

l5.t: Sophie, let's write next week in the diary on the fridge. It's going to be a busy week.
OK, Dad. Monday first. I usually play badminton on Mondays, but the sports hall is closed next week.
So what are you doing instead?
My guitar teacher can't come on Thursday as usual, so she's moved my lesson to Monday at five.
Fine. Tuesday – that's your appointment with the dentist, isn't it? At quarter past four.
Yes. I wanted to go to homework club that day, but I can go the week after.
And Wednesday? There's swimming after school.
That's right. We're practising for the competition, so I can't miss it.
Then Thursday. No guitar, so you're free?
Not really. I've joined the cooking club. We're making pizza this week!
Great – bring some home! And Friday? Your friends asked about the cinema.
They want to see a film on Friday evening, but it's Grandma's birthday, and we're all having dinner at her house.
Of course! I nearly forgot. Let's go to the cinema on Saturday instead.

l1_0.t: Mum, I'm hungry. When's dinner? Seven o'clock, as usual?
Not tonight. Dad's working late, and he won't be home until half past seven.
So we'll eat as soon as he gets home?
A bit after that. The chicken needs half an hour in the oven, so let's say eight o'clock.

l1_1.t: Is your piano exam this Thursday, Rosa?
It was on Thursday, but my teacher moved it.
To Tuesday, then?
No, Tuesday is my normal lesson. The exam's the day after, on Wednesday, at quarter to ten in the morning.

l1_2.t: What are you getting Anna for her birthday, Ben? A watch?
She's already got one. I thought about a calendar with photos of horses on it.
Oh, she'll love that.
Hmm, but I saw one just like it in her room yesterday. So I'm going to buy her a diary. She can write in it every day.

l1_3.t: Is the school concert still on the twelfth of May?
No, that was the old date. They changed it because the new hall isn't ready yet.
So is it in June now?
No, it's on the twenty-second of May. The second of June is sports day.

l1_4.t: You look tired, Pete. Did you go to bed late last night?
Yes. I usually go at ten o'clock, but there was a great film on TV.
Did it finish at midnight?
No, at eleven. I went to bed straight after it finished.

l2.t: Good morning, and welcome to What's On. This week, the Old Town Clock Museum is having a special event called Night at the Museum. It's on Saturday the twenty-ninth of October – that's the night when the clocks go back one hour. The museum usually closes at five, but on that evening it opens again at half past seven, and the event finishes at ten. Tickets for adults cost eight pounds. Children under sixteen pay four pounds, and children under five can go in free. There are more than two hundred clocks in the museum. The oldest one is four hundred years old, and it still works! At nine o'clock, a guide will show visitors how it works. There's also a talk about the famous clock-maker John Harlow. That's H-A-R-L-O-W. He made the big clock on the town hall in eighteen sixty. You can buy tickets on the museum website, or at the door on the night. And don't forget to change your clocks before you go to bed!

l3.t: Theo, it's Kim's birthday next Friday. Shall we have a surprise party for her?
Great idea! On Friday evening?
She has a violin lesson every Friday, and she doesn't finish until eight. What about Saturday?
I've got football on Saturday afternoon. Can we have it in the evening?
Yes, Saturday evening is fine. And we can have it at my flat. My parents said it's OK.
Why not at Kim's house? It's much bigger.
Because then it isn't a surprise! Her mum is going to bring her to my flat at seven o'clock. So everyone has to arrive before that – at quarter to seven at the latest.
OK, I'll tell everyone. What about food?
My dad's making pizzas. Can you bring a cake? You make really good chocolate ones.
Sure. And drinks?
Lily's bringing the drinks. Now, the present. I thought about a book, but she's got so many.
What about a new watch? She's always asking people what time it is!
Ha – perfect! Her old one broke last month. Let's all pay for it together.
Good. I'll send everyone a message tonight with the date, the time and the plan. Kim mustn't see it!

l4_0.t: Only one week of the holidays left! Are you sad?
Very! Every year it's the same. In June I think I've got so much time – nine whole weeks! But then suddenly it's the end of August, and I haven't done half the things I wanted.
I'm a bit bored now, actually.
Not me! I'd like them to go on for ever.

l4_1.t: Hi Dad, it's Jamie. I'm at Leo's house. Tomorrow's the school trip, and the coach leaves at half past six in the morning! My alarm clock isn't working, so can you wake me up at quarter to six? Don't worry about driving me – Leo's mum is taking us. See you tonight.

l4_2.t: I used to work from nine to five every day, and I never saw my kids after school. Now I start at seven in the morning and finish at three. Getting up at six isn't easy, and the money's the same. But now I can meet my children at the school gate every afternoon, and we do things together.

l4_3.t: Did you see that film about time travel last night?
Yes. It was three hours long, but the time went really fast.
Was it funny? It looked funny in the advert.
Not really. And I didn't understand it at all. The boy goes back to the eighteenth century, then to next year, then to yesterday. I was completely lost!

l4_4.t: Your English exam is next Monday at nine o'clock. Please be in the hall by twenty to nine, because we can't let anyone in late. There are clocks on the walls, so you don't need to bring a watch. And please don't study until midnight on Sunday – go to bed early!

l5.t: Max, for our project we need to know what time everyone in your family gets up. Let's start with your dad.
Dad's a baker, so he gets up really early – at half past five. Well, his alarm rings at five, but he stays in bed for another thirty minutes!
And your mum?
She starts work at eight, but she gets up at quarter past six. She likes to go running before breakfast.
What about your sister?
Ella's sixteen. Her alarm goes off at seven, but she never gets up then. Mum has to shout at half past seven, and then she finally gets up.
Ha! And your grandpa? He lives with you, doesn't he?
Yes. You'd think he'd sleep late because he doesn't work any more. But he gets up at quarter to seven every day to walk the dog. Then he goes back to bed at half past nine!
That's funny. And you?
At seven o'clock. I have breakfast at quarter past and leave home at eight.
Great, thanks. I'll write it all down.

l1_0.t: Hi Zoe. Did you come on your bike today? It's a lovely morning.
I wanted to, but it's got a flat tyre.
So did your mum drive you?
She couldn't. She had to leave early for work. So I took the bus. It was really crowded!

l1_1.t: Shall we meet at the station entrance at ten?
It's always so busy there. What about the ticket office?
We've already got our tickets, so we don't need to go there. Let's meet in the café next to platform one. We can have a hot drink before the train leaves.
Good idea. See you there.

l1_2.t: What does your uncle do, Sam? Is he still a taxi driver?
No, he stopped two years ago. Now he works at the airport.
Is he a pilot? That's so cool!
No, he repairs the engines of the planes. He's a mechanic. But he'd love to fly one day.

l1_3.t: How long is the coach journey to the mountains, Ms Lee?
Usually about two hours, but they're repairing the motorway, so it'll be longer this time.
Four hours?
No, not that bad! About three hours. We'll stop for lunch on the way.

l1_4.t: Excuse me, how do I get to the museum? Do I turn left at the traffic lights?
No, that road goes to the bus station. Go to the roundabout and turn right there.
Not straight on?
No, straight on takes you to the bridge. Turn right, and the museum's on your left.

l2.t: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to River Tours. My name's Paul and I'm your tour guide today. Our boat leaves in twenty minutes, at a quarter past ten, so please don't go too far. The tour usually starts at ten, but there's a small problem with the engine this morning, and the mechanic is just finishing. Our boat is called the Kestrel. That's K-E-S-T-R-E-L. It's the blue and white boat next to the bridge. We'll travel along the river for about an hour, and then we'll stop at the old market, where you can buy fruit and presents. After that, we'll sail to the castle. We'll have lunch at a restaurant next to the castle, and you'll have time to explore before we come back. Now, tickets. Adults pay twelve pounds for a return ticket, and students pay six pounds. If you only want a single ticket, it's four pounds. Please keep your ticket with you all day. And remember – don't stand near the sides of the boat while it's moving!

l3.t: Hi Mai! How was your trip to Scotland?
Great when we got there – but the journey was terrible! First, our train to the airport was cancelled, so Dad had to drive us there.
Oh no. Did you get there in time?
Yes, but then our flight was delayed for three hours.
Three hours! What did you do?
My brother played games on his phone, and Mum slept. I wanted to read my book, but I left it in the car! So I just watched the planes taking off and landing. It was actually quite interesting.
And when you arrived?
Our luggage didn't arrive with us! Mum's suitcase came the next day, but mine didn't come until two days after we arrived. I had to wear my cousin's clothes.
Ha! Did you have a good time with your cousins?
Brilliant. They live near a lake, and we went sailing every day in my uncle's small boat. I was scared at first, but by the end of the week I could sail it on my own.
Cool. Did you fly home too?
No, we came back by train this time. Dad said, 'No more planes!' We thought about taking the coach because it's cheaper, but the train was more comfortable. It took nine hours, but I didn't mind.

l4_0.t: How was the new school bus, Danny?
It's much bigger than the old one, and the seats are really comfortable.
That's nice.
But it's so slow! It stops at every bus stop in town. The journey took fifty minutes this morning!

l4_1.t: Hi Oscar, it's Nina. I'm on the train now, and it's on time, so I'll be at Central Station at four, like we planned. But please don't wait for me on the platform – it's very crowded on Saturdays. Let's meet outside the tourist information centre instead. It's just opposite the station. See you soon!

l4_2.t: People always think the best thing about being a pilot is travelling to other countries. But usually I only stay one night, so I just see the hotel and the airport! And I don't talk to the passengers much. For me, it's what I see from the window. Flying over the mountains when the sun comes up – it's amazing every time.

l4_3.t: Are you ready for the bike ride tomorrow, Hoa?
I'm not sure. It's forty kilometres, and I've never cycled that far before.
Don't worry, we'll stop lots of times.
I know, but there are some big hills, and I'm afraid I'll be too slow and everyone will have to wait for me.

l4_4.t: Attention, please. Because of a problem on the railway line, the eleven fifteen train to Bristol will not run today. Passengers for Bristol should leave the station by the main entrance, where coaches are waiting to take you there. You don't need a new ticket. We are very sorry for the delay to your journey.

l5.t: Kate, our project is about transport. How does everyone in your family travel every day? Let's start with your mum.
Mum works at the hospital in the city centre. She used to drive there, but parking was a problem. So now she goes on the tram. There's a stop just outside our house.
And your dad?
Dad's a mechanic at a garage near the motorway. It's too far to go by bike, so he rides his motorbike. He loves it!
What about your brother, Josh?
He's at university in another town. He catches the train every morning at quarter past seven. He'd like a car, but he hasn't got his driving licence yet.
And your grandma? Does she still work?
Not any more, but she goes to the swimming pool every morning. She takes the bus. She says taxis are too expensive.
And you?
I cycle to school. It only takes ten minutes. When it rains, Dad says I should walk, but I still take my bike!
Great, thanks, Kate. That's everyone in your family. Now let's ask my family the same questions.

l1_0.t: Have you got everything for the trip, Leo? What about your passport?
Yes, it's in my bag with my ticket.
And your sunglasses?
I'm wearing them! Oh no – my phone charger. It's still next to my bed at home.
Don't worry, you can borrow mine.

l1_1.t: Shall we get a taxi to the airport tomorrow?
It's too expensive. What about the bus? It stops right outside our house.
But it takes almost two hours. The train only takes forty minutes.
OK, let's do that. The station isn't far, and we can walk there with our suitcases.

l1_2.t: What time's our flight, Dad? Nine fifteen?
No, that's when we have to be at the airport. The flight leaves at ten fifty.
And when do we arrive in Paris?
At about one o'clock, if there aren't any delays.

l1_3.t: Your son loves planes, doesn't he? Does he want to be a pilot?
He did when he was little. Now he's more interested in how planes work.
So an engineer?
Yes, he wants to design plane engines. His best friend wants to be a train driver, but that's not for him.

l1_4.t: Your Uncle Mark drives a coach, doesn't he? He took us on the school trip.
No, that was my other uncle, Uncle Tony. Uncle Mark drives a lorry.
Oh! Does he go far?
Yes, all over Europe. He was a taxi driver when he was young, but he loves long journeys more.

l2.t: OK, everyone, listen carefully. Our visit to City Airport is next week. It was on Monday, but the airport asked us to change it, so we're going on Tuesday instead. The coach will leave from the school gate at half past eight, so please be there by quarter past. The journey takes about an hour if the traffic isn't bad. When we arrive, we'll watch the planes taking off from the top floor of the airport. After that, we'll go inside a real plane, and you can sit in the seats and look at the engines. A pilot is going to talk to us about his job, so think of some good questions. Last year, students met one of the engineers, but this year he isn't free. For lunch, there's a café at the airport. A sandwich and a drink cost five pounds. Or you can bring your own lunch if you prefer. Our guide at the airport is Mrs Brennan. That's B-R-E-N-N-A-N. And remember – you don't need your passport, because we aren't flying anywhere!

l3.t: Hello. I'm here with my family for three days. What's the best way to get around the city?
The trams are the quickest. You can buy a travel card for one day for eight pounds, or for three days for eighteen pounds.
Three days, please. We arrived this morning and we're leaving on Sunday. Can we use the card on the buses too?
Yes, on the buses and the trams, but not on the underground. That's a different ticket.
OK. We'd like to visit the castle tomorrow. How do we get there?
Take tram number four from the stop outside. It's about fifteen minutes. You could walk, but it's a long way, and it's all uphill. There's no bus that goes there.
The tram, then. And is there a boat tour on the river?
Yes, there's one every hour from the bridge. It usually costs ten pounds, but today it's free for children because it's a national holiday.
Brilliant! My little brother loves boats. Is there anything else we should see?
The railway museum is very popular. It's open every day except Monday. There are lots of old trains, and you can even drive a model train.
My dad will love that! Can I take a map, please?
Here you are. It's free, and it shows all the tram stops.

l4_0.t: How was your flight to Spain, Amy? It was your first one, wasn't it?
Yes! I thought I'd be scared, but I wasn't at all.
Long flights can be boring, though.
It was only two hours, and I looked out of the window the whole time. When we went up through the clouds, I couldn't stop smiling!

l4_1.t: And now the traffic news. There are long delays on the motorway this morning, near the airport. A lorry has stopped on the road with an engine problem, and a mechanic is on the way. There's no accident, and no one is hurt, but drivers should leave home early. And the road repairs on Bridge Street have finished, so that road is open again.

l4_2.t: My grandma is seventy-two, but she's always travelling. Last year she went to Peru, and this spring she's going to Japan. She's been to about forty countries now! She doesn't enjoy long flights, but she says it's worth it. She stopped working ten years ago, so now she has lots of time to explore.

l4_3.t: Mum, why are we stopping here? We've got lots of petrol.
I know. But the car felt strange on the motorway, so I want to look at the tyres.
Can I get some crisps from the shop while you do that?
No, we'll have lunch soon. Wait in the car, please.

l4_4.t: Hi Mum, it's me. I'm at the station. I'm really sorry, but I missed the four o'clock train. The bus from school was slow because of the traffic, and when I got to the platform, the train was just leaving. Don't worry, I've still got my ticket, and I can use it on the next train. It arrives at quarter past five. Can you meet me then?

l5.t: Hi Hugo! How was your holiday in Italy?
Good, but my family forgot so many things! Dad forgot his passport. We were already on the motorway, and we had to drive back home to get it.
Oh no! Did you miss the flight?
No, luckily. And Dad had all our tickets on his phone, so that was OK.
And your mum? She's usually so organised.
She packed everything, but she left her sunglasses on the kitchen table. It was really sunny, so she had to buy some at the airport.
What about your sister?
Lily forgot her camera. She was upset, because she wanted to take photos of the beach. She used Mum's phone instead.
Your grandpa came too, didn't he?
Yes. He remembered to bring a map of the city, but he forgot his umbrella. And of course it rained on the second day!
And you? Did you remember everything?
I thought so. But when we opened the suitcases at the hotel, I didn't have my swimming shorts! I had to borrow some from Grandpa. They were enormous!

l1_0.t: Dad, are we still going to the beach on Saturday?
I think so. The forecast says it won't rain this weekend.
Great! Will it be sunny?
Not really. It'll be quite cloudy on Saturday, and very windy too. Sunday will be sunny, but you've got your swimming lesson on Sunday.
Then Saturday's fine. I'll take my kite!

l1_1.t: Hana, you're really wet! Where's your umbrella?
I left it on the bus this morning. I only noticed when it started raining.
Oh no. Have you got your gloves and your scarf? It's getting cold.
Yes, they're both in my bag. But I'll need to buy a new umbrella.

l1_2.t: It's so hot today! Shall we go to the outdoor swimming pool?
I went there yesterday and it was full of people. What about a walk in the park?
There aren't many trees there, and it's thirty-two degrees!
OK, then let's go to the museum. It's cool inside, and there's a new exhibition about volcanoes.
Good idea.

l1_3.t: Hi Tom, are you on the train yet?
No, Mum. Because of the snow, my train is late. It was at half past two, but now it leaves at three o'clock.
So when will you get here?
At about half past four, I think. Can you meet me at the station?
Of course. Keep warm!

l1_4.t: Where are you going, Leo?
To Grandma's farm. I said I'd help her with the animals.
It rained all night, so the fields will be really wet and muddy. Put your boots on, not your trainers.
OK. But it's warm now, so I don't need my coat.
That's fine. And you don't need your cap either – there's no sun today.

l2.t: Good morning, everyone. As you know, Year 8 are going to visit the National Weather Centre next month. We planned to go on Monday the twelfth, but the centre is closed that day, so now we're going on Tuesday the thirteenth. The coach will leave from the school car park at quarter past eight. Please don't be late – last time we waited twenty minutes for some of you! The journey takes about an hour. When we arrive, a guide will show us the computers that they use to make weather forecasts. After that, we'll watch a short film. Last year's group saw a film about snow and ice, but this year it's about storms – how they start and why they're so dangerous. In the afternoon, we'll go outside to measure the wind and the rain, so please bring an umbrella. You won't need sun cream – it's not summer! Lunch is included in the price, so you don't need to bring any food. Finally, we'll meet one of the weather presenters from TV, Kate Barton. That's B-A-R-T-O-N. She's going to answer your questions, so think about what you'd like to ask her.

l3.t: Hi Lily. How was your camping trip with the Scouts?
Well, it was very different from our plan! We wanted to stay three nights by the lake, but we came home after only one.
Why? Was it too cold?
No, it was quite warm, actually. But on the first night there was a huge thunderstorm. The wind was so strong that it broke two of our tents.
Oh no! Where did you sleep?
Our leader, Mrs Price, phoned a farmer near the campsite. He let us sleep in his barn with the cows! It was a bit smelly, but it was dry.
Ha! Were you frightened during the storm?
My friend Zoe was really scared, but I wasn't. I thought the lightning over the lake was amazing. I was just unhappy because my new sleeping bag got wet.
So what did you do the next day?
It was still raining in the morning, so we couldn't go walking or swimming. The farmer showed us how to make bread in his kitchen instead. That was great fun.
Would you go camping again?
Definitely! But next time I'll check the weather forecast first. What about you? Did you have a good weekend?
Not bad. It was too wet to play tennis, so I stayed at home and watched films.

l4_0.t: Good morning. It's a foggy start today, so drivers should be careful, but the fog will go by ten o'clock. Tomorrow morning will be cloudy and quite cold, and in the afternoon there'll be heavy rain and strong winds across the whole country. If you want some sunshine, you'll have to wait for the weekend, when it will be warm and sunny again.

l4_1.t: How was your holiday in Scotland?
Beautiful! Everyone told me it rains all the time there, so I packed my raincoat and boots. But we had sunshine every single day – I even got sunburnt! I couldn't believe it.
Lucky you! It rained here all week.

l4_2.t: Hi Dan, it's Ravi. The tennis courts are closed today because they're covered in ice, so we can't play this afternoon. Sorry! Let's try again next week when it's warmer. Oh, and you can keep my racket until then – I've got another one.

l4_3.t: Listen, everyone. It's going to be very hot today – more than thirty degrees. At break time you can still play outside, but please stay under the trees and don't run around too much. And make sure you wear a sun hat. I've got some spare ones here if you forgot yours. I can see you've all brought water bottles, so that's good.

l4_4.t: Mum, it's been snowing all night! Look outside!
I know. Do you want to go to the ski centre with Dad? Or sledging in the park?
Not today. It's too windy on the hills. I just want to stay in the garden and make a snowman with Tim.
OK, but come in when you get cold.

l5.t: So, Rosie, have all your friends come back from their holidays now?
Yes, and I've had messages from all of them. Kim went to Spain. She thought it would be really hot, but she says it was quite cool, and so windy that she couldn't put her umbrella up on the beach!
Oh dear. And Oscar? Didn't he go to Norway?
Yes, to the mountains. He expected it to be cold and cloudy. It wasn't very cold, actually, but guess what – one day it snowed! In July!
Amazing. What about Hannah? She went to London, didn't she?
That's right. She wanted to take photos of the city from the London Eye, but it was foggy all morning and she couldn't see anything. It was quite warm, though.
What a shame. And Duc went to Vietnam to see his grandparents?
Yes. He thought it would be hot, but it was actually quite cool, because it rained every day. He says it was wetter than here!
And Leila?
She went to Egypt. There were no clouds at all – it was forty degrees every day! She had to stay inside the hotel at lunchtime.
Well, we had that terrible storm on our holiday, didn't we?
Don't remind me, Dad! Our tent nearly flew away.

l1_0.t: How was your birthday party in the garden, Nadia?
Well, the forecast said it would be sunny, so we planned to eat outside.
And did it rain?
No, luckily it stayed dry. And there wasn't any sun – it was cloudy and so windy! The paper plates flew all over the garden.

l1_1.t: Has everyone got their life jackets? Oh, wait. Sorry, everyone. There's a thunderstorm coming, so there's no sailing on the lake today.
Oh no! Can we go horse riding instead?
Yes, riding is still happening at two o'clock. And climbing is on the indoor wall, so that's happening too.
Great. I'll do climbing, then.

l1_2.t: Have you got everything for the beach, Sam? It's going to be really sunny today.
Yes, Mum. I've got my sunglasses on already, and my cap's in the car.
Did you pack the sun cream?
Oh no, I didn't! I'll get it from the bathroom.

l1_3.t: It's cold this morning! The radio said it's only five degrees.
That was at seven o'clock. It's warmer now – the thermometer in the garden says fifteen.
Will it get warmer this afternoon?
Not much. The forecast says it'll be twenty-five tomorrow, but not today.

l1_4.t: Mum, can I cycle to school today? It's sunny.
The roads are still icy after last night. It isn't safe on a bike.
Can you drive me, then?
Sorry, I've got to be at work early. Take the bus – it stops right outside the school.

l2.t: And now, what's on this weekend. If you enjoy windy weather, don't miss the Kite Festival at Polwick Beach. That's P-O-L-W-I-C-K. It's just ten minutes from the town centre by bus. The festival opens on Saturday at half past ten. Last year it started at nine, but people said that was too early! There'll be kites of every colour and size – some are as big as a bus. Last year adult tickets were six pounds, but this year they only cost four pounds, and children under twelve can go for free. Now, the weather. The forecast for Saturday is good – sunny with strong winds, which is perfect for kites. But if there's a thunderstorm, it isn't safe to fly kites, so the festival will move to Sunday. Please don't bring an umbrella – the wind is too strong for umbrellas on the beach! It can get quite cold by the sea, even when it's sunny, so remember to bring a jacket. You can buy food and drink at the festival café. For more information, visit the festival website.

l3.t: Hi Alex. Have you started the science project yet?
Yes, I have. Mr Grant said we could choose any topic about the weather, so I'm doing mine on fog.
Fog? Why?

Well, I wanted to do snow first, but three other people chose it. Then my dad told me about a day when he was flying home and his plane couldn't land because of fog. He had to wait at another airport for six hours! So I got interested.
Cool. What are you going to do for it?
I'm going to make a big poster. I thought about making a video, but my camera's broken. What's your topic?
Rain. I'm measuring how much rain falls in our garden every day for a month. I made the thing to measure it from an old plastic bottle.
Has it rained much?
Not at all! It's been sunny for ten days. My little brother keeps asking when it's going to rain, because he wants to play in the puddles.
Ha! When do we have to give the projects to Mr Grant?
On the fifteenth. That's Friday next week. Oh – no, sorry, he changed it. It's Monday the eighteenth now.
Good, I need more time. Are you going to the library after school? I need some books about fog.
I can't today – I've got swimming. But I can go tomorrow.
OK, let's go tomorrow, then.

l4_0.t: We went to the beach on Sunday. The morning was cloudy and a bit cold, so at first I was disappointed. But at lunchtime the sun came out and it got really warm. We swam, played volleyball and ate ice cream. By the evening I was so happy that I didn't want to go home!

l4_1.t: Dad, it's raining really hard and I'm meeting Lucy at her house at four.
Take my big umbrella – it's by the door.
It's too windy for an umbrella. It'll break! Could you take me there in the car? It's only five minutes.
OK, go and get your coat.

l4_2.t: Good evening. Tonight it'll be very cold, and by tomorrow morning there will be thick fog in many places, especially near rivers. If you're driving to work or school, please go slowly and turn your lights on. The fog should go by lunchtime, and the afternoon will be dry and sunny. There's no snow yet – but it might come next week.

l4_3.t: How was the match on Saturday?

Well, it was raining when we started, but that was OK – we often play in the rain. Then in the second half we heard thunder and saw lightning over the hills, so the referee stopped the game. We were winning two-nil!
That's bad luck.

l4_4.t: Most of my friends love summer, but autumn is my favourite season. It's still quite warm in September, and I don't mind the cold, foggy days in November either. But the best thing is walking through the park when all the leaves are red, orange and yellow. It's so beautiful. I always take lots of photos.

l5.t: Hi Leo! How was the activity camp?
Great, Grandma! But the weather changed every day, so we didn't always do what we planned.
What happened on Monday?
It was really sunny and hot, so we went swimming in the lake all afternoon. We were going to play football, but it was too hot to run around.
Very sensible. And Tuesday?
On Tuesday it was so foggy that we couldn't see the other side of the lake. So no canoeing! We did climbing on the indoor wall instead.
And Wednesday?
Wednesday was cloudy but dry, and there was no wind at all, so we finally went canoeing. I fell in the water twice!
Oh, Leo! What about Thursday?
There was a big thunderstorm in the morning and it rained all day. Some people did drawing, but I chose the cooking class. We made pizza!
Lovely. And on the last day?
The sun came back, but it was windy and quite cold. We went for a long walk in the hills. I wanted to go fishing, but there wasn't time.
It sounds wonderful.

l1_0.t: Is that your uncle in the photo? Is he a pilot? He's wearing a uniform.
No, that was for a fancy dress party. He's a dentist. He works at the hospital in town.
Really? I thought he was a teacher at your school.
That's my aunt, his wife. She teaches maths.

l1_1.t: Does your sister still work in that big office in the city centre?
No, she left in March. She works at a hotel by the sea now.
As a receptionist?
Yes. And before the office, she worked in a car factory, but she hated it.

l1_2.t: Dad, can you drive me to school tomorrow?
Sorry, love. Usually I start work at half past nine, but tomorrow there's an early meeting at nine.
How long is it?
An hour. It finishes at ten, and then I've got to meet some customers.

l1_3.t: Mum starts her new job as a manager on Monday. I want to buy her something.
What about a new bag for work?
Dad's already bought her one.
A diary, then, for all her meetings?
She uses her phone for that. I'll get her a mug for her desk – she drinks so much coffee!

l1_4.t: What do you want to be when you leave school, Tara?
Everyone thinks I'll be a singer because I'm in the school choir. But that's just a hobby.
You're great in the school plays. What about an actor?
I'm too shy for that, really. I want to be a photographer. I love taking pictures of people.

l2.t: Hello, everyone. My name's Julia, and I work at Greenfield Zoo. We need some young people to work for us this summer. You must be sixteen or older – sorry, we can't take fifteen-year-olds. The jobs are in our café and our gift shop, and we also need some guides to help visitors find their way around. The working day starts at half past eight, before the zoo opens at ten, and finishes at four. You'll work five days a week, and that includes weekends. Last year we paid six pounds fifty an hour, but this year you'll earn seven pounds an hour, and you'll get a free lunch every day in the staff café. We'll give you a uniform – a green T-shirt and a cap. You'll need to bring your own black trousers and comfortable shoes. If you're interested, please send an email to our manager, Mrs Fenwick. That's F-E-N-W-I-C-K. Tell her about yourself and why you'd like to work with us. The last day to send it is the thirtieth of April. Thank you!

l3.t: Grandpa, for my homework I have to ask someone about their first job. What was yours?
Well, I left school at sixteen and got a job in a shoe factory. My father wanted me to work on our farm, but I wanted to earn my own money.
What did you do there?
At first I cleaned the machines. It was a dirty job! After a year, they made me a driver. I took the shoes to shops all over the country.
Did you like that?
I loved it. I saw lots of different towns that I didn't know. The hours were long, though. Sometimes I didn't get home until ten at night.
How much did you earn?
Eight pounds a week! That sounds like nothing now, but it was quite a lot then. I gave half to my mother and saved the rest.
What did you buy with your money?
My friends all bought motorbikes, but I wanted a guitar. I played in a band in the evenings.
Really? So why did you leave the factory?
When I was twenty-two, the factory closed down. I didn't know what to do. Then a friend told me the police were looking for new officers. I was a police officer for thirty years after that.
Wow! Can I interview you for my project, then?
Of course you can.

l4_0.t: My mum has just started a new job at the hospital. She's a nurse on the children's ward. She works at night sometimes, so I don't see her much, but I don't mind. She helps so many sick kids, and they all love her. I tell everyone at school about her!

l4_1.t: Hi. I bought this jacket last week, but it's too small.
I'm sorry. We haven't got a bigger one in the shop at the moment, but I can order a large one for you. It'll be here on Thursday.
Can't I just have my money back?
Only with a receipt, I'm afraid. Have you got one?
No. OK, please order it.

l4_2.t: Hi Sam, it's Oliver. Guess what! The café near the station needs someone to wash dishes on Saturday mornings. My cousin works there, and she says the manager wants a student. You said you wanted to earn some money, so call them soon! See you at football practice.

l4_3.t: I've been a tour guide for ten years. I take groups around Italy and France. People think the travelling is the best part, but I'm tired of hotels and buses! And yes, I speak four languages, which is useful. But really, it's the people. Every week I meet new guests from all over the world, and some of them become good friends.

l4_4.t: Which talk did you go to on Careers Day?
The one by the engineer. I only went because my friend wanted to, and I thought it would be boring.
And was it?
Not at all! She showed us how she builds bridges, and then we made a small one from paper. I loved it. Maybe I'll be an engineer!

l5.t: Ethan, did you meet any interesting people at Careers Day yesterday? I was ill, so I missed it.
Yes, lots! First there was Mr Carter. Everyone thought he was a footballer, because he was wearing a sports shirt. But he repairs cars – he's got his own garage.
So he's a mechanic. What about Mrs Okafor?
She's a chemist. She works in a pharmacy in the town centre, and she told us how to choose the right medicine.
Interesting. And Ms Lee? Is she the one who paints?
No, that's her sister – she's an artist. Ms Lee writes for the local newspaper. She interviewed me for a story about the day!
Cool! Who was next?
Mr Novak. He played the violin for us. He plays in an orchestra and travels all over the world.
So he's a musician. Was he good?
Brilliant! He said he practises for four hours every day, even on holiday.
Wow. And the last one?
Mrs Garcia. She used to be a travel agent, but now she designs bridges and roads. She was my favourite.
I'm sorry I missed it!

l1_0.t: Your mum works at the hospital, doesn't she, Carlos? Is she a doctor?
No, she's a nurse. My aunt's a doctor at the same hospital.
Oh! I saw your mum in a uniform at the station last week.
Ah, that was my other aunt. She's a police officer.

l1_1.t: Mum, are we going to meet Dad at his office?
No, he finishes late today, so it's easier to meet in town. Let's wait for him at the café opposite the station.
Why not inside the station?
It's too busy and cold in there. The café's much warmer.

l1_2.t: You babysit for your neighbours, don't you? How much do they pay you?
Eight pounds an hour. My friend gets ten, but she looks after three children!
That's not bad. I only get five pounds for washing my dad's car.
Five pounds an hour?
No, for the whole car!

l1_3.t: How was your school trip to the TV studio?
Brilliant! We hoped to see a famous singer, but she wasn't there that day.
Did you see any actors?
We saw where they film a drama, but there weren't any actors. But we met a journalist who reads the news. She was really friendly and talked to us for ages.

l1_4.t: When do you start your new job at the bank, Paul?
On Monday. They give us a uniform, so I don't need any shirts.
What about shoes?
I've got some good black ones. But I need a bag for my laptop – my old one's broken.

l2.t: Do you love writing? Are you between eleven and fifteen? Then why not enter our Young Reporter competition? This year, we'd like you to write a news story about a person in your town who has an unusual job. Last year the topic was sport, and we got hundreds of stories about footballers! This time, think about someone different – maybe a man who repairs old clocks, or a woman who works with snakes at the zoo. You'll need to talk to them and ask lots of questions, just like a real journalist. Your story must be no longer than three hundred words. Two hundred is fine too, but please don't send more than three hundred. The last day to send your story is the twenty-eighth of February – we can't accept anything after that. The winner will spend a day working with one of our photographers at the newspaper, taking pictures of real news stories. The winning story will also appear in the newspaper. Please email your story to our editor, Simon Dawlish. That's D-A-W-L-I-S-H. Good luck!

l3.t: Hi Tom! How was your work experience week at the Grand Hotel?
It was brilliant, Ruby. I wanted to work in the kitchen, but they didn't need anyone there, so I helped the receptionist instead.
What did you do?
I answered the phone and helped guests when they arrived. I also wrote emails to people who wanted to book rooms. The manager checked them before I sent them.
Was it difficult?

Not really. The worst thing was the uniform! I had to wear a black suit and tie every day, and it was so hot. But the guests were really nice. One old man from Canada gave me a book about his country.
That's kind. Did you have to work long hours?
I started at eight and finished at four. That's the same as school, really – but with no lessons! The receptionists usually work until eleven at night, though.
Would you like to work in a hotel when you're older?
Maybe. The manager said I'd be good at it, because I'm friendly and I can speak French. But I'd prefer to be a pilot. Then I can stay in hotels all over the world!
Ha! I'm doing my work experience next month at a hairdresser's.
Really? I thought you wanted to go to the zoo.
I did, but all the places there were taken.

l4_0.t: My dad's a painter – not pictures, houses! He paints people's walls and doors. He says it's an easy job, but it isn't. He climbs ladders all day and carries heavy things, and when he gets home, he falls asleep on the sofa before dinner! He doesn't earn much money, but he likes being his own boss.

l4_1.t: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the castle. My name's Helen, and I'll be with you for the next hour. We'll start in the Great Hall, where the king and queen ate their dinner, and finish in the gift shop. Please stay together, and don't touch the paintings. Any questions before we start? No? Follow me, then.

l4_2.t: I've got an interview tomorrow for the Saturday job at the pet shop.
That's great! Are you looking forward to it?
Not really. I can't stop thinking about it. What if they ask me something I don't know? My hands are shaking just talking about it!
Don't worry. You'll be fine.

l4_3.t: Hello, Mrs Taylor. This is Dave from Northside Garage. I'm calling about your car. We've finished the work, and it's ready to collect. It cost a bit less than we said – just ninety pounds. We're open until six today, or you can come tomorrow morning if that's easier. Thanks. Bye.

l4_4.t: Next Thursday an explorer called Anna Rivera is coming to talk to us. She has travelled to the North Pole! She'll show us photos and a short film. You don't need to prepare any questions – she'll answer anything you like at the end. But please look at her website before Thursday and read about her journeys. Then you'll understand her talk better.

l5.t: Daniel, for our English homework we have to write about our families' jobs. Can I ask you about yours?
Sure. My mum used to work in an office, but now she works at the hospital. She isn't a doctor or a nurse, though – she's a receptionist there.
And your dad? Didn't he work in a bank?
He did, but he left last year. Now he's a manager at a big car factory outside town. He loves it.
What about your sister? She's still a student, isn't she?
She finished university in June. She wanted to be a teacher, but she changed her mind. Now she's a chemist, so she works in a pharmacy.
And your uncle – the one who drives a taxi?
No, that's my other uncle. Uncle Tony is a waiter. He works in a hotel restaurant by the sea.
And your grandmother? Has she stopped working?
No! She's seventy, but she still works three days a week in a clothes shop. She loves talking to the customers.
What a busy family!
